+/-! ## Direct polynomial collision estimate -/
+
+/-- Two distinct direct polynomial representatives agree at a uniformly
+sampled direct point with probability at most `m d / q`.
+
+This is the Schwartz--Zippel estimate `polynomialAgreement_avg_le_mdq` of the
+low individual degree test, read through the polynomial and point
+identifications of the direct low-degree game; it is the collision
+hypothesis of `lem:ld-sandwich` (blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:454-480`,
+paper `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:465-501`). -/
+theorem directPolynomialAgreement_avg_le_mdq (D : DirectLdParams)
+    (g g' : PolyIndex D.m (DirectScalarQ D) D.d) (hneq : g ≠ g') :
+    avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))
+        (fun u => if MvPolynomial.eval u g.1 = MvPolynomial.eval u g'.1 then
+          (1 : Error) else 0) ≤
+      (D.m * D.d : Error) / D.q := by
+  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+  let gLdt := directPolyEquivPolynomial D g
+  let g'Ldt := directPolyEquivPolynomial D g'
+  have hneqLdt : gLdt ≠ g'Ldt := by
+    intro heq
+    exact hneq ((directPolyEquivPolynomial D).injective heq)
+  calc
+    avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))
+        (fun u => if MvPolynomial.eval u g.1 = MvPolynomial.eval u g'.1 then
+          (1 : Error) else 0) =
+      avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))
+        (fun u => if gLdt (directPointEquiv D u) =
+          g'Ldt (directPointEquiv D u) then (1 : Error) else 0) := by
+            apply avgOver_congr
+            intro u
+            simp only [gLdt, g'Ldt, directPolyEquivPolynomial_apply]
+            exact if_congr
+              ((directScalarEquiv D).injective.eq_iff.symm) rfl rfl
+    _ = avgOver (uniformDistribution (Point D.toLDTParameters))
+        (fun u : Point D.toLDTParameters =>
+          if gLdt u = g'Ldt u then (1 : Error) else 0) := by
+      simpa using
+        (avgOver_uniform_equiv (directPointEquiv D)
+          (fun u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D =>
+            if gLdt (directPointEquiv D u) =
+              g'Ldt (directPointEquiv D u) then (1 : Error) else 0))
+    _ ≤ (D.m * D.d : Error) / D.q :=
+      polynomialAgreement_avg_le_mdq D.toLDTParameters gLdt g'Ldt hneqLdt
+
+/-! ## Palindromic tuple measurements -/
+
+/-- Combine coordinate polynomial projective measurements into a tuple-valued
+POVM by the ordered palindromic product of `lem:ld-sandwich` (blueprint
+`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:454-507`, paper
+`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:465-501`).
+
+No commutativity between different coordinate measurements is assumed. -/
+noncomputable def directSandwichPolynomialMeasurement
+    (D : DirectLdParams) {iota : Type*} [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
+    (G : Fin D.k → PolyMeas D.m (DirectScalarQ D) D.d iota)
+    (hG : ∀ r, Measurement.IsProjective (G r)) :
+    DirectPolyMeasTuple D iota := by
+  let hmeasurement := SandwichProduct.sandwichProduct_isMeasurement
+    (G := fun r (_ : Unit) => G r) (hG := fun r (_ : Unit) => hG r) ()
+  exact Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne
+    (fun g => sandwichProduct (fun r (_ : Unit) h => (G r).effect h) () g)
+    hmeasurement.1 hmeasurement.2
+
+/-- The effects of the tuple POVM are its defining palindromic products. -/
+@[simp] theorem directSandwichPolynomialMeasurement_effect
+    (D : DirectLdParams) {iota : Type*} [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
+    (G : Fin D.k → PolyMeas D.m (DirectScalarQ D) D.d iota)
+    (hG : ∀ r, Measurement.IsProjective (G r))
+    (g : DirectPolyTuple D) :
+    (directSandwichPolynomialMeasurement D G hG).effect g =
+      sandwichProduct (fun r (_ : Unit) h => (G r).effect h) () g :=
+  rfl
+
+/-- Relabeling a polynomial projective measurement of the low individual
+degree test by direct polynomial representatives preserves projectivity. -/
+theorem directPolynomialMeasurement_isProjective
+    (D : DirectLdParams) :
+    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+    ∀ {iota : Type*} [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
+      (G : ProjMeas (Polynomial D.toLDTParameters) iota),
+      Measurement.IsProjective (directPolynomialMeasurement D G) := by
+  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+  intro iota _ _ G g
+  rw [directPolynomialMeasurement_effect]
+  refine { isIdempotentElem := ?_, isSelfAdjoint := ?_ }
+  · exact G.proj (directPolyEquivPolynomial D g)
+  · exact (Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mp
+      (G.outcome_pos (directPolyEquivPolynomial D g))).1.isSelfAdjoint
+
+/-! ## Coordinatewise low individual degree soundness -/
+
+/-- Quantum soundness of the low individual degree test (`thm:main-formal`,
+paper `references/ldt-paper/test_definition.tex:180-202`) applied to one
+coordinate of a projective strategy for the direct low-degree game.
+
+The coordinate strategy passes the test with failure probability at most
+`3 ε`, and the theorem is instantiated at the auxiliary sampling parameter
+`directLdAuxParameter D`; both numerical side conditions of the theorem follow
+from the positivity of the dimension and of the degree.  Blueprint
+`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:170-215`, paper
+`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:413-458`. -/
+theorem directCoordinateMainFormal
+    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
+    (hS : S.IsProjective) (r : Fin D.k) (ε : Error)
+    (hwin : 1 - ε ≤ S.value) :
+    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+    ∃ GA : ProjMeas (Polynomial D.toLDTParameters) S.ιA,
+      ∃ GB : ProjMeas (Polynomial D.toLDTParameters) S.ιB,
+        ConsRel (directCoordinateProjStrat D S hS r).state
+            (uniformDistribution (Point D.toLDTParameters))
+            (IdxProjMeas.toIdxSubMeas
+              (directCoordinateProjStrat D S hS r).pointMeasurementA)
+            (polynomialEvaluationFamily D.toLDTParameters GB.toSubMeas)
+            (Test.mainFormalError D.toLDTParameters
+              (directLdAuxParameter D) (3 * ε)) ∧
+          ConsRel (directCoordinateProjStrat D S hS r).state
+            (uniformDistribution (Point D.toLDTParameters))
+            (polynomialEvaluationFamily D.toLDTParameters GA.toSubMeas)
+            (IdxProjMeas.toIdxSubMeas
+              (directCoordinateProjStrat D S hS r).pointMeasurementB)
+            (Test.mainFormalError D.toLDTParameters
+              (directLdAuxParameter D) (3 * ε)) ∧
+          ConsRel (directCoordinateProjStrat D S hS r).state
+            (uniformDistribution Unit)
+            (constSubMeasFamily GA.toSubMeas)
+            (constSubMeasFamily GB.toSubMeas)
+            (Test.mainFormalError D.toLDTParameters
+              (directLdAuxParameter D) (3 * ε)) := by
+  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+  exact Test.mainFormal D.toLDTParameters
+    (directCoordinateProjStrat D S hS r) (3 * ε)
+    (directCoordinate_passes D S hS r ε hwin).soundnessHypothesis
+    (directLdAuxParameter D) (four_hundred_mul_le_directLdAuxParameter D)
+    (directLdAuxParameter_pos D)
+
+/-! ## One-coordinate tuples -/
+
+/-- Relabeling an outcome by a constant tuple over a one-element index set is
+selected by the value of the tuple at the unique index. -/
+private theorem const_tuple_eq_iff {iota beta : Type*} [Unique iota]
+    (v : iota → beta) (b : beta) :
+    v = (fun _ => b) ↔ v default = b := by
+  constructor
+  · intro h
+    exact congrFun h default
+  · intro h
+    funext i
+    rw [Unique.eq_default i]
+    exact h
+
+/-- The effect of a tuple-relabeled measurement at a constant tuple over a
+one-element index set is the effect of the relabeling by the unique
+coordinate. -/
+private theorem postprocess_effect_const_tuple
+    {alpha beta iota d : Type*} [Fintype alpha] [DecidableEq alpha]
+    [Fintype beta] [DecidableEq beta] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
+    [Unique iota] [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
+    (M : Quantum.Measurement alpha d) (f : alpha → iota → beta) (b : beta) :
+    (M.postprocess f).effect (fun _ => b) =
+      (M.postprocess (fun a => f a default)).effect b := by
+  simp only [Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect]
+  exact Finset.sum_congr
+    (Finset.filter_congr fun a _ => const_tuple_eq_iff (f a) b)
+    (fun _ _ => rfl)
+
+/-- Reading a measurement as a one-coordinate tuple measurement does not
+change its effects. -/
+private theorem postprocess_const_tuple_effect_self
+    {alpha iota d : Type*} [Fintype alpha] [DecidableEq alpha]
+    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota] [Unique iota] [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
+    (M : Quantum.Measurement alpha d) (p : alpha) :
+    (M.postprocess (fun a (_ : iota) => a)).effect (fun _ => p) = M.effect p := by
+  rw [postprocess_effect_const_tuple]
+  simp only [Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect, Finset.filter_eq',
+    Finset.mem_univ, if_true, Finset.sum_singleton]
+
+/-- The identification of values with constant tuples over a one-element
+index set. -/
+private def constTupleEquiv (iota beta : Type*) [Unique iota] :
+    beta ≃ (iota → beta) where
+  toFun b := fun _ => b
+  invFun v := v default
+  left_inv _ := rfl
+  right_inv v := by
+    funext i
+    rw [Unique.eq_default i]
+
+/-- The polynomial-tuple conclusion of `lem:ld-soundness` for simultaneity
+parameter `1`: the coordinate conclusions of the low individual degree
+theorem, read as one-coordinate tuples.
+
+The three consistency defects carry the error of `thm:main-formal` at the
+auxiliary parameter `directLdAuxParameter D` and pass bound `3 ε`; its
+absorption into the error function `deltaLd` is
+`exists_directLdTransportConstants`.  For simultaneity parameter at least `2`
+the coordinate conclusions do not determine simultaneous polynomial
+measurements; see the module docstring and
+`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-simultaneous-sandwich.tex`.  Blueprint
+`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:170-215`, paper
+`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:413-458`. -/
+theorem exists_directSimultaneousPolynomialMeasurements_of_k_eq_one
+    (D : DirectLdParams) (hk : D.k = 1) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
+    (hS : S.IsProjective) (ε : Error) (hwin : 1 - ε ≤ S.value) :
+    ∃ GA : DirectPolyMeasTuple D S.ιA,
+      ∃ GB : DirectPolyMeasTuple D S.ιB,
+        consistencyDefect
+            (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))
+            (fun u outcome =>
+              heteroKron
+                (((S.A (directLdPointQuestionOf D u)).postprocess
+                  (directLdPointValuesOrZero D)).effect outcome) 1)
+            (fun u outcome =>
+              heteroKron 1
+                ((GB.postprocess (evalDirectPolyTupleAt u)).effect outcome))
+            S.ψ ≤
+          Test.mainFormalError D.toLDTParameters (directLdAuxParameter D) (3 * ε) ∧
+        consistencyDefect
+            (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))
+            (fun u outcome =>
+              heteroKron
+                ((GA.postprocess (evalDirectPolyTupleAt u)).effect outcome) 1)
+            (fun u outcome =>
+              heteroKron 1
+                (((S.B (directLdPointQuestionOf D u)).postprocess
+                  (directLdPointValuesOrZero D)).effect outcome))
+            S.ψ ≤
+          Test.mainFormalError D.toLDTParameters (directLdAuxParameter D) (3 * ε) ∧
+        consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Unit)
+            (fun _ g => heteroKron (GA.effect g) 1)
+            (fun _ g => heteroKron 1 (GB.effect g))
+            S.ψ ≤
+          Test.mainFormalError D.toLDTParameters (directLdAuxParameter D) (3 * ε) := by
+  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+  haveI hU : Unique (Fin D.k) :=
+    { default := ⟨0, by omega⟩
+      uniq := fun i => Fin.ext (by have := i.isLt; omega) }
+  obtain ⟨GA₀, GB₀, h1, h2, h3⟩ :=
+    directCoordinateMainFormal D S hS default ε hwin
+  refine ⟨(directPolynomialMeasurement D GA₀).postprocess (fun g _ => g),
+    (directPolynomialMeasurement D GB₀).postprocess (fun g _ => g), ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
+  · have h1' := directPointPolynomial_consistencyDefect_le D S hS default GB₀ _ h1
+    refine ((consistencyDefect_outcome_equiv _
+      (constTupleEquiv (Fin D.k) (DirectScalarQ D)) _ _ S.ψ).symm.trans
+      (consistencyDefect_congr _ _ _ _ _ S.ψ ?_ ?_)).trans_le h1'
+    · intro u a
+      change heteroKron (((S.A (directLdPointQuestionOf D u)).postprocess
+        (directLdPointValuesOrZero D)).effect (fun _ => a)) 1 = _
+      rw [postprocess_effect_const_tuple]
+      rfl
+    · intro u a
+      change heteroKron 1 ((((directPolynomialMeasurement D GB₀).postprocess
+        (fun g _ => g)).postprocess (evalDirectPolyTupleAt u)).effect
+          (fun _ => a)) = _
+      rw [MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_comp,
+        postprocess_effect_const_tuple]
+      rfl
+  · have h2' := directPolynomialPoint_consistencyDefect_le D S hS default GA₀ _ h2
+    refine ((consistencyDefect_outcome_equiv _
+      (constTupleEquiv (Fin D.k) (DirectScalarQ D)) _ _ S.ψ).symm.trans
+      (consistencyDefect_congr _ _ _ _ _ S.ψ ?_ ?_)).trans_le h2'
+    · intro u a
+      change heteroKron ((((directPolynomialMeasurement D GA₀).postprocess
+        (fun g _ => g)).postprocess (evalDirectPolyTupleAt u)).effect
+          (fun _ => a)) 1 = _
+      rw [MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_comp,
+        postprocess_effect_const_tuple]
+      rfl
+    · intro u a
+      change heteroKron 1 (((S.B (directLdPointQuestionOf D u)).postprocess
+        (directLdPointValuesOrZero D)).effect (fun _ => a)) = _
+      rw [postprocess_effect_const_tuple]
+      rfl
+  · have h3' := directPolynomialPolynomial_consistencyDefect_le D S GA₀ GB₀ _ h3
+    refine ((consistencyDefect_outcome_equiv _
+      (constTupleEquiv (Fin D.k) (PolyIndex D.m (DirectScalarQ D) D.d)) _ _
+        S.ψ).symm.trans
+      (consistencyDefect_congr _ _ _ _ _ S.ψ ?_ ?_)).trans_le h3'
+    · intro _ p
+      change heteroKron (((directPolynomialMeasurement D GA₀).postprocess
+        (fun g _ => g)).effect (fun _ => p)) 1 = _
+      rw [postprocess_const_tuple_effect_self]
+    · intro _ p
+      change heteroKron 1 (((directPolynomialMeasurement D GB₀).postprocess
+        (fun g _ => g)).effect (fun _ => p)) = _
+      rw [postprocess_const_tuple_effect_self]
+
+end
+
+end MIPStarRE.QPBT

 # The directly indexed low-degree game
 
 The low-degree game used by the Pauli-basis combining argument is needed in
 dimension `2 * m + 2`.  The existing conditionally linear game represents a
 coordinate index by an equally sized fiber in the scalar field and therefore
 requires the dimension to divide the field size.  This file gives the separate
 directly indexed variant which samples that index directly.
 
 The geometric line carrier records the sampled coordinate, and line evaluation
 uses an `Option` outcome rather than assigning a value when a point does not
 determine one.  The game retains the point, axis-line, and diagonal-line answer
 formats and the nine ordered type branches of the original low-degree game.
 
 The `Transport` modules relate the direct game to the seed-indexed game and to
 the low individual degree test: `Transport.Correspondence`
 identifies coordinates, answers, and the question law of the two QPBT
 presentations; `Transport.SeedFiber` dilates a seed-indexed strategy to a
 direct strategy by a correlated residue register, and `Transport.SeedFiberValue`
 shows that the dilation preserves the value exactly; `Transport.Questions`
 reads LDT lines as canonical direct questions and rebases direct answers;
-`Transport.Strategy` reads one coordinate of a projective direct strategy as a
+`Transport.Strategy` reads one coordinate of a projective direct strategy as an
 LDT projective strategy, with exact Born-weight formulas for both constructions;
 `Transport.Consistency` reexpresses the three single-polynomial LDT consistency
 relations in direct coordinates, the first two at a fixed tuple coordinate; and
 `Transport.BranchComparison`, `Transport.DiagonalRecursion`, and
 `Transport.PassConversion` convert a value bound of the direct game into the
 pass hypothesis of the low individual degree theorem for every
 coordinate strategy.  `GameValue` supplies the rejection calculus relating the
 direct value to the LDT branch weights.  `Transport.Error` carries the
 scalar half of the transport: the auxiliary sampling parameter with which
-the low individual degree theorem is applied, bounds on the three terms of its error
-function, and the absorption of the resulting simultaneous-measurement
-estimate into the error function of `lem:ld-soundness`.
+the low individual degree theorem is applied, bounds on the three terms of its
+error function, and the absorption of the resulting simultaneous-measurement
+estimate into the error function of `lem:ld-soundness`; and
+`Transport.Simultaneous` applies that theorem to every coordinate, combines
+coordinate polynomial measurements by the palindromic product of
+`lem:ld-sandwich`, and proves the polynomial-tuple conclusion of
+`lem:ld-soundness` for simultaneity parameter `1`.  It also records why the
+coordinate conclusions do not determine simultaneous measurements for larger
+parameters.
 
 ## References
 
 The underlying game is `def:ld-game` in
 `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`, with source origin

 	\begin{enumerate}
 		\item (\emph{Game correspondence.}) The source asserts that the two games are identical; they are not.  \section{The Magic Square game}
 % Paper label sec:ms kept for cross-reference fidelity.
 \label{sec:ms}
 
 We recall the Magic Square game of Mermin and Peres. It is a simple self-test for two EPR pairs, and it allows one to test that a pair of binary observables \emph{anticommutes}; both properties are used in the Pauli basis test. Here it is presented as a binary constraint satisfaction game. Throughout this section and the next, $\sigma^X$ and $\sigma^Z$ denote the single-qubit Pauli observables, with associated two-outcome projective measurements $\{\sigma^W_b\}_{b \in \F_2}$ for $W \in \{X,Z\}$.
 
 \begin{definition}[The Magic Square game]\label{def:ms-game}
 	\uses{def:game, def:graph-distribution}
 	The Magic Square game $\mathfrak{G}^{\mathrm{MS}}$ is the following two-player game. There are $9$ variables $x_1,\ldots,x_9$ taking values in $\F_2$, arranged in a $3 \times 3$ grid: the cell in row $r$ and column $c$ contains the variable $x_{3(r-1)+c}$. There are $6$ linear equations over these variables: for each of the three rows and each of the first two columns, the sum of the three variables in it equals $0$; for the third column, the sum of the three variables in it equals $1$.
 
 	The question types are
 	\begin{align*}
 		\mathcal T^{\mathrm{mc}} &= \{\mathsf{Constraint}_i : i = 1,2,\ldots,6\}\;,\\
 		\mathcal T^{\mathrm{mv}} &= \{\mathsf{Variable}_j : j = 1,2,\ldots,9\}\;,\\
 		\mathcal T^{\mathrm{ms}} &= \mathcal T^{\mathrm{mc}} \cup \mathcal T^{\mathrm{mv}}\;,
 	\end{align*}
 	where $\mathsf{Constraint}_i$ for $i \in \{1,2,3\}$ denotes the constraint of row $i$ (with variables $x_{3(i-1)+1}, x_{3(i-1)+2}, x_{3(i-1)+3}$), $\mathsf{Constraint}_4$ and $\mathsf{Constraint}_5$ denote the constraints of the first two columns, and $\mathsf{Constraint}_6$ denotes the constraint of the third column (with variables $x_{i-3}, x_{i}, x_{i+3}$ for $\mathsf{Constraint}_i$, $i \in \{4,5,6\}$).
 
 	The question distribution is as follows: the verifier samples $\mathsf{Constraint}_i$ uniformly from $\mathcal T^{\mathrm{mc}}$, then samples $\mathsf{Variable}_j$ uniformly among the three variables appearing in the row or column of $\mathsf{Constraint}_i$; one player, chosen uniformly at random, receives $\mathsf{Constraint}_i$ and the other receives $\mathsf{Variable}_j$. Equivalently, the verifier samples a uniformly random edge of the bipartite \emph{type graph} $G^{\mathrm{ms}}$ on vertex sets $\mathcal T^{\mathrm{mc}}$ and $\mathcal T^{\mathrm{mv}}$, whose edges are $\mathsf{Constraint}_i \,\text{---}\, \mathsf{Variable}_{3(i-1)+j}$ for $i,j \in \{1,2,3\}$ and $\mathsf{Constraint}_i \,\text{---}\, \mathsf{Variable}_{(i-3)+3(j-1)}$ for $i \in \{4,5,6\}$, $j \in \{1,2,3\}$ ($18$ edges in total, and no self-loops), and sends one endpoint to a uniformly random player and the other endpoint to the other player.
 
 	The $\mathsf{Constraint}$ player answers with three bits $(\beta_{v_1}, \beta_{v_2}, \beta_{v_3}) \in \F_2^3$, where $(v_1,v_2,v_3)$ are the indices of the three variables of $\mathsf{Constraint}_i$; the $\mathsf{Variable}$ player answers with a single bit $\gamma \in \F_2$. The players win if and only if the $\mathsf{Constraint}$ player's answer satisfies the equation associated with $\mathsf{Constraint}_i$ and $\gamma = \beta_j$.
 \end{definition}
 
 The following theorem records the self-testing (rigidity) properties of the Magic Square game. It is used in the soundness analysis of the Pauli basis test to enforce anticommutation relations between certain pairs of observables.
 With zero-based labels, the paper's variables $1$ and $5$ have labels $0$ and
 $4$, respectively.
 
 \begin{theorem}[Rigidity of the Magic Square game]\label{thm:ms-rigidity}
 	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_ms_rigidity}
 	\leanok
 	\uses{def:ms-game, def:tensor-product-value, def:EPR, def:povm-distance}
 	Let $\mathcal S = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$ be a strategy that succeeds in the Magic Square game $\mathfrak{G}^{\mathrm{MS}}$ with probability $1-\eps$, where $\ket{\psi} \in \hilb_{\mathrm A} \ot \hilb_{\mathrm B}$. Then there exist local isometries $\phi_{\mathrm A}\colon \hilb_{\mathrm A} \to \hilb_{\mathrm A'} \ot \hilb_{\mathrm A''}$ and $\phi_{\mathrm B}\colon \hilb_{\mathrm B} \to \hilb_{\mathrm B'} \ot \hilb_{\mathrm B''}$, where $\hilb_{\mathrm A'}, \hilb_{\mathrm B'} \cong (\C^2)^{\ot 2}$ and $\hilb_{\mathrm A''}, \hilb_{\mathrm B''}$ are finite dimensional, and a state $\ket{\mathrm{aux}} \in \hilb_{\mathrm A''} \ot \hilb_{\mathrm B''}$, such that:
 	\begin{enumerate}
 		\item $\bigl\| \phi_{\mathrm A} \ot \phi_{\mathrm B} \ket{\psi} - \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_2}^{\ot 2} \ot \ket{\mathrm{aux}} \bigr\| \le O(\sqrt\eps)$;
 		\item letting $\tilde A^x_a = \phi_{\mathrm A} A^x_a \phi_{\mathrm A}^\dagger$ and $\tilde B^y_b = \phi_{\mathrm B} B^y_b \phi_{\mathrm B}^\dagger$,

 			I_{\mathrm{A'A''}} \ot \tilde B^{\mathsf{Variable}_5}_b &\approx_{\sqrt\eps} I_{\mathrm{A'A''B''}} \ot (\sigma^Z_b)_{\mathrm B'}\;,

+\documentclass[11pt]{article}

+\title{Simultaneous Polynomial Measurements Are Not Obtained Coordinatewise}
+\author{}
+\date{2026-09-05}
+
+\begin{document}
+\maketitle
+
+\section{At a glance}
+
+\begin{itemize}
+  \item \textbf{Difficulty.} Easy for simultaneity parameter $k = 1$, hard
+  for general $k$.  The coordinatewise route planned for the formalization
+  applies the single-polynomial soundness theorem to each coordinate and
+  combines the resulting measurements by the sandwich of the source's
+  Lemma~\texttt{lem:ld-sandwich}; an explicit pair of measurements refutes
+  every bound this route could produce.  The source instead cites a
+  reduction of the $k$-tuple test to the single-polynomial test in $m + k$
+  variables, which is not formalized.
+  \item \textbf{Estimated weight.} The case $k = 1$ is closed by relabeling
+  the coordinate conclusions (about 150 lines).  The combining reduction
+  needs a combined strategy for the directly indexed game in dimension
+  $m + k$, a transfer of the success probability, and the extraction of
+  $k$ polynomials from one polynomial by linearity: roughly 8--15 new
+  definitions and 3000--5000 lines of formal proof.
+  \item \textbf{Mathlib/project split.} The counterexample is finite Fourier
+  analysis over $\F_{2^s}$ and a Gram-matrix estimate.  The missing reduction
+  is almost entirely project-local (game constructions and the consistency
+  calculus), with the Schwartz--Zippel lemma and multivariate polynomial
+  algebra taken from Mathlib.
+  \item \textbf{Key mathematical inputs.} Additive characters of $\F_q^2$
+  and isotropic vectors of a symmetric pairing in characteristic two; the
+  eigenvalue bound for nearly orthogonal unit vectors; the reduction proving
+  Theorem~4.43 from Theorem~4.40 in \cite{Natarajan2018NEEXP}.  Tracked in
+  \ghissue{134}.
+\end{itemize}
+
+\section{Key theorem forms}
+
+The source theorem (\texttt{lem:ld-soundness}) states that for every
+projective strategy passing the low individual degree game with parameters
+$(q,m,d,k)$ with probability at least $1 - \eps$ there are polynomial-tuple
+measurements $G^{\mathrm A}$ and $G^{\mathrm B}$, with outcomes
+$(g_1,\dots,g_k)$ of individual degree at most $d$, such that on average over
+a uniform point $u \in \F_q^m$
+\[
+  A^{\mathsf{Point},u}_{a} \ot I \simeq_{\delta_{\mathrm{ld}}}
+    I \ot G^{\mathrm B}_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot) = a]},
+  \qquad
+  G^{\mathrm A}_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot) = a]} \ot I \simeq_{\delta_{\mathrm{ld}}}
+    I \ot B^{\mathsf{Point},u}_{a},
+  \qquad
+  G^{\mathrm A}_{g} \ot I \simeq_{\delta_{\mathrm{ld}}} I \ot G^{\mathrm B}_{g},
+  \tag{source form}
+\]
+where $a = (a_1,\dots,a_k)$ and
+$\mathrm{eval}_u(g_1,\dots,g_k) = (g_1(u),\dots,g_k(u))$.
+
+The formalization planned to derive this from the case $k = 1$ as follows.
+Reading the $i$-th coordinate of every answer yields $k$ strategies for the
+game with $k = 1$, each passing with probability at least $1 - 3\eps$; the
+single-polynomial theorem gives projective measurements $G^{w,i}$ with
+\[
+  A^{\mathsf{Point},u}_{[a_i]} \ot I \simeq_{\delta}
+    I \ot G^{\mathrm B,i}_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot) = a_i]},
+  \qquad
+  G^{\mathrm A,i}_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot) = a_i]} \ot I \simeq_{\delta}
+    I \ot B^{\mathsf{Point},u}_{[a_i]},
+  \qquad
+  G^{\mathrm A,i}_{g} \ot I \simeq_{\delta} I \ot G^{\mathrm B,i}_{g},
+  \tag{coordinate form}
+\]
+where $A^{\mathsf{Point},u}_{[a_i]}$ is the $i$-th marginal of the joint
+point measurement; and the planned combination was the sandwich
+\[
+  C^{w}_{g_1,\dots,g_k}
+    = G^{w,k}_{g_k} \cdots G^{w,2}_{g_2}\, G^{w,1}_{g_1}\,
+      G^{w,2}_{g_2} \cdots G^{w,k}_{g_k},
+  \qquad
+  A^{\mathsf{Point},u}_{a} \ot I \simeq_{C k (\delta + md/q)^{1/2}}
+    I \ot C^{\mathrm B}_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot) = a]},
+  \tag{planned form}
+\]
+with a universal constant $C$, and likewise on the other side and for the
+global relation.  We show that no statement of the planned form holds: the
+coordinate form, even with $\delta = 0$ and even with both point
+measurements and all $2k$ polynomial measurements available, does not
+determine any polynomial-tuple measurement consistent with the joint point
+measurement.
+
+What the formalization proves is the source form for $k = 1$, with the
+error of the low individual degree theorem at the auxiliary parameter used
+by the transport, and this is the only value of $k$ instantiated by the
+Pauli basis test analysis.%
+\footnote{The declaration is
+\leanid{exists\_directSimultaneousPolynomialMeasurements\_of\_k\_eq\_one}
+in \doclink{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/DirectLowDegree/Transport/Simultaneous.lean};
+the instantiation with $k = 1$ at dimension $2m+2$ is in the proof of
+\texttt{lem:qld-4-7}, \path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex}.}
+
+\section{The source assertion}
+
+The proof of \texttt{lem:ld-soundness} in
+\cite[lines~413--458]{Ji2020MIPStar} treats $k = 1$ by an identification
+with the tensor-code test of \cite{Ji2021Quantum} (the identification is
+examined in \path{docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex}) and
+then extends to general $k$ by reference to the derivation of Theorem~4.43
+from Theorem~4.40 in \cite[lines~1409--1503]{Natarajan2018NEEXP}.  That
+derivation is not coordinatewise.  It builds two combined provers who play
+the single-polynomial test in $m + k$ variables: on a point $(\alpha, u)$
+the combined prover asks the original prover for the $k$ values
+$(b_1,\dots,b_k)$ at $u$ and returns $\sum_i \alpha_i b_i$, and on a line
+it returns the corresponding combination of the $k$ answer polynomials.  The
+single-polynomial theorem then yields one measurement with outcomes
+$g(\alpha,u)$, and the $k$ polynomials are recovered from $g$ because
+$g$ is exactly linear in $\alpha$ with high probability, by the
+Schwartz--Zippel lemma.  The simultaneity of the $k$ outputs is thus
+inherited from the joint answers of the original provers through a single
+application of the $k = 1$ theorem.
+
+\section{The counterexample}
+
+Let $q = 2^s$, let $d = 1$, and let $\Gamma$ be the set of univariate
+polynomials $g = g_0 + g_1 x$ over $\F_q$, so $|\Gamma| = N = q^2$.  Two
+distinct elements of $\Gamma$ agree at a uniformly random point of $\F_q$
+with probability at most $1/q$.  Bob's Hilbert space is $\C^{\Gamma}$ with
+standard basis $\{\ket{g}\}$; Alice's is a second copy, and the state is
+the maximally entangled state
+$\ket{\psi} = N^{-1/2} \sum_{g \in \Gamma} \ket{g}\ket{g}$, for which
+$(X \ot I)\ket{\psi} = (I \ot X^{\mathsf T})\ket{\psi}$ and
+$\bra{\psi} X \ot Y \ket{\psi} = N^{-1}\tr(X Y^{\mathsf T})$.
+
+Equip $\Gamma \cong \F_q^2$ with the symmetric pairing
+$\langle h, g\rangle = h_0 g_1 + h_1 g_0$ and the additive character
+$\chi(t) = (-1)^{\mathrm{tr}(t)}$, where $\mathrm{tr}$ is the absolute
+trace of $\F_q$; the pairing is nondegenerate, so
+$\phi_h = N^{-1/2} \sum_{g} \chi(\langle h, g\rangle)\ket{g}$, $h \in \Gamma$,
+is an orthonormal basis.  Evaluation at $u \in \F_q$ is represented by the
+vector $v_u = u + x$, since $\langle h, v_u\rangle = h_0 + h_1 u = h(u)$, and
+$\langle v_u, v_u\rangle = 2u = 0$ in characteristic two.  Bob's two
+coordinate measurements are
+\[
+  G^{1}_h = \ket{\phi_h}\bra{\phi_h},
+  \qquad
+  G^{2}_g = \ket{g}\bra{g},
+  \qquad
+  Q^{1,u}_{[a]} = \sum_{h(u) = a} G^1_h,
+  \qquad
+  Q^{2,u}_{[b]} = \sum_{g(u) = b} G^2_g .
+\]
+Writing $H_u = \{h : h(u) = 0\} = \F_q v_u$ and summing the character over
+the coset $\{h : h(u) = a\}$ gives the matrix elements
+\[
+  \bra{g'} Q^{1,u}_{[a]} \ket{g}
+    = \frac1N \sum_{h(u) = a} \chi(\langle h, g - g'\rangle)
+    = \frac{1}{q}\, \chi(\langle h_a, g - g'\rangle)\,
+      \mathbf 1[\,g(u) = g'(u)\,],
+\]
+where $h_a$ is any polynomial with $h_a(u) = a$: the sum over
+$H_u = \F_q v_u$ vanishes unless $\langle v_u, g - g'\rangle = 0$, that is,
+unless $g(u) = g'(u)$, because $v_u$ is isotropic.  Hence $Q^{1,u}_{[a]}$
+is block diagonal for the partition of $\Gamma$ by the value at $u$, it
+commutes with every $Q^{2,u}_{[b]}$, its diagonal entries all equal $1/q$,
+and each product $\Pi^u_{a,b} = Q^{1,u}_{[a]} Q^{2,u}_{[b]}$ is the rank-one
+projector onto the unit vector
+$\xi^u_{a,b} = q^{-1/2} \sum_{g(u) = b} \chi(\langle h_a, g\rangle)\ket{g}$.
+
+Let both players answer the point question $u$ with the joint projective
+measurement $\{\Pi^u_{a,b}\}_{a,b}$, which is real symmetric, and let Alice's
+coordinate polynomial measurements be the transposes $(G^{i})^{\mathsf T}$.
+On $\ket{\psi}$ every relation of the coordinate form holds with error
+$0$: the marginals of the joint point measurement are $Q^{1,u}_{[a]}$ and
+$Q^{2,u}_{[b]}$, which are exactly the evaluated coordinate measurements, and
+$(G^i)^{\mathsf T} \ot I$ agrees with $I \ot G^i$ on $\ket{\psi}$.  The
+collision probability is $1/q$.  The sandwich on Bob's side, evaluated at
+$u$, is
+\[
+  C^{\mathrm B}_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot) = (a,b)]}
+    = \sum_{g(u) = b} \ket{g}\bra{g}\, Q^{1,u}_{[a]}\, \ket{g}\bra{g}
+    = \frac1q\, Q^{2,u}_{[b]},
+\]
+and its consistency with the joint point measurement is
+\[
+  \sum_{a,b} \bra{\psi} \Pi^u_{a,b} \ot C^{\mathrm B}_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot) = (a,b)]}
+    \ket{\psi}
+    = \frac{1}{qN} \sum_{a,b} \tr\bigl(Q^{1,u}_{[a]} Q^{2,u}_{[b]}\bigr)
+    = \frac1q ,
+\]
+so the consistency defect is $1 - 1/q$ for every $u$, whereas the planned
+form promises at most $2C\,(1/q)^{1/2}$.  No universal constant $C$ survives
+$q \to \infty$; with the constant $C = 8$ established for the structured
+sandwich, the planned bound already fails at $q = 2^{9}$.  The same
+computation with the roles of the players exchanged refutes the planned
+bound for Alice's sandwich against Bob's point measurement, and
+$\sum_{g} \bra{\psi} (C^{\mathrm B}_g)^{\mathsf T} \ot C^{\mathrm B}_g \ket{\psi}
+= N^{-1} \sum_{g_1,g_2} |\langle g_2 | \phi_{g_1}\rangle|^4 = 1/N$ refutes it
+for the global relation.
+
+The obstruction is not specific to the sandwich.  Let
+$\{B_{g_1,g_2}\}$ be any POVM on Bob's space with polynomial-pair outcomes,
+and write $B_{g_1,g_2} = N p_{g_1,g_2}\,\rho_{g_1,g_2}$ with
+$p$ a probability distribution and $\rho$ density matrices.  Its
+consistency with the joint point measurement is
+\[
+  \E_{u} \sum_{g_1,g_2} p_{g_1,g_2}\,
+    \bra{\xi^u_{g_1(u),g_2(u)}}\, \rho_{g_1,g_2}\, \ket{\xi^u_{g_1(u),g_2(u)}}
+  \le \max_{g_1,g_2}\,
+    \lambda_{\max}\Bigl(\E_{u}\, \ket{\xi^u_{g_1(u),g_2(u)}}\!\bra{\xi^u_{g_1(u),g_2(u)}}\Bigr).
+\]
+For $u \ne u'$ the supports $\{g : g(u) = g_2(u)\}$ and
+$\{g : g(u') = g_2(u')\}$ meet exactly in $\{g_2\}$, so the $q$ unit vectors
+$\xi^u_{g_1(u),g_2(u)}$ have pairwise inner products of modulus $1/q$, and
+the largest eigenvalue of their Gram matrix is at most $1 + (q-1)/q < 2$.
+Hence the consistency of every polynomial-pair POVM with the joint point
+measurement is below $2/q$, on either side.  Consequently no argument that
+uses only the coordinate form --- with any error, any number of applications
+of the pasting or sandwich facts, and either player as reference --- can
+produce the source form for $k \ge 2$.
+
+Two remarks.  First, the pair $(\ket{\psi}, \Pi, G^1, G^2)$ is not a
+strategy for the low-degree game passing with high probability: by the same
+Gram-matrix bound no line measurement with polynomial-pair outcomes is
+consistent with the point measurements, so the source theorem is not
+contradicted; what fails is the coordinatewise route.  Second, the pasting
+fact (Fact~4.35 of \cite{Natarajan2018NEEXP}, imported as
+\texttt{lem:pasting}) does not repair the route: it requires the two
+coordinates to be evaluated at points $y_1, y_2$ whose conditional
+distribution supports a collision bound $\eta < 1$, whereas the low-degree
+game evaluates all coordinates at the same point, for which the conditional
+collision probability of any two polynomials agreeing there is $1$.
+
+\section{Comparison with the blueprint and formalization}
+
+The blueprint proof of \texttt{lem:ld-soundness} records the source route,
+including the extension from $k = 1$ to general $k$ by the derivation of
+Theorem~4.43 in \cite{Natarajan2018NEEXP}, and lists the game
+correspondence and the parameter bound as open obligations.  The present
+note adds a third: the extension is the combining reduction and must be
+formalized as such.  The directly indexed game and its transport prove the
+coordinate form from the low individual degree theorem for every $k$, and
+the source form for $k = 1$; the combination of the coordinate measurements
+by the sandwich is defined and is a POVM, but it carries no consistency
+estimate, and by the computation above it cannot.
+
+\section{Conclusion}
+
+The source statement is not contradicted.  Its proof for general $k$ is a
+reduction to a single application of the $k = 1$ theorem in $m + k$
+variables, and the formalization must follow that reduction; a
+coordinatewise application of the $k = 1$ theorem followed by any
+combination of the coordinate measurements provably cannot yield the
+theorem.  The application in the analysis of the Pauli basis test uses
+$k = 1$ only, for which the source form is proved from the low individual
+degree theorem.
+

+\bibliography{references}
+

blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:197:	The source states the two line-versus-point clauses with ``the'' $t \in \F_q$ such that $x_{\overline w} = u_0 + t v$. When the direction is nonzero and $x_{\overline w}$ lies on the line, exactly one such $t$ exists and the formulation above agrees with the source. But zero directions occur: Definition~\ref{def:line} explicitly permits them, and the question distribution of Definition~\ref{def:ld-question-distribution} produces $\mathsf{DLine}$ questions with $v' = \pi_{i-1}(v) = 0$ with positive probability, namely whenever the last $m - i + 1$ coordinates of $v$ vanish. In that case $\ell(u_0, 0) = \{u_0\}$, every $t \in \F_q$ satisfies $x_{\overline w} = u_0 + t v'$ when $x_{\overline w} = u_0$, and the source clause does not determine acceptance for a nonconstant answer polynomial. The universal quantification over $t$ adopted in Definition~\ref{def:ld-win-predicate} makes the predicate a well-defined function of its arguments; it accepts vacuously when no such $t$ exists, a case the question distribution never produces. Completeness is unaffected: the restriction of a polynomial $g$ to the singleton line $\ell(u_0,0)$, expressed through the parameterization $t \mapsto u_0 + t \cdot 0$, is the constant polynomial with value $g(u_0)$, which passes the check for every $t$. Soundness is likewise unaffected: zero directions occur with probability at most $2/(mq)$, so any acceptance convention on this event changes success probabilities by at most that amount; the game-correspondence obligation enumerated in the proof of Theorem~\ref{lem:ld-soundness} accounts for this event explicitly, and an error of this shape is absorbed into the universal constants of $\delta_{\mathrm{ld}}$.

blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:280:	The extension from $k = 1$ to general $k$ cited in the proof of Theorem~\ref{lem:ld-soundness} is the reduction deriving Theorem~4.43 from Theorem~4.40 in \cite{Natarajan2018NEEXP}: the $k$ answer polynomials are combined into the single polynomial $(\alpha, u) \mapsto \sum_i \alpha_i g_i(u)$ in $m + k$ variables, the case $k = 1$ is applied once to the combined strategy, and the $k$ polynomials are recovered from the resulting measurement by exact linearity in $\alpha$ and the Schwartz--Zippel lemma.     58	instance (D : DirectLdParams) : Nonempty (Fin D.m) := ⟨D.firstIndex⟩

    60	/-- The direct game used at the extended dimension of the combining map.  Its
    61	field, degree, and simultaneity parameters are inherited from `P`, while its
    62	dimension is `2 * P.m + 2`; no divisibility assertion is introduced.
    63	
    64	The construction has dimension `2 * P.m + 2` without requiring
    65	`2 * P.m + 2 ∣ P.q`; it supplies the directly indexed line and coordinate
    66	spaces used in the dimension-extension argument of
    67	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1257-1293`.
    68	-/
    69	def AdmissibleParams.extendedDirectLd (P : AdmissibleParams) : DirectLdParams where
    70	  q := P.q
    71	  m := 2 * P.m + 2
    72	  d := P.d
    73	  k := 1
    74	  hm := by omega
    75	  hd := P.hd
    76	  hk := by decide
    77	  hq := P.hq

    79	/-- A common random sample for the directly indexed question distribution.
    80	The point, coordinate index, and unrestricted direction are mutually uniform. -/
    81	structure DirectLdSpace (D : DirectLdParams) where
    82	  point : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D
    83	  index : Fin D.m
    84	  direction : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D
    85	  deriving DecidableEq, Fintype
    86	
    87	instance (D : DirectLdParams) : Nonempty (DirectLdSpace D) :=
    88	  ⟨⟨0, D.firstIndex, 0⟩⟩
    89	
    90	/-- Decompose a direct sample into its point and the remaining independent
    91	coordinates. -/
    92	private def directLdSpacePointEquiv (D : DirectLdParams) :
    93	    DirectLdSpace D ≃
    94	      (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) ×
    95	        (Fin D.m × (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) where
    96	  toFun sample := (sample.point, sample.index, sample.direction)
    97	  invFun sample := ⟨sample.1, sample.2.1, sample.2.2⟩
    98	  left_inv sample := by cases sample; rfl
    99	  right_inv sample := by cases sample; rfl
   100	
   101	/-- Decompose a direct sample into its stored index and the remaining
   102	independent coordinates. -/
   103	def directLdSpaceIndexEquiv (D : DirectLdParams) :
   104	    DirectLdSpace D ≃
   105	      Fin D.m ×
   106	        ((Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) ×
   107	          (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) where
   108	  toFun sample := (sample.index, sample.point, sample.direction)
   109	  invFun sample := ⟨sample.2.1, sample.1, sample.2.2⟩
   110	  left_inv sample := by cases sample; rfl
   111	  right_inv sample := by cases sample; rfl
   112	
   113	/-- Compatibility name for the index-first direct-sample decomposition. -/
   114	abbrev directLdSpaceIndexSplitEquiv (D : DirectLdParams) :
   115	    DirectLdSpace D ≃
   116	      Fin D.m × ((Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) × (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) :=
   117	  directLdSpaceIndexEquiv D
   118	
   119	/-- Zero the coordinates preceding the directly sampled prefix index. -/
   120	def directPrefixProjection {D : DirectLdParams} (i : Fin D.m)
   121	    (v : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D :=
   122	  fun j => if j.val < i.val then 0 else v j
   123	
   124	/-- Canonical line descriptions whose coordinate index is stored directly.
   125	Coordinates are numbered from zero, so `index = i` represents coordinate
   126	`i + 1` in the paper. -/
   127	inductive DirectLineDesc (D : DirectLdParams) where
   128	  | axis (base : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) (index : Fin D.m)
   129	      (baseFixed : lineRepMap (coordinateDirection index) base = base)
   130	  | diagonal (base : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) (index : Fin D.m)
   131	      (direction : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)
   132	      (baseFixed : lineRepMap direction base = base)
   133	      (prefixZero : ∀ j : Fin D.m, j.val < index.val → direction j = 0)
   134	  deriving DecidableEq
   135	
   136	/-- The kind of a directly indexed line. -/
   137	def DirectLineDesc.kind {D : DirectLdParams} : DirectLineDesc D → LineKind
   138	  | .axis _ _ _ => .axis
   139	  | .diagonal _ _ _ _ _ => .diagonal
   140	
   141	/-- The coordinate index stored in a directly indexed line. -/
   142	def DirectLineDesc.index {D : DirectLdParams} : DirectLineDesc D → Fin D.m
   143	  | .axis _ index _ => index
   144	  | .diagonal _ index _ _ _ => index
   145	
   146	/-- The canonical base point of a directly indexed line. -/
   147	def DirectLineDesc.base {D : DirectLdParams} :
   148	    DirectLineDesc D → Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D
   149	  | .axis base _ _ => base
   150	  | .diagonal base _ _ _ _ => base
   151	
   152	/-- The geometric direction of a directly indexed line. -/
   153	def DirectLineDesc.direction {D : DirectLdParams} (line : DirectLineDesc D) :
   154	    Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D :=
   155	  match line with
   156	  | .axis _ index _ => coordinateDirection index
   157	  | .diagonal _ _ direction _ _ => direction
   158	
   159	/-- The base of a directly indexed description is fixed by its geometric
   160	direction. -/
   161	theorem DirectLineDesc.base_fixed {D : DirectLdParams} (line : DirectLineDesc D) :
   162	    lineRepMap line.direction line.base = line.base := by
   163	  cases line with
   164	  | axis base index baseFixed => exact baseFixed
   165	  | diagonal base index direction baseFixed prefixZero => exact baseFixed
   166	
   167	/-- Every directly indexed diagonal description retains its prefix-zero
   168	invariant. -/
   169	theorem DirectLineDesc.diagonal_prefix_zero {D : DirectLdParams}
   170	    (line : DirectLineDesc D) (hline : line.kind = .diagonal) :
   171	    ∀ j : Fin D.m, j.val < line.index.val → line.direction j = 0 := by
   172	  cases line with
   173	  | axis base index baseFixed => simp [DirectLineDesc.kind] at hline
   174	  | diagonal base index direction baseFixed prefixZero => exact prefixZero
   175	
   176	/-- The point set represented by a directly indexed line. -/
   177	noncomputable def DirectLineDesc.pointSet {D : DirectLdParams}
   178	    (line : DirectLineDesc D) : Set (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) :=
   179	  linePoints line.base line.direction
   180	
   181	/-- Turn a direct sample into its canonical axis-line description. -/
   182	noncomputable def directALineDescOf (D : DirectLdParams)
   183	    (sample : DirectLdSpace D) : DirectLineDesc D :=
   184	  let direction := coordinateDirection sample.index
   185	  let base := lineRepMap direction sample.point
   186	  .axis base sample.index (lineRepMap_apply_self direction sample.point)
   187	
   188	/-- Turn a direct sample into its canonical diagonal-line description. -/
   189	noncomputable def directDLineDescOf (D : DirectLdParams)
   190	    (sample : DirectLdSpace D) : DirectLineDesc D :=
   191	  let direction := directPrefixProjection sample.index sample.direction
   192	  let base := lineRepMap direction sample.point
   193	  .diagonal base sample.index direction
   194	    (lineRepMap_apply_self direction sample.point) (by
   195	      intro j hj
   196	      change directPrefixProjection sample.index sample.direction j = 0
   197	      rw [directPrefixProjection, if_pos hj])
   198	
   199	/-- The axis-line/point law with a directly sampled coordinate index. -/
   200	noncomputable def directALinePointDist (D : DirectLdParams) :
   201	    Distribution (DirectLineDesc D × (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) :=
   202	  (uniformDistribution (DirectLdSpace D)).map fun sample =>
   203	    (directALineDescOf D sample, sample.point)
   204	
   205	/-- The diagonal-line/point law with a directly sampled prefix index. -/
   206	noncomputable def directDLinePointDist (D : DirectLdParams) :
   207	    Distribution (DirectLineDesc D × (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) :=
   208	  (uniformDistribution (DirectLdSpace D)).map fun sample =>
   209	    (directDLineDescOf D sample, sample.point)
   210	
   211	/-- The equal mixture of the directly indexed axis and diagonal line-point
   212	laws.  This is the replacement for the otherwise undefined extended-dimension
   213	instance used at paper
   214	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1020-1116`. -/
   215	noncomputable def directLinePointDist (D : DirectLdParams) :
   216	    Distribution (DirectLineDesc D × (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) :=
   217	  Distribution.mix (1 / 2) (by norm_num) (by norm_num)
   218	    (directALinePointDist D) (directDLinePointDist D)
   219	
   220	/-- The directly indexed axis-line/point law is probabilistic. -/
   221	theorem directALinePointDist_isProbability (D : DirectLdParams) :
   222	    (directALinePointDist D).IsProbability := by
   223	  exact (uniformDistribution_isProbability (DirectLdSpace D)).map _
   224	
   225	/-- The directly indexed diagonal-line/point law is probabilistic. -/
   226	theorem directDLinePointDist_isProbability (D : DirectLdParams) :
   227	    (directDLinePointDist D).IsProbability := by
   228	  exact (uniformDistribution_isProbability (DirectLdSpace D)).map _
   229	
   230	/-- The directly indexed line-point mixture is probabilistic. -/
   231	theorem directLinePointDist_isProbability (D : DirectLdParams) :
   232	    (directLinePointDist D).IsProbability := by
   233	  exact Distribution.mix_isProbability _ _ _
   234	    (directALinePointDist_isProbability D) (directDLinePointDist_isProbability D)
   235	    (by norm_num) (by norm_num)
   236	
   237	/-- The point and stored-index marginals of the direct axis-line law are
   238	uniform.  This is a direct-index analogue of `lem:alnf`, required by
   239	the repair described in `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`;
   240	the source distribution is at
   241	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:243-257`.
   242	-/
   243	theorem directALinePointDist_point_index_marginal_uniform (D : DirectLdParams) :
   244	    (directALinePointDist D).map Prod.snd =
   245	        uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) ∧
   246	      (directALinePointDist D).map (fun sample => sample.1.index) =
   247	        uniformDistribution (Fin D.m) := by
   248	  constructor
   249	  · unfold directALinePointDist
   250	    rw [Distribution.map_map]
   251	    simpa [Function.comp_def] using
   252	      (uniformDistribution_map_fst_of_equiv
   253	        (e := directLdSpacePointEquiv D)
   254	        (f := fun sample : DirectLdSpace D => sample.point) (by intro; rfl))
   255	  · unfold directALinePointDist
   256	    rw [Distribution.map_map]
   257	    simpa [Function.comp_def, directALineDescOf, DirectLineDesc.index] using
   258	      (uniformDistribution_map_fst_of_equiv
   259	        (e := directLdSpaceIndexEquiv D)
   260	        (f := fun sample : DirectLdSpace D => sample.index) (by intro; rfl))

     4	/-!
     5	# The directly indexed low-degree game
     6	
     7	This module defines polynomial evaluation, questions, answers, and the game
     8	for the directly indexed low-degree interface.
     9	
    10	## References
    11	
    12	The underlying game is `def:ld-game` in
    13	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`, with source origin
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    15	-/
    16	
    17	open scoped BigOperators
    18	
    19	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    20	
    21	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    22	open MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries
    23	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    24	
    25	noncomputable section
    26	
    27	/-- Coefficient lists for a univariate polynomial of degree at most `c` in the
    28	direct scalar field. -/
    29	abbrev DirectDegPoly (D : DirectLdParams) (c : ℕ) :=
    30	  Fin (c + 1) → DirectScalarQ D
    31	
    32	/-- A direct line polynomial evaluates to `a` at `u` when `u` lies on the line
    33	and every parameter presenting `u` gives value `a`.  The universal clause
    34	keeps the zero-direction case explicit. -/
    35	def DirectEvaluatesTo {D : DirectLdParams} {c : ℕ} (line : DirectLineDesc D)
    36	    (f : DirectDegPoly D c) (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)
    37	    (a : DirectScalarQ D) : Prop :=
    38	  (∃ t : DirectScalarQ D, u = line.base + t • line.direction) ∧
    39	    ∀ t : DirectScalarQ D, u = line.base + t • line.direction →
    40	      evalCoefficient f t = a
    41	
    42	/-- Option-completed evaluation of a direct line polynomial.  `none` is an
    43	explicit outcome when the point does not determine an evaluation; no field
    44	value is used as a fallback. -/
    45	noncomputable def directEvalOpt {D : DirectLdParams} {c : ℕ}
    46	    (line : DirectLineDesc D) (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)
    47	    (f : DirectDegPoly D c) : Option (DirectScalarQ D) := by
    48	  classical
    49	  exact if h : ∃ a : DirectScalarQ D, DirectEvaluatesTo line f u a then
    50	    some (Classical.choose h)
    51	  else none
    52	
    53	/-- The typed question alphabet of the directly indexed game. -/
    54	abbrev DirectLdQuestion (D : DirectLdParams) := LdType × DirectLdSpace D
    55	
    56	/-- Canonicalize a common direct sample for one question type.  Irrelevant
    57	coordinates are fixed, so point questions reveal no sampled line index and
    58	axis-line questions reveal no diagonal direction. -/
    59	noncomputable def directLdMap (D : DirectLdParams) :
    60	    LdType → DirectLdSpace D → DirectLdSpace D
    61	  | .point, sample => ⟨sample.point, D.firstIndex, 0⟩
    62	  | .aline, sample =>
    63	      let direction := coordinateDirection sample.index
    64	      ⟨lineRepMap direction sample.point, sample.index, 0⟩
    65	  | .dline, sample =>
    66	      let direction := directPrefixProjection sample.index sample.direction
    67	      ⟨lineRepMap direction sample.point, sample.index, direction⟩
    68	
    69	/-- The directly indexed question distribution.  It has the same uniform
    70	ordered type-pair branches as `ldQuestionDistribution`, but its common sample
    71	contains an actual coordinate index rather than a field seed. -/
    72	noncomputable def directLdQuestionDistribution (D : DirectLdParams) :
    73	    Distribution (DirectLdQuestion D × DirectLdQuestion D) :=
    74	  (uniformDistribution ((LdType × LdType) × DirectLdSpace D)).map fun sample =>
    75	    ((sample.1.1, directLdMap D sample.1.1 sample.2),
    76	      (sample.1.2, directLdMap D sample.1.2 sample.2))
    77	
    78	/-- The directly indexed question law is probabilistic. -/
    79	theorem directLdQuestionDistribution_isProbability (D : DirectLdParams) :
    80	    (directLdQuestionDistribution D).IsProbability := by
    81	  exact (uniformDistribution_isProbability
    82	    ((LdType × LdType) × DirectLdSpace D)).map _
    83	
    84	/-- The answer alphabet of the directly indexed game. -/
    85	inductive DirectLdAnswer (D : DirectLdParams) where
    86	  | pointVals (a : Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D)
    87	  | alinePolys (a : Fin D.k → Fin (D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)
    88	  | dlinePolys (a : Fin D.k → Fin (D.m * D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)
    89	  deriving DecidableEq
    90	
    91	/-- A finite code for the directly indexed answer alphabet. -/
    92	abbrev DirectLdAnswerCode (D : DirectLdParams) :=
    93	  (Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D) ⊕
    94	    ((Fin D.k → Fin (D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D) ⊕
    95	      (Fin D.k → Fin (D.m * D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D))
    96	
    97	/-- Constructor-preserving equivalence between the inductive answer type and
    98	its finite code. -/
    99	noncomputable def directLdAnswerEquiv (D : DirectLdParams) :
   100	    DirectLdAnswer D ≃ DirectLdAnswerCode D where
   101	  toFun
   102	    | .pointVals a => .inl a
   103	    | .alinePolys a => .inr (.inl a)
   104	    | .dlinePolys a => .inr (.inr a)
   105	  invFun
   106	    | .inl a => .pointVals a
   107	    | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePolys a
   108	    | .inr (.inr a) => .dlinePolys a
   109	  left_inv := by intro answer; cases answer <;> rfl
   110	  right_inv := by
   111	    intro answer
   112	    rcases answer with a | a
   113	    · rfl
   114	    · rcases a with a | a <;> rfl
   115	
   116	instance (D : DirectLdParams) : Inhabited (DirectLdAnswer D) :=
   117	  ⟨.pointVals 0⟩
   118	
   119	noncomputable instance (D : DirectLdParams) : Fintype (DirectLdAnswer D) :=
   120	  Fintype.ofEquiv (DirectLdAnswerCode D) (directLdAnswerEquiv D).symm
   121	
   122	/-- Check that a direct-game answer has the constructor required by its
   123	question type. -/
   124	def validDirectLdAnswer {D : DirectLdParams} (t : LdType)
   125	    (answer : DirectLdAnswer D) : Bool :=
   126	  match t, answer with
   127	  | .point, .pointVals _ => true
   128	  | .aline, .alinePolys _ => true
   129	  | .dline, .dlinePolys _ => true
   130	  | _, _ => false
   131	
   132	/-- The directly indexed axis-line versus point acceptance relation. -/
   133	def directAlinePointCondition (D : DirectLdParams)
   134	    (line point : DirectLdSpace D)
   135	    (f : Fin D.k → Fin (D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)
   136	    (a : Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D) : Prop :=
   137	  ∀ t : DirectScalarQ D,
   138	    point.point = line.point + t • coordinateDirection line.index →
   139	      ∀ j : Fin D.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   140	
   141	/-- The directly indexed diagonal-line versus point acceptance relation. -/
   142	def directDlinePointCondition (D : DirectLdParams)
   143	    (line point : DirectLdSpace D)
   144	    (f : Fin D.k → Fin (D.m * D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)
   145	    (a : Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D) : Prop :=
   146	  ∀ t : DirectScalarQ D,
   147	    point.point = line.point + t • line.direction →
   148	      ∀ j : Fin D.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   149	
   150	/-- The directly indexed low-degree win predicate.  It differs from
   151	`ldWinPredicate` only by reading the coordinate index directly from each line
   152	question. -/
   153	noncomputable def directLdWinPredicate (D : DirectLdParams) :
   154	    DirectLdQuestion D → DirectLdQuestion D →
   155	      DirectLdAnswer D → DirectLdAnswer D → Bool :=
   156	  open Classical in
   157	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   158	    if validDirectLdAnswer tA a && validDirectLdAnswer tB b then
   159	      match tA, tB, a, b with
   160	      | .point, .point, .pointVals u, .pointVals v => decide (u = v)
   161	      | .aline, .point, .alinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   162	          decide (directAlinePointCondition D xA xB f u)
   163	      | .point, .aline, .pointVals u, .alinePolys f =>
   164	          decide (directAlinePointCondition D xB xA f u)
   165	      | .dline, .point, .dlinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   166	          decide (directDlinePointCondition D xA xB f u)
   167	      | .point, .dline, .pointVals u, .dlinePolys f =>
   168	          decide (directDlinePointCondition D xB xA f u)
   169	      | .aline, .aline, .alinePolys f, .alinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   170	      | .dline, .dline, .dlinePolys f, .dlinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   171	      | _, _, _, _ => true
   172	    else false
   173	
   174	/-- The directly indexed low-degree game at an arbitrary positive dimension.
   175	It is an internal analysis game, not the conditionally linear verifier game
   176	`ldGame`. -/
   177	noncomputable def directLdGame (D : DirectLdParams) : Game where
   178	  QuestionA := DirectLdQuestion D
   179	  QuestionB := DirectLdQuestion D
   180	  AnswerA := DirectLdAnswer D
   181	  AnswerB := DirectLdAnswer D
   182	  μ := directLdQuestionDistribution D
   183	  μ_prob := directLdQuestionDistribution_isProbability D
   184	  decide := directLdWinPredicate D
   185	
   186	/-- The canonical point question associated with a geometric point. -/
   187	def directLdPointQuestionOf (D : DirectLdParams)
   188	    (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) : DirectLdQuestion D :=
   189	  (.point, ⟨u, D.firstIndex, 0⟩)
   190	
   191	/-- Total point-answer relabeling used in the direct soundness conclusion.
   192	Wrong-form answers are folded into the zero tuple, exactly as for
   193	`ldPointValuesOrZero`. -/
   194	def directLdPointValuesOrZero (D : DirectLdParams) :
   195	    DirectLdAnswer D → Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D
   196	  | .pointVals values => values
   197	  | .alinePolys _ => 0
   198	  | .dlinePolys _ => 0
   199	
   200	/-- A simultaneous tuple of bounded polynomials for the directly indexed
   201	game. -/
   202	noncomputable abbrev DirectPolyTuple (D : DirectLdParams) :=
   203	  Fin D.k → PolyIndex D.m (DirectScalarQ D) D.d
   204	
   205	/-- A polynomial-tuple POVM for the directly indexed game. -/
   206	noncomputable abbrev DirectPolyMeasTuple (D : DirectLdParams) (ι : Type*)
   207	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] :=
   208	  MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement (DirectPolyTuple D) ι
   209	
   210	/-- Evaluate every component of a direct polynomial tuple at a point. -/
   211	def evalDirectPolyTupleAt {D : DirectLdParams}
   212	    (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) (g : DirectPolyTuple D) :
   213	    Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D :=
   214	  fun j => MvPolynomial.eval u (g j).1
   215	
   216	end

    33	/-! ## From a direct strategy to a mature LDT strategy -/
    34	
    35	/-- Regard a matrix-valued projective measurement as a projective measurement
    36	in the mature LDT interface. -/
    37	noncomputable def matrixMeasurementToLDTProjMeas
    38	    {alpha iota : Type*} [Fintype alpha] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    39	    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota)
    40	    (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M) :
    41	    MIPStarRE.LDT.ProjMeas alpha iota where
    42	  toMeasurement := {
    43	    toSubMeas := {
    44	      outcome := M.effect

   368	/-- Correlated residue registers turn two block-diagonal effects into the
   369	uniform average of their matching source-block Born weights. -/
   370	private theorem seedFiberBlockBornAmplitude
   371	    {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) (L : LdParams)
   372	    (A : Fin (L.q / L.m) → Op S.ιA)
   373	    (B : Fin (L.q / L.m) → Op S.ιB) :
   374	    vectorBornAmplitude (seedFiberLiftedState S L)
   375	        (Matrix.blockDiagonal A) (Matrix.blockDiagonal B) =
   376	      (Fintype.card (Fin (L.q / L.m)) : ℂ)⁻¹ *
   377	        ∑ residue, vectorBornAmplitude S.ψ (A residue) (B residue) := by
   378	  classical
   379	  letI : Nonempty (Fin (L.q / L.m)) :=
   380	    Fin.pos_iff_nonempty.mp L.seedFiberCard_pos
   381	  unfold vectorBornAmplitude applyOperatorToState heteroKron Matrix.kronecker
   382	  simp_rw [EuclideanSpace.inner_eq_star_dotProduct]
   383	  simp only [Matrix.toEuclideanLin, Matrix.toLpLin_apply,
   384	    dotProduct, Matrix.mulVec]
   385	  simp_rw [← Finset.univ_product_univ, Finset.sum_product]
   386	  simp [seedFiberLiftedState_apply, Matrix.blockDiagonal_apply,
   387	    mul_assoc, mul_comm]
   388	  ring_nf
   389	  simp_rw [mul_assoc, ← Finset.mul_sum]
   390	  ring_nf
   391	  simp_rw [mul_assoc, ← Finset.mul_sum]
   392	  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
   393	  rw [← mul_assoc]
   394	  congr 1
   395	  exact inv_sqrt_natCast_mul_self (L.q / L.m)

   404	        (Matrix.blockDiagonal A) (Matrix.blockDiagonal B) =

   412	of the original seed-dependent Born weights over the correlated residue. -/
   413	theorem ldStrategyToDirect_bornWeight

   471	          (((directCoordinateProjStrat D S hS r).pointMeasurementA u).outcome a)

   490	            (hS.2 (directPointQuestionOf D v)))
   491	          (directPointAnswerReadout D r)).outcome b)) = _

    30	private theorem directPolynomialRename_degreeOf_le
    31	    (D : DirectLdParams) (p : MvPolynomial (Fin D.m) (DirectScalarQ D))
    32	    (hp : ∀ i, MvPolynomial.degreeOf i p ≤ D.d) (i : Fin D.m) :
    33	    MvPolynomial.degreeOf i (MvPolynomial.rename Fin.rev p) ≤ D.d := by
    34	  rw [← Fin.rev_rev i,
    35	    MvPolynomial.degreeOf_rename_of_injective Fin.rev_injective]
    36	  exact hp (Fin.rev i)

    38	private theorem ldtPolynomial_ext
    39	    {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
    40	    {g h : MIPStarRE.LDT.Polynomial params} (hpoly : g.poly = h.poly) : g = h := by
    41	  cases g with
    42	  | mk gp hg =>
    43	      cases h with
    44	      | mk hp hh =>
    45	          simp only at hpoly
    46	          subst hp
    47	          rfl

    49	/-- Bounded QPBT polynomial representatives are equivalent to LDT
    50	polynomial outcomes.  The variable renaming is the same coordinate reversal
    51	as `directPointEquiv`, so evaluation retains the direct coordinate order. -/
    52	noncomputable def directPolyEquivPolynomial (D : DirectLdParams) :
    53	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
    54	    PolyIndex D.m (DirectScalarQ D) D.d ≃
    55	      MIPStarRE.LDT.Polynomial D.toLDTParameters := by
    56	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
    57	  refine
    58	    { toFun := fun g =>
    59	        { poly := MvPolynomial.rename Fin.rev g.1
    60	          lowIndividualDegree := directPolynomialRename_degreeOf_le D g.1
    61	            (degreeOf_le_of_mem_polyFunc g.2) }
    62	      invFun := fun g =>
    63	        ⟨MvPolynomial.rename Fin.rev g.poly, ?_⟩
    64	      left_inv := ?_
    65	      right_inv := ?_ }
    66	  · rw [MvPolynomial.mem_restrictDegree]
    67	    intro s hs i
    68	    exact (MvPolynomial.degreeOf_le_iff.mp
    69	      (directPolynomialRename_degreeOf_le D g.poly g.lowIndividualDegree i)) s hs
    70	  · intro g
    71	    apply Subtype.ext
    72	    change MvPolynomial.rename Fin.rev
    73	      (MvPolynomial.rename Fin.rev g.1) = g.1
    74	    rw [MvPolynomial.rename_rename]
    75	    rw [show Fin.rev ∘ Fin.rev = id by funext i; simp]
    76	    exact MvPolynomial.rename_id_apply g.1
    77	  · intro g
    78	    cases g with
    79	    | mk p hp =>
    80	        have hpoly : MvPolynomial.rename Fin.rev
    81	            (MvPolynomial.rename Fin.rev p) = p := by
    82	          rw [MvPolynomial.rename_rename]
    83	          rw [show Fin.rev ∘ Fin.rev = id by funext i; simp]
    84	          exact MvPolynomial.rename_id_apply p
    85	        apply ldtPolynomial_ext
    86	        exact hpoly

    88	@[simp] theorem directPolyEquivPolynomial_poly
    89	    (D : DirectLdParams) (g : PolyIndex D.m (DirectScalarQ D) D.d) :
    90	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
    91	    (directPolyEquivPolynomial D g).poly = MvPolynomial.rename Fin.rev g.1 := by
    92	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
    93	  rfl

    95	/-- The polynomial equivalence commutes with evaluation after the direct point
    96	and scalar codings. -/
    97	@[simp] theorem directPolyEquivPolynomial_apply
    98	    (D : DirectLdParams) (g : PolyIndex D.m (DirectScalarQ D) D.d)
    99	    (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) :
   100	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   101	    directPolyEquivPolynomial D g (directPointEquiv D u) =
   102	      directScalarEquiv D (MvPolynomial.eval u g.1) := by
   103	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   104	  unfold MIPStarRE.LDT.Polynomial.toFun evalPolynomialModel
   105	  rw [directPolyEquivPolynomial_poly]
   106	  unfold decodePoint
   107	  rw [MvPolynomial.eval_rename]
   108	  congr 1
   109	  apply congrArg (fun v : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D =>
   110	    MvPolynomial.eval v g.1)
   111	  funext i
   112	  simp only [Function.comp_apply, directPointEquiv_apply, Fin.rev_rev]
   113	  change (directScalarEquiv D).symm (directScalarEquiv D (u i)) = u i
   114	  exact (directScalarEquiv D).symm_apply_apply (u i)

   201	/-- Evaluating the transported polynomial measurement is the relabeling of

   203	theorem directPolynomialMeasurement_evaluation_effect
   204	    (D : DirectLdParams) :
   205	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   206	    ∀ {iota : Type*} [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   207	      (G : ProjMeas (MIPStarRE.LDT.Polynomial D.toLDTParameters) iota)

   212	          (ProjMeas.postprocess G
   213	            (fun g => g (directPointEquiv D u))).toMeasurement).effect
   214	            (directScalarEquiv D a) := by
   215	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel

   239	/-! ## Correlated-ancilla compression -/
   240	
   241	/-!
   242	The diagonal-block conditional expectation preserves either mixed defect
   243	exactly because the point measurement on the opposite carrier is constant on
   244	the residue register.  It does not yield a global/global compression theorem:
   245	the lifted state pairs equal residues, whereas separately compressing both
   246	polynomial measurements produces an independent double average over residues.
   247	Neither quantity bounds the other in general.  This open obstruction is
   248	recorded in `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`.
   249	-/
   250	
   251	/-- The normalized diagonal-block average of an operator on a carrier with a
   252	finite ancillary register.  This is the local conditional expectation used to
   253	discard one half of the correlated seed-residue ancilla. -/
   254	noncomputable def averageDiagonalBlock
   255	    {iota block : Type*} [Fintype iota] [Fintype block]
   256	    (A : Op (iota × block)) : Op iota := by
   257	  classical
   258	  exact (Fintype.card block : ℝ)⁻¹ •
   259	    ∑ r, A.submatrix (fun i => (i, r)) (fun i => (i, r))
   260	
   261	/-- Compress a POVM through the normalized diagonal-block average.  The
   262	nonemptiness assumption says precisely that the normalized finite average is
   263	defined over at least one ancillary basis element. -/
   264	noncomputable def correlatedAncillaCompressMeasurement
   265	    {alpha iota block : Type*}
   266	    [Fintype alpha] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   267	    [Fintype block] [DecidableEq block] [Nonempty block]
   268	    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha (iota × block)) :
   269	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota :=
   270	  MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne
   271	    (fun a => averageDiagonalBlock (M.effect a))
   272	    (fun a => by
   273	      unfold averageDiagonalBlock
   274	      apply smul_nonneg
   275	      · positivity
   276	      · exact Finset.sum_nonneg fun r _ =>
   277	          Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mpr
   278	            ((Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mp (M.pos a)).submatrix
   279	              (fun i => (i, r))))
   280	    (by
   281	      classical
   282	      ext i j
   283	      simp only [averageDiagonalBlock, Matrix.sum_apply, Matrix.smul_apply,
   284	        Matrix.submatrix_apply]
   285	      calc
   286	        ∑ a, (Fintype.card block : ℝ)⁻¹ •
   287	              ∑ r, M.effect a (i, r) (j, r) =
   288	            (Fintype.card block : ℝ)⁻¹ •
   289	              ∑ a, ∑ r, M.effect a (i, r) (j, r) := by
   290	                rw [Finset.smul_sum]
   291	        _ = (Fintype.card block : ℝ)⁻¹ •
   292	              ∑ r, ∑ a, M.effect a (i, r) (j, r) := by
   293	                rw [Finset.sum_comm]
   294	        _ = (Fintype.card block : ℝ)⁻¹ •
   295	              ∑ r, (1 : Op (iota × block)) (i, r) (j, r) := by
   296	                congr 1
   297	                apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   298	                intro r _
   299	                simpa only [Matrix.sum_apply] using
   300	                  congrFun (congrFun M.sum_eq_one (i, r)) (j, r)
   301	        _ = (1 : Op iota) i j := by
   302	              simp [Matrix.one_apply, Fintype.card_ne_zero])
   303	
   304	@[simp] theorem correlatedAncillaCompressMeasurement_effect
   305	    {alpha iota block : Type*}
   306	    [Fintype alpha] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   307	    [Fintype block] [DecidableEq block] [Nonempty block]
   308	    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha (iota × block)) (a : alpha) :
   309	    (correlatedAncillaCompressMeasurement M).effect a =
   310	      averageDiagonalBlock (M.effect a) :=
   311	  rfl
   312	
   313	private theorem averageDiagonalBlock_finset_sum
   314	    {alpha iota block : Type*} [Fintype iota] [Fintype block]
   315	    (s : Finset alpha) (A : alpha → Op (iota × block)) :
   316	    averageDiagonalBlock (∑ a ∈ s, A a) =
   317	      ∑ a ∈ s, averageDiagonalBlock (A a) := by
   318	  classical
   319	  ext i j
   320	  simp only [averageDiagonalBlock, Matrix.smul_apply, Matrix.sum_apply,
   321	    Matrix.submatrix_apply]
   322	  simp_rw [Finset.smul_sum]
   323	  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
   324	
   325	/-- Normalized diagonal-block compression commutes with deterministic outcome
   326	postprocessing. -/
   327	theorem correlatedAncillaCompressMeasurement_postprocess
   328	    {alpha beta iota block : Type*}
   329	    [Fintype alpha] [DecidableEq alpha]
   330	    [Fintype beta] [DecidableEq beta]
   331	    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   332	    [Fintype block] [DecidableEq block] [Nonempty block]
   333	    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha (iota × block))
   334	    (f : alpha → beta) :
   335	    correlatedAncillaCompressMeasurement (M.postprocess f) =
   336	      (correlatedAncillaCompressMeasurement M).postprocess f := by
   337	  classical
   338	  apply MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ext
   339	  intro b
   340	  rw [MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect,
   341	    correlatedAncillaCompressMeasurement_effect,
   342	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect]
   343	  exact averageDiagonalBlock_finset_sum
   344	    (Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b)) M.effect
   345	
   346	/-- Specialize ancillary compression to the nonempty residue fiber supplied by
   347	the divisibility data of `LdParams`. -/
   348	noncomputable def seedFiberCompressMeasurement
   349	    (L : LdParams) {alpha iota : Type*}
   350	    [Fintype alpha] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   351	    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha

    83	    [Fintype Y₂] [DecidableEq Y₂] [Fintype R₂] [DecidableEq R₂]

   277	      (∑ g : (i : Fin k) → Γ i,
   278	        sandwichProduct (fun i x' a => (G i x').effect a) x g) = 1 := by
   279	  classical
   280	  induction k with
   281	  | zero =>
   282	      constructor
   283	      · intro g
   284	        change 0 ≤ (1 : Op ι)
   285	        exact Matrix.PosSemidef.one.nonneg
   286	      · simp [sandwichProduct, orderedCoordinateProduct]
   287	  | succ k ih =>

   291	          · intro g

   294	          · change
   295	              (∑ g : (i : Fin 1) → Γ i,

   301	                exact Fintype.sum_equiv (Fin.snocEquiv Γ).symm _ _
   302	                  (by intro g; rw [Equiv.apply_symm_apply])
   303	              _ = ∑ a : Γ 0, (G 0 x).effect a := by
   304	                rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type]
   305	                apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   306	                intro a _
   307	                simp only [Fintype.sum_unique]
   308	                congr 1

   310	      | succ k =>
   311	          have hprev := ih
   312	            (G := fun i x' => G i.castSucc x')
   313	            (hG := fun i x' => hG i.castSucc x')
   314	          constructor
   315	          · intro g
   316	            change 0 ≤
   317	              (G (Fin.last (k + 1)) x).effect (g (Fin.last (k + 1))) *
   318	                orderedCoordinateProduct (k + 1) (fun i => Γ i.castSucc)
   319	                  (fun i a => (G i.castSucc x).effect a)
   320	                  (fun i => g i.castSucc) *
   321	                (G (Fin.last (k + 1)) x).effect (g (Fin.last (k + 1)))

   325	                (((G (Fin.last (k + 1)) x).effect (g (Fin.last (k + 1))))ᴴ *
   326	                  orderedCoordinateProduct (k + 1) (fun i => Γ i.castSucc)
   327	                    (fun i a => (G i.castSucc x).effect a)
   328	                    (fun i => g i.castSucc) *
   329	                  (G (Fin.last (k + 1)) x).effect
   330	                    (g (Fin.last (k + 1)))).PosSemidef :=
   331	              (Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mp hinner).conjTranspose_mul_mul_same _
   332	            rw [MIPStarRE.QPBT.DistanceCalculus.measurement_effect_hermitian] at hpos
   333	            exact hpos
   334	          · change
   335	              (∑ g : (i : Fin (k + 2)) → Γ i,
   336	                orderedCoordinateProduct (k + 2) Γ
   337	                  (fun i a => (G i x).effect a) g) = 1
   338	            calc
   339	              (∑ g : (i : Fin (k + 2)) → Γ i,
   340	                  orderedCoordinateProduct (k + 2) Γ
   341	                    (fun i a => (G i x).effect a) g) =
   342	                  ∑ p : Γ (Fin.last (k + 1)) ×
   343	                      ((i : Fin (k + 1)) → Γ i.castSucc),
   344	                    orderedCoordinateProduct (k + 2) Γ
   345	                      (fun i a => (G i x).effect a) ((Fin.snocEquiv Γ) p) := by
   346	                exact Fintype.sum_equiv (Fin.snocEquiv Γ).symm _ _
   347	                  (by intro g; rw [Equiv.apply_symm_apply])
   348	              _ = ∑ a : Γ (Fin.last (k + 1)),
   349	                    ∑ g : (i : Fin (k + 1)) → Γ i.castSucc,
   350	                      (G (Fin.last (k + 1)) x).effect a *

   354	                rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type]

   356	                intro a _
   357	                apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   358	                intro g _
   359	                simp [orderedCoordinateProduct]
   360	              _ = ∑ a : Γ (Fin.last (k + 1)),
   361	                    (G (Fin.last (k + 1)) x).effect a *
   362	                      (∑ g : (i : Fin (k + 1)) → Γ i.castSucc,
   363	                        orderedCoordinateProduct (k + 1) (fun i => Γ i.castSucc)
   364	                          (fun i b => (G i.castSucc x).effect b) g) *
   365	                      (G (Fin.last (k + 1)) x).effect a := by
   366	                apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   367	                intro a _
   368	                rw [Finset.mul_sum, Finset.sum_mul]

   374	                    orderedCoordinateProduct (k + 1) (fun i => Γ i.castSucc)

   382	/-- Splitting the last outcome from a tuple of length at least two exposes the
   383	recursive palindromic product. -/
   384	private theorem sandwichProduct_snoc {k : ℕ} {X ι : Type*}
   385	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {Γ : Fin (k + 2) → Type*}
   386	    [∀ i, Fintype (Γ i)]
   387	    (G : (i : Fin (k + 2)) → X → Measurement (Γ i) ι)
   388	    (x : X) (p : Γ (Fin.last (k + 1)) ×
   389	      ((i : Fin (k + 1)) → Γ i.castSucc)) :
   390	    sandwichProduct (fun i x' a => (G i x').effect a) x
   391	        ((Fin.snocEquiv Γ) p) =
   392	      (G (Fin.last (k + 1)) x).effect p.1 *
   393	        sandwichProduct (fun i x' a => (G i.castSucc x').effect a) x p.2 *
   394	      (G (Fin.last (k + 1)) x).effect p.1 := by
   395	  simp [sandwichProduct, orderedCoordinateProduct]

   194	    change ConsRel (directCoordinateProjStrat D S hS r).state
   195	      (uniformDistribution (Point D.toLDTParameters))
   196	      (polynomialEvaluationFamily D.toLDTParameters G.toSubMeas)
   197	      (IdxProjMeas.toIdxSubMeas
   198	        (directCoordinateProjStrat D S hS r).pointMeasurementB) delta
   199	    exact h
   200	  have hldt := strategyConsRel_consistencyDefect_le S
   201	    (uniformDistribution (Point D.toLDTParameters))
   202	    (uniformDistribution_isProbability (Point D.toLDTParameters))
   203	    (ldtPolynomialEvaluationMeasurement D G)
   204	    (ldtCoordinatePointMeasurementB D S hS r) delta hbase
   205	  have heq := consistencyDefect_congr
   206	    (uniformDistribution (Point D.toLDTParameters))
   207	    (ldtPolynomialEvaluationLeft D G)
   208	    (fun u a => heteroKron
   209	      ((ldtPolynomialEvaluationMeasurement D G u).outcome a) 1)
   210	    (ldtPointBPlaced D S hS r)
   211	    (fun u a => heteroKron 1
   212	      ((ldtCoordinatePointMeasurementB D S hS r u).outcome a)) S.ψ
   213	    (by intro u a; rfl) (by intro u a; rfl)
   214	  rw [directPolynomialPoint_consistencyDefect_eq D S hS r G, heq]
   215	  exact hldt
