   217	/-- Relabeling both global polynomial measurements identifies their direct
   218	QPBT defect with the LDT global/global defect. -/
   219	theorem directPolynomialPolynomial_consistencyDefect_eq
   220	    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D)) :
   221	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   222	    ∀ (GA : ProjMeas (MIPStarRE.LDT.Polynomial D.toLDTParameters) S.ιA)
   223	      (GB : ProjMeas (MIPStarRE.LDT.Polynomial D.toLDTParameters) S.ιB),
   224	      consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Unit)
   225	          (fun _ g => heteroKron ((directPolynomialMeasurement D GA).effect g) 1)
   226	          (fun _ g => heteroKron 1 ((directPolynomialMeasurement D GB).effect g))
   227	          S.ψ =
   228	        consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Unit)
   229	          (fun _ g => ldtPolynomialLeftPlaced D GA g)
   230	          (fun _ g => ldtPolynomialRightPlaced D GB g) S.ψ := by
   231	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   232	  intro GA GB
   233	  calc
   234	    consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Unit)
   235	        (fun _ g => heteroKron ((directPolynomialMeasurement D GA).effect g) 1)
   236	        (fun _ g => heteroKron 1 ((directPolynomialMeasurement D GB).effect g))
   237	        S.ψ =
   238	      consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Unit)
   239	        (fun _ g => ldtPolynomialLeftPlaced D GA (directPolyEquivPolynomial D g))
   240	        (fun _ g => ldtPolynomialRightPlaced D GB (directPolyEquivPolynomial D g))
   241	        S.ψ := by
   242	          apply consistencyDefect_congr
   243	          · intro _ g
   244	            unfold ldtPolynomialLeftPlaced
   245	            rw [directPolynomialMeasurement_effect]
   246	          · intro _ g
   247	            unfold ldtPolynomialRightPlaced
   248	            rw [directPolynomialMeasurement_effect]
   249	    _ = consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Unit)
   250	        (fun _ g => ldtPolynomialLeftPlaced D GA g)
   251	        (fun _ g => ldtPolynomialRightPlaced D GB g) S.ψ :=
   252	      consistencyDefect_outcome_equiv (uniformDistribution Unit)
   253	        (directPolyEquivPolynomial D)
   254	        (fun _ g => ldtPolynomialLeftPlaced D GA g)
   255	        (fun _ g => ldtPolynomialRightPlaced D GB g) S.ψ
   256	
   257	/-- Convert the global/global conclusion of `LDT.Test.mainFormal` to the direct
   258	QPBT defect, with the identical numerical bound. -/
   259	theorem directPolynomialPolynomial_consistencyDefect_le
   260	    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D)) :
   261	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   262	    ∀ (GA : ProjMeas (MIPStarRE.LDT.Polynomial D.toLDTParameters) S.ιA)
   263	      (GB : ProjMeas (MIPStarRE.LDT.Polynomial D.toLDTParameters) S.ιB)
   264	      (delta : ℝ),
   265	      ConsRel (strategyQuantumState S) (uniformDistribution Unit)
   266	          (constSubMeasFamily GA.toSubMeas)
   267	          (constSubMeasFamily GB.toSubMeas) delta →
   268	        consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Unit)
   269	          (fun _ g => heteroKron ((directPolynomialMeasurement D GA).effect g) 1)
   270	          (fun _ g => heteroKron 1 ((directPolynomialMeasurement D GB).effect g))
   271	          S.ψ ≤ delta := by
   272	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   273	  intro GA GB delta h
   274	  have hldt := strategyConsRel_consistencyDefect_le S
   275	    (uniformDistribution Unit) (uniformDistribution_isProbability Unit)
   276	    (fun _ => GA) (fun _ => GB) delta h
   277	  have heq := consistencyDefect_congr (uniformDistribution Unit)
   278	    (fun _ g => ldtPolynomialLeftPlaced D GA g)
   279	    (fun _ g => heteroKron (GA.outcome g) 1)
   280	    (fun _ g => ldtPolynomialRightPlaced D GB g)
   281	    (fun _ g => heteroKron 1 (GB.outcome g)) S.ψ
   282	    (by intro _ g; rfl) (by intro _ g; rfl)
   283	  rw [directPolynomialPolynomial_consistencyDefect_eq D S GA GB, heq]
   284	  exact hldt

   286	/-- Deprecated specialization of `strategyConsRel_consistencyDefect_le` for
   287	Alice's LDT point family and Bob's polynomial-evaluation family. -/
   288	@[deprecated strategyConsRel_consistencyDefect_le (since := "2026-09-05")]
   289	theorem maturePointPolynomial_consistencyDefect_le
   290	    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
   291	    (hS : S.IsProjective) (r : Fin D.k) :
   292	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   293	    ∀ (G : ProjMeas (MIPStarRE.LDT.Polynomial D.toLDTParameters) S.ιB)
   294	      (delta : ℝ),
   295	      ConsRel (strategyQuantumState S)
   296	          (uniformDistribution (Point D.toLDTParameters))
   297	          (fun u => (ldtCoordinatePointMeasurementA D S hS r u).toSubMeas)
   298	          (fun u => (ldtPolynomialEvaluationMeasurement D G u).toSubMeas) delta →
   299	        consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Point D.toLDTParameters))
   300	          (ldtPointAPlaced D S hS r)
   301	          (ldtPolynomialEvaluationRight D G) S.ψ ≤ delta := by
   302	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   303	  intro G delta h
   304	  exact strategyConsRel_consistencyDefect_le S
   305	    (uniformDistribution (Point D.toLDTParameters))
   306	    (uniformDistribution_isProbability (Point D.toLDTParameters))
   307	    (ldtCoordinatePointMeasurementA D S hS r)
   308	    (ldtPolynomialEvaluationMeasurement D G) delta h

     5	/-!
     6	# Strategy transport for the directly indexed low-degree game
     7	
     8	This module reads one coordinate of a projective directly indexed strategy as
     9	a two-space mature low individual degree strategy.  The question and answer
    10	transport of `Transport.Questions` supplies the canonical direct question of
    11	every mature line, with the reversed coordinate order and the leading index
    12	of the decoded diagonal direction, together with answer readouts that are
    13	covariant under line rebasing; this establishes all four covariance
    14	conditions of `ProjStrat`.  The module also records exact Born-weight
    15	formulas for both directions of strategy transport.
    16	
    17	## References
    18	
    19	- `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-458`
    20	- `references/ldt-paper/test_definition.tex:49-151`
    21	- `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`
    22	-/

    35	/-- Regard a matrix-valued projective measurement as a projective measurement
    36	in the mature LDT interface. -/
    37	noncomputable def matrixMeasurementToLDTProjMeas
    38	    {alpha iota : Type*} [Fintype alpha] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    39	    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota)
    40	    (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M) :
    41	    MIPStarRE.LDT.ProjMeas alpha iota where
    42	  toMeasurement := {
    43	    toSubMeas := {
    44	      outcome := M.effect
    45	      total := 1
    46	      outcome_pos := M.pos
    47	      sum_eq_total := M.sum_eq_one
    48	      total_le_one := le_rfl
    49	    }
    50	    total_eq_one := rfl
    51	  }
    52	  proj a := (hM a).isIdempotentElem.eq
    53	
    54	@[simp] theorem matrixMeasurementToLDTProjMeas_outcome
    55	    {alpha iota : Type*} [Fintype alpha] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    56	    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota)
    57	    (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M) (a : alpha) :
    58	    (matrixMeasurementToLDTProjMeas M hM).outcome a = M.effect a :=
    59	  rfl

    67	      MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement (DirectLdAnswer D) iota)

   114	/-- The coordinate axis-line family is independent of the chosen affine
   115	parametrization of a mature line. -/
   116	theorem directCoordinateAxisMeasurement_reparam
   117	    (D : DirectLdParams) (r : Fin D.k)
   118	    {iota : Type*} [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   119	    (M : DirectLdQuestion D →
   120	      MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement (DirectLdAnswer D) iota)
   121	    (hM : ∀ q, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (M q)) :
   122	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   123	    AxisParallelMeasurementReparamInvariant D.toLDTParameters
   124	      (directCoordinateAxisMeasurement D r M hM) := by
   125	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   126	  classical
   127	  intro line t f
   128	  simp only [directCoordinateAxisMeasurement, ProjMeas.postprocess,
   129	    SubMeas.postprocess_outcome, matrixMeasurementToLDTProjMeas_outcome]
   130	  rw [directAxisQuestionOf_rebase]
   131	  have hfiber :
   132	      Finset.univ.filter (fun answer =>
   133	        directAxisAnswerReadout D r (line.rebaseAt t) answer =
   134	          AxisLinePolynomial.reparamAt f t) =
   135	        Finset.univ.filter (fun answer =>
   136	          directAxisAnswerReadout D r line answer = f) := by
   137	    ext answer
   138	    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
   139	    rw [directAxisAnswerReadout_rebase]
   140	    exact (AxisLinePolynomial.reparamAtEquiv t).injective.eq_iff
   141	  rw [hfiber]

   143	/-- The coordinate diagonal-line family is independent of the chosen affine
   144	parametrization, including the zero-direction convention. -/
   145	theorem directCoordinateDiagonalMeasurement_reparam
   146	    (D : DirectLdParams) (r : Fin D.k)
   147	    {iota : Type*} [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   148	    (M : DirectLdQuestion D →
   149	      MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement (DirectLdAnswer D) iota)
   150	    (hM : ∀ q, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (M q)) :
   151	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   152	    DiagonalMeasurementReparamInvariant D.toLDTParameters
   153	      (directCoordinateDiagonalMeasurement D r M hM) := by
   154	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   155	  classical
   156	  intro line t f
   157	  simp only [directCoordinateDiagonalMeasurement, ProjMeas.postprocess,
   158	    SubMeas.postprocess_outcome, matrixMeasurementToLDTProjMeas_outcome]
   159	  rw [directDiagonalQuestionOf_rebase]
   160	  have hfiber :
   161	      Finset.univ.filter (fun answer =>
   162	        directDiagonalAnswerReadout D r (line.rebaseAt t) answer =
   163	          DiagonalLinePolynomial.reparamAt f t) =
   164	        Finset.univ.filter (fun answer =>
   165	          directDiagonalAnswerReadout D r line answer = f) := by
   166	    ext answer
   167	    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
   168	    rw [directDiagonalAnswerReadout_rebase]
   169	    exact (DiagonalLinePolynomial.reparamAtEquiv t).injective.eq_iff

   172	private theorem strategy_carrier_nonempty {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) :
   173	    Nonempty (S.ιA × S.ιB) := by
   174	  by_contra h
   175	  rw [not_nonempty_iff] at h
   176	  letI := h
   177	  have hzero : S.ψ = 0 := Subsingleton.elim _ _
   178	  have hnorm := S.ψ_norm
   179	  rw [hzero, norm_zero] at hnorm
   180	  exact zero_ne_one hnorm

   182	/-- The pure LDT state represented by a game's unit strategy vector. -/

   184	    [Nonempty (S.ιA × S.ιB)] : PureState (S.ιA × S.ιB) where
   185	  vector := S.ψ
   186	  unit := by
   187	    rw [dotProduct_comm, ← EuclideanSpace.inner_eq_star_dotProduct,
   188	      inner_self_eq_norm_sq_to_K, S.ψ_norm]
   189	    norm_num

   205	/-- The complex Born amplitude of a vector and two local effects. -/
   206	private noncomputable def vectorBornAmplitude
   207	    {iotaA iotaB : Type*}
   208	    [Fintype iotaA] [DecidableEq iotaA]
   209	    [Fintype iotaB] [DecidableEq iotaB]
   210	    (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ (iotaA × iotaB))
   211	    (A : Op iotaA) (B : Op iotaB) : ℂ :=
   212	  inner ℂ psi (applyOperatorToState (heteroKron A B) psi)
   213	
   214	/-- The real Born quadratic form of a vector and two local effects. -/
   215	private noncomputable def vectorBornWeight
   216	    {iotaA iotaB : Type*}
   217	    [Fintype iotaA] [DecidableEq iotaA]
   218	    [Fintype iotaB] [DecidableEq iotaB]
   219	    (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ (iotaA × iotaB))
   220	    (A : Op iotaA) (B : Op iotaB) : ℝ :=
   221	  (vectorBornAmplitude psi A B).re
   222	
   223	private theorem vectorBornAmplitude_add_left
   224	    {iotaA iotaB : Type*}
   225	    [Fintype iotaA] [DecidableEq iotaA]
   226	    [Fintype iotaB] [DecidableEq iotaB]
   227	    (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ (iotaA × iotaB))
   228	    (A₁ A₂ : Op iotaA) (B : Op iotaB) :
   229	    vectorBornAmplitude psi (A₁ + A₂) B =
   230	      vectorBornAmplitude psi A₁ B + vectorBornAmplitude psi A₂ B := by
   231	  unfold vectorBornAmplitude applyOperatorToState heteroKron Matrix.kronecker
   232	  rw [Matrix.add_kronecker]
   233	  simp
   234	
   235	private theorem vectorBornAmplitude_add_right
   236	    {iotaA iotaB : Type*}
   237	    [Fintype iotaA] [DecidableEq iotaA]
   238	    [Fintype iotaB] [DecidableEq iotaB]
   239	    (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ (iotaA × iotaB))
   240	    (A : Op iotaA) (B₁ B₂ : Op iotaB) :
   241	    vectorBornAmplitude psi A (B₁ + B₂) =
   242	      vectorBornAmplitude psi A B₁ + vectorBornAmplitude psi A B₂ := by
   243	  unfold vectorBornAmplitude applyOperatorToState heteroKron Matrix.kronecker
   244	  rw [Matrix.kronecker_add]
   245	  simp
   246	
   247	private theorem vectorBornAmplitude_zero_left
   248	    {iotaA iotaB : Type*}
   249	    [Fintype iotaA] [DecidableEq iotaA]
   250	    [Fintype iotaB] [DecidableEq iotaB]
   251	    (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ (iotaA × iotaB)) (B : Op iotaB) :
   252	    vectorBornAmplitude psi 0 B = 0 := by
   253	  unfold vectorBornAmplitude applyOperatorToState heteroKron Matrix.kronecker
   254	  rw [Matrix.zero_kronecker]
   255	  simp

   257	private theorem vectorBornAmplitude_zero_right
   258	    {iotaA iotaB : Type*}
   259	    [Fintype iotaA] [DecidableEq iotaA]
   260	    [Fintype iotaB] [DecidableEq iotaB]
   261	    (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ (iotaA × iotaB)) (A : Op iotaA) :

   267	private theorem vectorBornWeight_add_left
   268	    {iotaA iotaB : Type*}
   269	    [Fintype iotaA] [DecidableEq iotaA]
   270	    [Fintype iotaB] [DecidableEq iotaB]
   271	    (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ (iotaA × iotaB))

   279	    {iotaA iotaB : Type*}
   280	    [Fintype iotaA] [DecidableEq iotaA]
   281	    [Fintype iotaB] [DecidableEq iotaB]
   282	    (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ (iotaA × iotaB))
   283	    (A : Op iotaA) (B₁ B₂ : Op iotaB) :
   284	    vectorBornWeight psi A (B₁ + B₂) =

   289	private theorem vectorBornWeight_finset_sum_left
   290	    {alpha iotaA iotaB : Type*}
   291	    [Fintype iotaA] [DecidableEq iotaA]
   292	    [Fintype iotaB] [DecidableEq iotaB]
   293	    (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ (iotaA × iotaB))
   294	    (s : Finset alpha) (A : alpha → Op iotaA) (B : Op iotaB) :
   295	    vectorBornWeight psi (∑ a ∈ s, A a) B =
   296	      ∑ a ∈ s, vectorBornWeight psi (A a) B := by
   297	  classical
   298	  induction s using Finset.induction_on with
   299	  | empty =>
   300	      simp [vectorBornWeight, vectorBornAmplitude_zero_left]
   301	  | @insert a s ha ih =>
   302	      rw [Finset.sum_insert ha, Finset.sum_insert ha,
   303	        vectorBornWeight_add_left, ih]
   304	
   305	private theorem vectorBornWeight_finset_sum_right
   306	    {beta iotaA iotaB : Type*}
   307	    [Fintype iotaA] [DecidableEq iotaA]
   308	    [Fintype iotaB] [DecidableEq iotaB]
   309	    (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ (iotaA × iotaB))
   310	    (A : Op iotaA) (s : Finset beta) (B : beta → Op iotaB) :
   311	    vectorBornWeight psi A (∑ b ∈ s, B b) =
   312	      ∑ b ∈ s, vectorBornWeight psi A (B b) := by
   313	  classical
   314	  induction s using Finset.induction_on with
   315	  | empty =>
   316	      simp [vectorBornWeight, vectorBornAmplitude_zero_right]
   317	  | @insert b s hb ih =>
   318	      rw [Finset.sum_insert hb, Finset.sum_insert hb,

    11	# The directly indexed low-degree game
    12	
    13	The low-degree game used by the Pauli-basis combining argument is needed in
    14	dimension `2 * m + 2`.  The existing conditionally linear game represents a
    15	coordinate index by an equally sized fiber in the scalar field and therefore
    16	requires the dimension to divide the field size.  This file gives the separate
    17	directly indexed variant which samples that index directly.
    18	
    19	The geometric line carrier records the sampled coordinate, and line evaluation
    20	uses an `Option` outcome rather than assigning a value when a point does not
    21	determine one.  The game retains the point, axis-line, and diagonal-line answer
    22	formats and the nine ordered type branches of the original low-degree game.
    23	
    24	The `Transport` modules relate the direct game to the seed-indexed game and to
    25	the low individual degree test: `Transport.Correspondence`
    26	identifies coordinates, answers, and the question law of the two QPBT
    27	presentations; `Transport.SeedFiber` dilates a seed-indexed strategy to a
    28	direct strategy by a correlated residue register, and `Transport.SeedFiberValue`
    29	shows that the dilation preserves the value exactly; `Transport.Questions`
    30	reads LDT lines as canonical direct questions and rebases direct answers;
    31	`Transport.Strategy` reads one coordinate of a projective direct strategy as an
    32	LDT projective strategy, with exact Born-weight formulas for both constructions;
    33	`Transport.Consistency` reexpresses the three single-polynomial LDT consistency
    34	relations in direct coordinates, the first two at a fixed tuple coordinate; and
    35	`Transport.BranchComparison`, `Transport.DiagonalRecursion`, and
    36	`Transport.PassConversion` convert a value bound of the direct game into the
    37	pass hypothesis of the low individual degree theorem for every
    38	coordinate strategy.  `GameValue` supplies the rejection calculus relating the
    39	direct value to the LDT branch weights.  `Transport.Error` carries the
    40	scalar half of the transport: the auxiliary sampling parameter with which
    41	the low individual degree theorem is applied, bounds on the three terms of its

\title{Documenting Possible Gaps, Counterexamples, and Formalization Deviations}
\author{}
\date{2026-04-29}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

\section{Purpose}

When a formalization relies on a cited mathematical source, the cited source
should remain intact.  It is a source, not an errata file.  If a possible gap,
missing hypothesis, incorrect numerical constant, or other mathematical
discrepancy is found, the matter should be recorded in a separate LaTeX note.
In this repository such notes live under \path{docs/paper-gaps/}.  The same
principle applies when the formal development has already diverged from the
cited source, for instance by changing a statement so that it compiles, or by
using a different mathematical route because an available formal-library theorem
has a slightly different form.  Such a note is a mathematical note first, and a
record of the formalization second: it should be readable by a mathematician or
mathematical physicist who has not followed the issue discussion.

The note should isolate the mathematical mechanism.  It should say what the
cited source asserts, what the cited results actually imply, where a term or
hypothesis is lost, and what statement the formal development proves instead.
If the formal proof takes a different route, the note should explain the
replacement argument and the hypotheses on which it rests.  This is especially
important when the proof uses a theorem, construction, or convention from
Mathlib which is not part of the cited argument.  In that case the note should
state the Mathlib result in ordinary mathematical language, explain how it is
specialized to the notation of the paper, and compare its hypotheses and
conclusion with the step it replaces.  It should not merely say that \Lean{} did
not accept a proof, that the modified proof compiles, or that a named library
lemma was applied.

The documents in this directory should themselves follow this standard.  A
policy or template which reads like a checklist will tend to produce checklist
notes; the examples and templates should therefore be written as mathematical
prose.

\section{Concision and Readability}

A paper-gap note should be short enough that a reader can understand the issue
in one sitting.  The first page should answer four questions: what the source
uses, how hard the remaining formal work is, what the formalization or audit
checked, and what the current verdict is.  Begin with a short
\emph{At a glance} section when the note concerns an open or recently resolved
formalization task.  That section should estimate the difficulty, the rough
implementation weight, the split between Mathlib reuse and project-local work,
and the key Mathlib APIs or modules.  Use honest ranges, not false precision.

The \emph{Key theorem forms} section should be Section~2, immediately after
\emph{At a glance}.  Put the theorem forms before the source details so the
reader knows what the formalization is aiming to prove.  After that, keep the
source assertion, the mechanism being checked, the blueprint/formal comparison,
and the conclusion.  Use more sections only when a counterexample or long
derivation genuinely needs room.

Keep background to the minimum needed for the local point.  Prefer one clear
special case over a general restatement of the surrounding theorem.  Use displayed
equations for the source assertion, the key calculation, and the theorem forms;
avoid displays for traceability data, declaration names, or long lists.  The
blueprint/formal comparison should be compact and should not repeat the theorem
forms.  The section ``Form of the Note'' below specifies where traceability data
belongs; the body should read as mathematical prose, not as a log.

If the verdict is that there is no mathematical discrepancy, say so plainly and
stop.  Keep the conclusion highly compact, normally under twenty source lines.
If the only remaining work is an implementation task, name it briefly and link
the issue or pull request in a footnote.

\section{When the Investigation Starts}

The investigation starts when the obstruction appears to be mathematical rather
than merely formal.  No final judgement is needed at this stage.  It is enough
that, after reading the relevant source and attempting the corresponding formal
statement, the proof seems to require a different scalar, an additional
hypothesis, a different tensor placement, a distinction between two objects which
the prose identifies, or an auxiliary assertion not supplied by the cited
argument.

The same investigation should also start when such a deviation is discovered
after the fact.  If the existing formal development or informal blueprint has
already changed the statement, strengthened a hypothesis, weakened a conclusion,
inserted an unadvertised lemma, or replaced the cited proof by a different
formal-library argument, the mathematical change should be documented even if all
relevant files already compile.

At this early stage the purpose is to preserve the question while it is still
local.  The note may later conclude that the matter is only notational, that an
intermediate estimate in the cited source needs a harmless correction, that a
missing hypothesis is genuinely needed, or that no discrepancy remains.  Thus
the trigger is not the severity of the eventual verdict, but the appearance of a
real mismatch between the cited reasoning and the statement that can be
formalized.

A failed tactic search, a missing formal lemma, or an inconvenient coercion is
not enough.  The obstruction must survive translation back into ordinary
mathematics.

Once a cited statement is established to be mathematically false, the repair
and escalation procedure is governed by Section~6 of
\path{local/protocols/issues-prs.md}.  Before asking the human owner to choose a
replacement, a dedicated mathematical-gap session must produce a correction
which is correct, sufficient for every paper and blueprint use, and minimal,
then iterate it against the Lean statement and its downstream consumers.  A
Claude Fable~5.1 session is currently launched by the owner session through its
Agent tool; a Codex main session requests that lane on progress log~\#27 rather
than dispatching a Codex worker.  Only after the astra poller reports
availability on owner inbox~\#26 does the Codex route become
\texttt{dispatch.sh --role mathfix} with astra.  A change to a mathematical
definition or game is escalated immediately; other repairs reach the owner
inbox only after the shared convergence budget expires.

Sometimes an investigation uncovers an improvement that is not a discrepancy:
the formalization works correctly, but it could be simplified by using an
existing library, replacing a custom type, or adopting a cleaner proof route.
These are not, by themselves, paper-gap notes.  They are action items.  When
such an improvement is identified, open a GitHub issue or pull request that
describes the proposed change.  If the investigation also produces a paper-gap
note, link the issue or pull request from that note: the note records the
mathematical justification, and the issue or pull request drives the
implementation.

\section{When to Write a Note}

A note should be written once the source argument and the formal proof no longer
match as mathematical arguments.  This includes, for instance, a numerical
estimate whose constant does not follow from the cited lemma, a displayed
conclusion which uses an unstated hypothesis, or a step in which two objects are
identified although they must remain distinct.  In analytic, algebraic,
probabilistic, or quantum arguments, such distinctions may concern the domain of
a map, the placement of a tensor factor, the type of an outcome, the distinction
between a structure and a substructure, or the scalar carried by an approximation
relation.

A note is required when an audit finds that a Lean declaration associated with a
source-labelled statement has acquired an extra non-source hypothesis, such as
bridge, residual, repair, producer, or obligation-structure data.  Such a
declaration is temporary proof debt, not a replacement for the source theorem,
and should not be introduced merely to avoid a \verb|sorry|.  The note must say
plainly that the Lean result is conditional, identify the source-faithful theorem
form that remains to be proved, and give the intended obligation discharger or
removal plan.  The blueprint should not mark the source-labelled statement with
\verb|\leanok| by pointing to this conditional helper.

Changing a Lean theorem away from the statement in
\path{references/ldt-paper/} is strongly discouraged.  A paper-gap note should
not make such a change look routine: it should explain the mathematical
necessity, or else classify the change as proof debt to be removed.

When an existing conditional helper is audited, the first task is to extract any
argument it already contains into source-faithful lemmas.  If the remaining
bridge hypothesis cannot be derived from the paper hypotheses, the formal
development should restore the source theorem statement and record the missing
proof obligation explicitly, rather than retaining the strengthened statement as
though it were the paper theorem.

This requirement is not meant to classify every explicit Lean side condition as
a discrepancy.  Positivity, nonemptiness, decidability, field-model instances,
and denominator nonvanishing hypotheses may be faithful encodings of the domain
in which the paper's theorem is stated.  The note should distinguish such
boundary hypotheses from hypotheses that supply an unproved step of the paper
argument.

A note is also appropriate when the proof becomes formal only after changing an
intermediate scalar, weakening a conclusion, strengthening a hypothesis, or
inserting an additional lemma which is not simply an expansion of the cited
argument.  These are mathematical changes, even when they are harmless for the
final theorem.  It is likewise appropriate when an available formal-library
theorem proves the needed result under a somewhat different formulation from the
cited source.  In that case the note should be deliberately pedagogical.  It
should explain, in ordinary mathematical language, what the replacement result
says, how it is specialized, which hypotheses are new or differently packaged,
and why the resulting statement is a legitimate substitute for the step in the
cited argument.  If the issue remains open after reasonable attempts, the note
should say what has been checked and what remains unknown.

\section{Counterexamples}

If the cited assertion appears to be false, the note should not stop at saying
that the proof cannot be formalized.  It should give the counterexample, or the
smallest relevant part of it, in ordinary mathematical notation.  The example
should be accompanied by enough verification that the reader can see both sides:
the hypotheses of the cited assertion hold, and its conclusion fails.

When feasible, the counterexample should also be formalized in \Lean{}.  This is
especially valuable when the example is finite, algebraic, computational, or
otherwise small enough that the failure can be checked without reproducing the
whole surrounding theory.  The note should then state the mathematical content
of the checked counterexample and identify the corresponding Lean declaration in
a footnote.  The Lean file is not a substitute for the prose: the prose should
still explain why the example refutes the cited assertion.

\section{Revision of a Note}

A paper-gap note may be provisional.  It may begin as soon as the mathematical
obstruction has been isolated well enough to state the question, and it may be
revised as the calculation, the blueprint, or the corresponding \Lean{}
declarations become clearer.  The first version need not know the final
classification, but it should say plainly which mathematical point is known and
which point remains unsettled.

Later revisions should not make the note into a chronological log.  They should
rewrite the document so that it remains a coherent account of the present
mathematical understanding.  If the verdict changes, the conclusion should state
the current verdict; the linked issue or pull request can preserve the earlier
discussion.

\section{Purpose}

This note fixes terminology for a recurring failure mode in the formalization
of the low individual degree test paper, \path{arXiv:2009.12982}.  It
complements the note-writing policy in \path{docs/paper-gaps/policy.tex} and
the source-statement audit tracked historically in \ghissue{1458}.  The current
source-boundary proof holes are tracked in \ghissue{1507} and \ghissue{422}.
A proof may be blocked at
an intermediate mathematical assertion.  If that assertion is added as a new
hypothesis to a theorem labelled as a paper theorem, the resulting \Lean{}
theorem
may be correct as a conditional statement, but it is no longer the theorem in
the cited source.  The apparent proof has not closed the paper theorem; it has
moved a proof obligation into the theorem statement.

The protocol below distinguishes such proof debt from legitimate formal
boundary conditions and from genuine mathematical corrections.  It is meant for
contributors and reviewers who must decide whether a bridge, residual, repair,
input, or obligation structure is a proved local construction, a tracked proof
gap, or statement drift which must be repaired before a theorem may be
advertised as a source theorem.  The default rule is restrictive: such data
must not be added to a paper-facing theorem unless it is part of the cited
source statement or a documented faithful encoding of its ambient hypotheses.

\section{Basic objects}

\paragraph{Source theorem.}
A source theorem is a theorem, lemma, proposition, or corollary in the paper
source under \path{references/ldt-paper/}.  Its hypotheses and conclusion are
the mathematical ground truth, subject only to faithful formal encoding and to
documented paper-gap corrections.

\paragraph{Paper-facing declaration.}
A \Lean{} declaration is paper-facing when it is named or cited as the
formalization of a source theorem, for instance through a blueprint
\verb|\lean{}| link on a theorem environment carrying a paper label.  Such a
declaration must match the source theorem in its public statement.  In
particular, it may not add an unproved bridge, residual, repair, input,
obligation structure, or other proof-obligation hypothesis which the paper does
not assume.

\paragraph{Proof obligation.}
A proof obligation is an intermediate assertion needed by the proof of a source
theorem.  It may be a construction, an estimate, a transport lemma, or a
comparison between two formal representations.  If the paper proves or invokes
this assertion, then the formalization should state it as a separate lemma or
theorem and prove it from the upstream hypotheses.

\paragraph{Obligation discharger.}
An obligation discharger is a theorem or definition which constructs a proof
obligation from the paper hypotheses already available at that point in the
argument.  This is the preferred representation of missing work.  If the proof
is not yet complete, the discharger may temporarily contain a tracked
\verb|sorry|, but the paper-facing theorem should call it rather than assume
its output as an additional theorem hypothesis.

\paragraph{Conditional helper.}
A conditional helper is a separately named theorem whose statement explicitly
assumes a proof obligation.  Names such as
\leanid{mainFormal\_ofInternalObligations},
\leanid{orthonormalization\_ofInput}, or names whose suffix advertises the
assumed obligation are permitted only when the declaration is not presented as
the source theorem.  A conditional helper is a quarantine for downstream proof
content; it does not close the source theorem.

\section{Bridge, residual, repair, input, and obligation structures}

The words \emph{bridge}, \emph{residual}, \emph{repair}, \emph{input}, and
\emph{obligation structure} name possible formal shapes.  They become dangerous
when their mathematical status is unclear or when their names make unproved
data look like acceptable hypotheses of a source theorem.

\paragraph{Bridge.}
A bridge should be a transport theorem between two already defined
mathematical forms: for example, a tensor-placement identity, a conversion
between two equivalent consistency relations, or a statement translating a
source object into a formal representation.  A bridge is harmless only after it
is proved from previously available assumptions.  It becomes proof debt when it
is assumed because the transport has not yet been proved.  It becomes theorem
drift when the assumed bridge is added to a paper-facing theorem.

\paragraph{Residual.}
A residual is a named remainder after part of an argument has been performed.
It is often a useful way to record the exact missing target after a completed
construction.  A residual may appear as the conclusion of a helper theorem or
as the input of a quarantined conditional helper.  It is not a permissible new
assumption on a paper theorem unless the paper itself assumes that residual.

\paragraph{Input.}
An input is a named bundle of data or hypotheses consumed by a construction or
conditional helper.  It is harmless only when each load-bearing field is either
part of the source hypotheses or is produced by an earlier theorem.  It becomes
proof debt when the bundle is merely assumed because the construction of its
fields is missing.  It becomes theorem drift when such a bundle is added to the
public statement of a source theorem.

\paragraph{Repair.}
A repair is a mathematical construction which replaces an approximate or
partial object by a better object, usually with a quantitative estimate.  In
the low individual degree test formalization, projectivization and
orthonormalization repairs are genuine mathematical operations.  A repair
should therefore appear as a construction or as a theorem discharging the
corresponding obligation.  If a theorem assumes the output of the repair instead
of constructing it, that theorem is conditional on the repair.

\paragraph{Obligation structure.}
An obligation structure is a record whose fields are the data and estimates
needed by a later construction.  This is acceptable only as an internal target
or as a hypothesis of a conditional helper.  Such a structure becomes statement
drift if it is added to a paper-facing theorem instead of being constructed
inside the proof.  The review question is whether every load-bearing field is
proved from the source hypotheses or is explicitly tracked as a missing
obligation.

\section{The main failure mode}

Suppose the paper proves
\[
  H \Longrightarrow C.
\]
During formalization, the proof may need an intermediate assertion \(B\).  The
paper theorem should be represented as
\[
  H \Longrightarrow B \Longrightarrow C
  \quad\text{inside the proof,}
\]
where \(B\) is obtained by a lemma or theorem from \(H\).  The following
public statement is a different theorem:
\[
  H \land B \Longrightarrow C.
\]
It is not unsound in \Lean{}, but it is not the paper theorem.  It says that the
conclusion follows if the missing bridge data is supplied.  Such a theorem is a
conditional helper, even if its conclusion looks exactly like the paper's
conclusion.

This is the situation colloquially described as ``adding a bridge
hypothesis''.  More precisely, an unproved intermediate step has been promoted
from the proof body to the theorem's assumptions.  The correction is not to hide
the hypothesis under a different structure name.  The correction is to keep a
paper-facing theorem with the source statement and move the missing step to a
named internal proof obligation.

\section{Faithful boundary hypotheses}

Not every extra formal hypothesis is a theorem drift.  Some hypotheses are
faithful boundary conditions introduced by formal encoding.  Examples include
nonnegativity needed for a real power, positivity needed to divide by a
quantity, finiteness and nonemptiness of an index type, a field-model instance,
or decidability instances required by \Lean{}.  Such hypotheses are acceptable
when they express part of the mathematical ambient setting or make explicit a
condition used implicitly in the paper.

The distinction is load-bearing.  A faithful boundary hypothesis describes the
domain in which the paper's objects live.  A proof-debt hypothesis supplies a
mathematical step that the proof should derive.  If removing the hypothesis
leaves an unproved construction or estimate from the paper proof, then the
hypothesis is proof debt, not a boundary condition.

\section{Definition drift and subtree repair}

Definition drift is especially dangerous because it propagates.  If a
definition is changed so that it no longer denotes the object in the paper,
then every downstream theorem using that definition may continue to compile
while proving statements about the wrong object.  Downstream theorem statements
can then be repaired piecemeal, but the development remains unstable because
the wrong definition is still upstream.

When a definition mismatch is found, the repair should proceed by a subtree
protocol.

\begin{enumerate}
  \item Identify the source object and the formal object precisely.
  \item Freeze a source-faithful definition or state an adapter theorem
  relating the existing definition to the source object.
  \item Recheck the downstream theorem chain against that definition or adapter.
  \item Re-formalize the affected subtree from the corrected interface, rather
  than adding local hypotheses to each downstream theorem.
  \item If a downstream proof cannot be completed, record the missing obligation
  at the lowest point where the paper proof needs it.
\end{enumerate}

This is slower than editing a final theorem signature, but it prevents a local
definition error from becoming a global theorem-statement error.

   264	  tuple $((u_0,s,v),(u,0,0))$ from the CL distribution $\mu_{L_\DLine,L_\Point}$,
   265	  and let $\line = \line(u_0,v)$ where $i = \chi(s)$.
   266	  Then $u$ is a uniformly random point in $\F_q^m$ and $\line$ is a random
   267	  diagonal line that goes through $u$ and shares the first $i-1$ coordinates
   268	  with $u$, for uniformly random $i$.
   269	\end{lemma}
   270	\begin{proof}
   271		The proof of this follows identically to \Cref{lem:alnf}.
   272	\end{proof}
   273	
   274	For later convenience we make the following definition. 
   275	
   276	\begin{definition}[Line-point distributions]
   277	        \label{def:line-point-dist}
   278	 The \emph{axis line-point distribution} $D_{\ALine}$ is the
   279	 distribution $\mu_{L_\ALine,L_\Point}$ over pairs $(\ell=(u_0,e_i),u)$
   280	 (we omit the $0$ elements for simplicity). The \emph{diagonal
   281	   line-point distribution} $D_{\DLine}$ is the distribution
   282	 $\mu_{L_\DLine,L_\Point}$  over $(\ell=(u_0,s,v),u)$. The
   283	 \emph{line-point distribution} $D_{\Line}$ is the equal mixture of the axis-parallel line-point distribution and the diagonal line-point distribution.
   284	 In other words, a sample from $D_{\Line}$ is distributed as follows:
   285	 with probability $\tfrac{1}{2}$, output a sample from $D_{\ALine}$,
   286	 and with probability $\tfrac{1}{2}$, output a sample from $D_{\DLine}$.
   287	\end{definition}

   320	\paragraph{Decision procedure} The decision procedure $\decider^\ld$ for the
   321	game $\game^\ld$ is presented in Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider}.
   322	The table at the top specifies a parsing scheme for the questions and answers,
   323	depending on the type of question.
   324	For example, when a player receives a question with type $\Point$, the question
   325	content $x$, a bit string of length $m \log q$, should be interpreted by the
   326	decision procedure and the players as an element of the vector space $\F_q^m$,
   327	as indicated in Section~\ref{sec:ff-representations}.
   328	Similarly the answer to a question with type $\Point$ is expected to be a bit
   329	string of length $\ldc \log q$, and is interpreted as an element of $\F_q^\ldc$.
   330	For questions with type $\ALine$, the question content is a $(m \log q + \log
   331	q)$-bit string, which is parsed as a pair $(u_0, s) \in \F_q^m \times \F_q$,
   332	which in turn can be interpreted as a specification for an axis-parallel line
   333	$\line(u_0,e_i)$ in $\F_q^m$ where $i = \chi(s)$, as described in
   334	\Cref{lem:alnf}.
   335	The answer is interpreted as the description of $\ldc$ degree-$d$ univariate
   336	polynomials defined on the line $\line(u_0,e_i)$, each polynomial given by a
   337	list of $d+1$ coefficients.
   338	For questions with type $\DLine$, the question content is a $(2m \log q + \log
   339	q)$-bit string, which is parsed as a triple $(u_0, s, v) \in \F_q^m \times \F_q
   340	\times \F_q^m$ that specifies a diagonal line $\line(u_0,v')$ where $v' =
   341	\pi_{i-1}(v)$ as described in \Cref{lem:dlnf}.
   342	The answer is interpreted as the description of $\ldc$ degree-$md$ univariate
   343	polynomials defined on the line $\line(u_0,v')$.
   344	If the answers returned by the players do not fit this format the decision
   345	procedure rejects.
   346

   394	We define a special class of measurements that are relevant to the soundness
   395	properties of the low-degree test.
   396	
   397	\begin{definition}[Low-degree polynomial measurements]
   398	  \label{def:ld-meas}
   399	  Define $\polymeas{m}{d}{q}$ to be the set of POVM measurements whose outcomes
   400	  correspond to (individual) degree-$d$ polynomials of $m$ variables over
   401	  $\F_q$.
   402	  More generally, for an integer $\ldc$ and tuples $m=(m_1, m_2, \ldots,
   403	  m_\ldc)$, $d=(d_1, d_2, \ldots, d_\ldc)$ and $q=(q_1, q_2, \ldots, q_\ldc)$,
   404	  we let $\simulpolymeas{m}{d}{q}{\ldc}$ be the set of measurements $G =
   405	  \{G_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots\,,\, g_\ldc}\}$ such that for $i\in\{1, 2, \ldots,
   406	  \ldc\}$, $g_i$ is a polynomial $g_i:\F_{q_i}^{m_i} \rightarrow
   407	  \F_{q_i}$ with individual degree $d_i$ (see \Cref{sec:ld-encoding} for a definition of individual degree). 
   408	\end{definition}
   409	
   410	Quantum soundness of a version of the classical low-degree test for polynomials of low \emph{total} degree was claimed
   411	in~\cite{natarajan2018low}, building on an analysis of a three-prover version of the test in~\cite{vidick2016three}. Unfortunately there is a gap in the soundness analysis of this test. For our construction we use the low individual degree test, whose quantum soundness is shown in~\cite{ML20} and generalized in~\cite{ji2021quantum}. We state the result in the form that is most directly useful for us, and show how the stated result follows from~\cite{ji2021quantum}.
   412	
   413	\begin{theorem}[Quantum soundness of the simultaneous classical low-degree test]
   414	  \label{lem:ld-soundness}
   415	  There exists a function $\delta_{\ld}(\eps, q, m, d, \ldc) = a (dm \ldc)^a (\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$ for universal constants $a\geq 1$ and $0<b\leq 1$ 
   416	such that the following
   417	  holds.
   418	  For all $\eps > 0$ and parameter tuple $\ldparams = (q, m, d, \ldc)$, for all
   419	  projective strategies $(\psi,A,B)$ that succeed with probability at least
   420	  $1-\eps$ in the game $\game^\ld_\ldparams$, there exists measurements
   421	  \[G^w \in \simulpolymeas{m}{d}{q}{\ldc}\] on $\mH_w$, for
   422	  $w\in\{\alice,\bob\}$, such that
   423	  \begin{equation*}
   424	    \begin{split}
   425	      A^{\Point,\, u}_{a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots\,,\, a_\ldc}
   426	      & \abc[\delta_{\ld}]
   427	      G^\bob_{[(g_1(u),g_2(u),\ldots,g_\ldc(u)) = (a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots \,,\, a_\ldc)]}\;,\\
   428	      G^\alice_{[(g_1(u),g_2(u),\ldots,g_\ldc(u)) = (a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots \,,\, a_\ldc)]}
   429	      & \abc[\delta_{\ld}]
   430				 B^{\Point,\, u}_{a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots\,,\, a_\ldc}\;,\\
   431	      G^\alice_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots \,,\, g_\ldc}
   432	      & \abc[\delta_{\ld}]
   433	      G^\bob_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots \,,\, g_\ldc}\;,
   434	    \end{split}
   435	  \end{equation*}
   436	  where $\delta_{\ld} = \delta_{\ld}(\eps, q, m, d, \ldc)$, 
   437	  and all three statements are with respect to the state $\ket{\psi}$.
   438	In addition, the first two approximations hold under the uniform distribution over $u\in \F_q^m$,
   439		whereas there is no question distribution associated with the third approximation.
   440	\end{theorem}
   441	
   442	\begin{proof}
   443	Let $\ldparams = (q, m, d, \ldc)$
   444	where $m, d, \ldc \in \N$ are integers, $q \in \N$ is an admissible field size,
   445	and $m$ divides $q$. Let $\Sigma=\F_q$. Let $\code \subseteq \Sigma^q$ be the Reed-Solomon code with degree $d$. Explicitly, $\code$ is the set of all $(p(x_1),\ldots,p(x_n))$ where $p:\F_q\to\F_q$ is a univariate polynomial of degree at most $d$ and $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ are an enumeration of $\F_q$. Then in the (standard) notation from~\cite{ji2021quantum} $\code$ is a linear $[q,d+1,n-d+1]_\Sigma$ code.
   446	
   447	Observe that the two-prover tensor code test, for the code $\code^{\otimes m}$, as described in~\cite[Figure 1 and Figure 2]{ji2021quantum}, is identical to the game $\game^\ld$ with parameters $\ldparams$ and $\ldc=1$, whose decider is presented in Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider}. This is because 
   448	\begin{enumerate}
   449	\item The \emph{axis-parallel line-versus-point test} from Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} is identical to the \emph{axis-parallel lines test} from~\cite[Figure 1]{ji2021quantum}, with the only difference that in Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} the roles of A and B are chosen uniformly at random. This is consistent with the two-prover variant of the tensor code test from~\cite[Section 4.1]{ji2021quantum}.
   450	\item The \emph{diagonal line-versus-point test} from Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} is identical to the \emph{subcube commutation test} from~\cite[Figure 1]{ji2021quantum}, with again the added symmetrization between players. 
   451	\item The \emph{consistency test} from Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} is identical to the \emph{synchronicity test} from~\cite[Figure 2]{ji2021quantum}.
   452	\end{enumerate}
   453	
   454	As a result,~\cite[Theorem 4.7]{ji2021quantum}, in which we choose the parameter $k$ as $k=m^3d$,  immediately yields \Cref{lem:ld-soundness}.
   455	
   456	To conclude it remains to extend the result to the case of general $\ldc$. This is done 
   457	via a standard reduction, following exactly the same steps as the derivation of Theorem 4.43 from Theorem 4.40 in~\cite{NW19}.
   458	\end{proof}

   473	tuple $\ldparams$ as input.

    27	open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder

    33	/-! ### Two-space source route -/
    34	
    35	/--
    36	Trivial saturated-error branch for the printed two-space theorem
    37	`thm:main-formal`.
    38	
    39	Paper origin: `references/ldt-paper/test_definition.tex:180-202`.
    40	
    41	**Source:** This is a source-faithful saturated-error branch: when the printed
    42	target error is at least `1`, the consistency conclusion follows from the
    43	normalization bound for bipartite consistency defects, without adding any
    44	construction hypothesis to the source theorem.
    45	
    46	Whenever `mainFormalError params k eps ≥ 1`, the three consistency conclusions
    47	hold for arbitrary projective polynomial measurements, since each underlying
    48	consistency defect is bounded by `1` for a normalized bipartite state and a

    51	theorem mainFormal_trivial_witness
    52	    (params : Parameters)
    53	    [FieldModel params.q]
    54	    {ιA ιB : Type*}
    55	    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA]
    56	    [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
    57	    (strategy : ProjStrat params ιA ιB)
    58	    (eps : Error)
    59	    (k : ℕ)
    60	    (herr : 1 ≤ mainFormalError params k eps) :
    61	    ∃ G_A : ProjMeas (Polynomial params) ιA,
    62	      ∃ G_B : ProjMeas (Polynomial params) ιB,
    63	        ConsRel strategy.state (uniformDistribution (Point params))
    64	            (IdxProjMeas.toIdxSubMeas strategy.pointMeasurementA)
    65	            (polynomialEvaluationFamily params G_B.toSubMeas)

    72	            (constSubMeasFamily G_A.toSubMeas)
    73	            (constSubMeasFamily G_B.toSubMeas)
    74	            (mainFormalError params k eps) := by
    75	  classical
    76	  haveI : Inhabited (Polynomial params) :=
    77	    ⟨⟨0, by intro i; simp [MvPolynomial.degreeOf_zero]⟩⟩

    81	    ProjMeas.trivialDistinguishedOutcome (default : Polynomial params)

    84	    (bipartiteConsError_uniform_le_one strategy.state strategy.isNormalized _ _) herr⟩
    85	
    86	/-- Source role-register conclusion after the scalar branch has supplied
    87	`0 < k`.

    92	`ProjStrat.sourceRoleRegisterFinalPointConsistency` and then weakens the three
    93	explicit pre-absorption errors to `mainFormalError` by the existing Step 8

    95	theorem mainFormalConclusion_ofRoleRegisterScalarBoundary
    96	    (params : Parameters)
    97	    [FieldModel params.q]
    98	    {ιA ιB : Type*}
    99	    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA]
   100	    [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
   101	    (strategy : ProjStrat params ιA ιB)
   102	    (eps : Error)
   103	    (hpass : strategy.PassesLowIndividualDegreeTest eps)
   104	    (k : ℕ)
   105	    (hk : 400 * params.m * params.d ≤ k)
   106	    (hk0 : 0 < k)
   107	    (hsmall : ¬ 1 ≤ mainFormalError params k eps) :

   109	      ∃ G_B : ProjMeas (Polynomial params) ιB,
   110	        ConsRel strategy.state (uniformDistribution (Point params))
   111	            (IdxProjMeas.toIdxSubMeas strategy.pointMeasurementA)
   112	            (polynomialEvaluationFamily params G_B.toSubMeas)
   113	            (mainFormalError params k eps) ∧
   114	          ConsRel strategy.state (uniformDistribution (Point params))
   115	            (polynomialEvaluationFamily params G_A.toSubMeas)
   116	            (IdxProjMeas.toIdxSubMeas strategy.pointMeasurementB)
   117	            (mainFormalError params k eps) ∧
   118	          ConsRel strategy.state (uniformDistribution Unit)
   119	            (constSubMeasFamily G_A.toSubMeas)
   120	            (constSubMeasFamily G_B.toSubMeas)
   121	            (mainFormalError params k eps) := by
   122	  classical
   123	  have hepsNN : 0 ≤ eps := ProjStrat.eps_nonneg_of_passes hpass
   124	  let scalars : MainFormalScalarBounds params eps k :=
   125	    MainFormalScalarBounds.ofNontrivialMainFormal hepsNN hk0 hsmall
   126	  let σsrc : Error :=
   127	    2 * MainInductionStep.mainInductionError params k (3 * eps) (3 * eps) (3 * eps)

   129	    σsrc + 2 * Real.sqrt (3 * eps + σsrc) + (params.m * params.d : Error) / params.q
   130	  let ζ₂src : Error := MakingMeasurementsProjective.orthonormalizeAndCompleteError ζ₁src

   132	    ζ₁src + Real.sqrt (MakingMeasurementsProjective.orthonormalizationError ζ₁src)

   137	    simp [ζ₁src, σsrc, MainFormalScalarBounds.zeta1, cascadeZeta1,
   138	      MainFormalScalarBounds.sigma, mainFormalScalarSigma_eq_mainInductionError]
   139	  have hζ₂src : ζ₂src ≤ scalars.zeta2 := by
   140	    change MakingMeasurementsProjective.orthonormalizeAndCompleteError ζ₁src ≤ scalars.zeta2

   142	    exact MainFormalScalarBounds.orthonormalizeAndCompleteError_zeta1_le_zeta2

   144	  have hηsrc : ηsrc = scalars.line169Error := by
   145	    have hζ0 : 0 ≤ scalars.zeta1 := MainFormalScalarBounds.zeta1_nonneg scalars
   146	    have hsqrt :
   147	        Real.sqrt (MakingMeasurementsProjective.orthonormalizationError scalars.zeta1) =
   148	          10 * Real.rpow scalars.zeta1 (1 / (8 : Error)) :=
   149	      MakingMeasurementsProjective.sqrt_orthonormalizationError_eq hζ0
   150	    simp [ηsrc, hζ₁src, MainFormalScalarBounds.line169Error,
   151	      cascadeLine169RepairError, hsqrt]
   152	  have hζ₃src : ζ₃src ≤ scalars.zeta3 := by
   153	    have hζ₁le : ζ₁src ≤ scalars.zeta1 := le_of_eq hζ₁src
   154	    have hcore : 6 * ζ₁src + 6 * ζ₂src ≤ 6 * scalars.zeta1 + 6 * scalars.zeta2 := by

   156	    simpa [ζ₃src, MainFormalScalarBounds.zeta3, cascadeZeta3] using hcore

   159	    have hrad :
   160	        ηsrc + ζ₃src / 2 ≤ scalars.line169Error + scalars.zeta3 / 2 := by
   161	      have hηle : ηsrc ≤ scalars.line169Error := le_of_eq hηsrc
   162	      nlinarith
   163	    have hsqrt :
   164	        Real.sqrt (ηsrc + ζ₃src / 2) ≤
   165	          Real.sqrt (scalars.line169Error + scalars.zeta3 / 2) :=
   166	      Real.sqrt_le_sqrt hrad
   167	    have hrepaired :
   168	        σsrc + 2 * Real.sqrt (ηsrc + ζ₃src / 2) ≤ scalars.zeta4Repaired := by
   169	      calc
   170	        σsrc + 2 * Real.sqrt (ηsrc + ζ₃src / 2)
   171	            = 2 * scalars.sigma + 2 * Real.sqrt (ηsrc + ζ₃src / 2) := by
   172	              rw [hσsrc]
   173	        _ ≤ 2 * scalars.sigma + 2 *
   174	              Real.sqrt (scalars.line169Error + scalars.zeta3 / 2) := by
   175	            nlinarith
   176	        _ = scalars.zeta4Repaired := by
   177	            rfl
   178	    exact hrepaired.trans (MainFormalScalarBounds.zeta4Repaired_le_mainFormalError scalars)
   179	  have hsourceSelf :
   180	      ζ₃src / 2 ≤ mainFormalError params k eps := by
   181	    have htoCascade : ζ₃src / 2 ≤ scalars.zeta3 / 2 := by
   182	      nlinarith
   183	    exact htoCascade.trans (MainFormalScalarBounds.zeta3_div_two_le_mainFormalError scalars)

   187	  rcases hrest with ⟨_hQQEval, hQQ⟩

   190	      simpa [σsrc, ζ₁src, ζ₂src, ηsrc, ζ₃src] using hsourcePoint) hA
   191	  · exact ConsRel.mono (by
   192	      simpa [σsrc, ζ₁src, ζ₂src, ηsrc, ζ₃src] using hsourcePoint) hB
   193	  · exact ConsRel.mono (by
   194	      simpa [σsrc, ζ₁src, ζ₂src, ηsrc, ζ₃src] using hsourceSelf) hQQ
   195	
   196	/--
   197	Small-error branch for the corrected two-space theorem
   198	`thm:main-formal`.
   199	
   200	Paper origin: `references/ldt-paper/test_definition.tex:180-202`.
   201

   215	theorem mainFormal_smallErrorConclusion

     5	
     6	This module identifies the low individual degree polynomial outcomes with the
     7	bounded polynomial representatives used by the directly indexed QPBT game.  It
     8	also transports complete measurements and their evaluation postprocessings
     9	without changing either coordinate order or consistency error.
    10	
    11	## References
    12	
    13	- `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:393-458`
    14	- `references/ldt-paper/test_definition.tex:180-202`

    17	
    18	open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder

    20	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

    22	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    23	open MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries
    24	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    25	
    26	noncomputable section
    27	
    28	/-! ## Polynomial outcomes -/
    29	
    30	private theorem directPolynomialRename_degreeOf_le
    31	    (D : DirectLdParams) (p : MvPolynomial (Fin D.m) (DirectScalarQ D))
    32	    (hp : ∀ i, MvPolynomial.degreeOf i p ≤ D.d) (i : Fin D.m) :
    33	    MvPolynomial.degreeOf i (MvPolynomial.rename Fin.rev p) ≤ D.d := by
    34	  rw [← Fin.rev_rev i,
    35	    MvPolynomial.degreeOf_rename_of_injective Fin.rev_injective]
    36	  exact hp (Fin.rev i)
    37	
    38	private theorem ldtPolynomial_ext
    39	    {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
    40	    {g h : MIPStarRE.LDT.Polynomial params} (hpoly : g.poly = h.poly) : g = h := by
    41	  cases g with
    42	  | mk gp hg =>
    43	      cases h with
    44	      | mk hp hh =>
    45	          simp only at hpoly
    46	          subst hp
    47	          rfl
    48	
    49	/-- Bounded QPBT polynomial representatives are equivalent to LDT
    50	polynomial outcomes.  The variable renaming is the same coordinate reversal
    51	as `directPointEquiv`, so evaluation retains the direct coordinate order. -/
    52	noncomputable def directPolyEquivPolynomial (D : DirectLdParams) :
    53	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
    54	    PolyIndex D.m (DirectScalarQ D) D.d ≃
    55	      MIPStarRE.LDT.Polynomial D.toLDTParameters := by
    56	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
    57	  refine
    58	    { toFun := fun g =>
    59	        { poly := MvPolynomial.rename Fin.rev g.1
    60	          lowIndividualDegree := directPolynomialRename_degreeOf_le D g.1
    61	            (degreeOf_le_of_mem_polyFunc g.2) }
    62	      invFun := fun g =>
    63	        ⟨MvPolynomial.rename Fin.rev g.poly, ?_⟩
    64	      left_inv := ?_
    65	      right_inv := ?_ }

   248	`thm:main-formal`.
   249	
   250	Paper origin: `references/ldt-paper/test_definition.tex:180-202`.

   252	This theorem closes the saturated-error branch of the source-boundary

   255	small-error branch `mainFormal_smallErrorConclusion`.  This reduction
   256	is not an additional hypothesis of `thm:main-formal`.

   259	    (params : Parameters)
   260	    [FieldModel params.q]
   261	    {ιA ιB : Type*}
   262	    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA]
   263	    [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
   264	    (strategy : ProjStrat params ιA ιB)

   275	            (mainFormalError params k eps) ∧

   277	            (polynomialEvaluationFamily params G_A.toSubMeas)
   278	            (IdxProjMeas.toIdxSubMeas strategy.pointMeasurementB)

   282	            (constSubMeasFamily G_B.toSubMeas)

     7	# The scalar error of the low-degree soundness transport
     8	
     9	This module supplies the scalar half of the soundness transport for the
    10	directly indexed low-degree game.  Its content is purely arithmetic: the
    11	auxiliary sampling parameter with which the mature low individual degree
    12	theorem is applied to a coordinate strategy, the resulting bounds on the three
    13	terms of the mature error `mainFormalError`, and the absorption of the
    14	simultaneous-measurement estimate into the error function `deltaLd` of
    15	`lem:ld-soundness`.
    16	
    17	## Main definitions
    18	
    19	* `directLdAuxParameter D = 2560000 m³ d` is the sampling parameter handed to
    20	  `MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.mainFormal`.  It is the multiple of the exponential scale
    21	  `2560000 m²` of `mainFormalError` with quotient `m d`, so that the
    22	  exponential term of the mature error is exactly `exp (-m d)`.
    23	
    24	## Main results
    25	
    26	* `directLdAuxParameter_pos` and `four_hundred_mul_le_directLdAuxParameter` are
    27	  the two hypotheses `0 < k` and `400 m d ≤ k` of `mainFormal`, proved from the
    28	  positivity of the dimension and of the degree alone.
    29	* `directLd_test_term_le`, `directLd_field_term_le` and
    30	  `directLd_exponential_term_le` bound the three terms of
    31	  `mainFormalError D.toLDTParameters (directLdAuxParameter D) (3 ε)`: the test
    32	  term by `3 ε^(1/40000)`, the field term by `d q^(-1/40000)`, and the
    33	  exponential term by `2^(-b m d)` for every `0 ≤ b ≤ 1`.
    34	* `exists_directLdTransportConstants` exhibits, for a sandwich constant
    35	  `C₀ ≥ 1`, the explicit universal constants `a = 2500000000 C₀` and
    36	  `b = 1/80000` for which `C₀ k √(mainFormalError + m d / q + ε)` is at most
    37	  `deltaLd a b ε q m d k` in the regime `0 < ε ≤ 1`.
    38	* `one_le_deltaLd_of_one_le_error` and
    39	  `one_le_deltaLd_of_fieldSize_le_degree` bound `deltaLd` below by one in the

    41	  `consistencyDefect_heteroKron_le_one` bounds every bipartite consistency
    42	  defect on a unit state above by one.  Together they close both degenerate

    41	private theorem sum_ldType (f : LdType → ℝ) :
    42	    ∑ t : LdType, f t = f .point + f .aline + f .dline := by
    43	  change (Finset.univ : Finset LdType).sum f = _
    44	  rw [show (Finset.univ : Finset LdType) = {.point, .aline, .dline} by decide]
    45	  simp [add_assoc]

    47	/-- The uniformly weighted rejection is one ninth of the sum over the nine
    48	ordered type pairs. -/
    49	private theorem directLdRejectionProbability_eq_sum (D : DirectLdParams)
    50	    (S : Strategy (directLdGame D)) :
    51	    directLdRejectionProbability D S =
    52	      (∑ types : LdType × LdType, directLdBranchRejectionProbability D S types) / 9 := by
    53	  unfold directLdRejectionProbability
    54	  rw [avgOver_uniform_eq_inv_card_mul_sum, Fintype.card_prod,
    55	    show Fintype.card LdType = 3 by decide, div_eq_inv_mul]
    56	  norm_num
    57	
    58	/-- Failure of the coordinate strategy compared with the mature-weighted
    59	rejection of the direct game.  The point and axis-line branches are dominated
    60	termwise, while each diagonal branch is dominated up to the factor two of the
    61	leading-index rereading; the surplus is the extra half weight of the diagonal
    62	branches.  The bare inequality against `directLdLdtWeightedFailureProbability`
    63	fails for index-sensitive strategies that answer the canonical question of
    64	a direction badly and the non-canonical questions of the same geometric line
    65	well, so the surplus term is not an artifact of the proof. -/
    66	theorem directCoordinate_failure_le_weightedFailure
    67	    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
    68	    (hS : S.IsProjective) (r : Fin D.k) :
    69	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
    70	    (directCoordinateProjStrat D S hS r).lowIndividualDegreeFailureProbability ≤
    71	      directLdLdtWeightedFailureProbability D S +
    72	        (directLdBranchRejectionProbability D S (.dline, .point) +
    73	          directLdBranchRejectionProbability D S (.point, .dline)) / 6 := by
    74	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
    75	  rw [ProjStrat.lowIndividualDegreeFailureProbability_eq_role_averages]
    76	  unfold ProjStrat.axisParallelRoleAverage ProjStrat.diagonalRoleAverage
    77	    directLdLdtWeightedFailureProbability
    78	  dsimp only
    79	  have h1 := directCoordinate_axis_line_point_le D S hS r
    80	  have h2 := directCoordinate_axis_point_line_le D S hS r
    81	  have h3 := directCoordinate_point_agreement_le D S hS r
    82	  have h4 := directCoordinate_diagonal_line_point_le D S hS r
    83	  have h5 := directCoordinate_diagonal_point_line_le D S hS r
    84	  linarith

    86	/-- Failure of the coordinate strategy is at most three times the uniformly
    87	weighted rejection of the direct game. -/
    88	theorem directCoordinate_failure_le_three_mul_rejection
    89	    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
    90	    (hS : S.IsProjective) (r : Fin D.k) :
    91	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
    92	    (directCoordinateProjStrat D S hS r).lowIndividualDegreeFailureProbability ≤
    93	      3 * directLdRejectionProbability D S := by
    94	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
    95	  have h := directCoordinate_failure_le_weightedFailure D S hS r
    96	  unfold directLdLdtWeightedFailureProbability at h
    97	  dsimp only at h
    98	  rw [directLdRejectionProbability_eq_sum, Fintype.sum_prod_type]
    99	  simp only [sum_ldType]
   100	  have hnonneg := directLdBranchRejectionProbability_nonneg D S
   101	  have hpp := hnonneg (.point, .point)
   102	  have hpa := hnonneg (.point, .aline)
   103	  have hpd := hnonneg (.point, .dline)
   104	  have hap := hnonneg (.aline, .point)
   105	  have haa := hnonneg (.aline, .aline)
   106	  have had := hnonneg (.aline, .dline)
   107	  have hdp := hnonneg (.dline, .point)
   108	  have hda := hnonneg (.dline, .aline)
   109	  have hdd := hnonneg (.dline, .dline)
   110	  linarith

   112	/-- The error passed to the mature theorem is nonnegative: the direct value
   113	never exceeds one. -/
   114	theorem directLd_error_nonneg_of_value (D : DirectLdParams)
   115	    (S : Strategy (directLdGame D)) (ε : ℝ) (hwin : 1 - ε ≤ S.value) :
   116	    0 ≤ ε := by
   117	  have h0 : 0 ≤ directLdRejectionProbability D S :=
   118	    avgOver_nonneg _ _ fun types => directLdBranchRejectionProbability_nonneg D S types
   119	  rw [directLdRejectionProbability_eq_one_sub_value] at h0
   120	  linarith

   122	/-- The error `3 * ε` passed to the mature theorem is nonnegative. -/
   123	theorem directCoordinate_three_mul_error_nonneg (D : DirectLdParams)
   124	    (S : Strategy (directLdGame D)) (ε : ℝ) (hwin : 1 - ε ≤ S.value) :
   125	    0 ≤ 3 * ε := by
   126	  have := directLd_error_nonneg_of_value D S ε hwin
   127	  linarith

   129	/-- A direct strategy of value at least `1 - ε` has coordinate strategies of
   130	low individual degree failure at most `3 * ε`. -/
   131	theorem directCoordinate_failure_le_three_mul_error
   132	    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
   133	    (hS : S.IsProjective) (r : Fin D.k) (ε : ℝ) (hwin : 1 - ε ≤ S.value) :
   134	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   135	    (directCoordinateProjStrat D S hS r).lowIndividualDegreeFailureProbability ≤
   136	      3 * ε := by
   137	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   138	  have hrej : directLdRejectionProbability D S ≤ ε := by
   139	    rw [directLdRejectionProbability_eq_one_sub_value]
   140	    linarith
   141	  calc
   142	    (directCoordinateProjStrat D S hS r).lowIndividualDegreeFailureProbability ≤
   143	        3 * directLdRejectionProbability D S :=
   144	      directCoordinate_failure_le_three_mul_rejection D S hS r
   145	    _ ≤ 3 * ε := by linarith

   147	/-- The pass hypothesis of the mature low individual degree theorem for every
   148	coordinate of a direct strategy of value at least `1 - ε`, with error
   149	`3 * ε` and no further assumption. -/
   150	theorem directCoordinate_passes
   151	    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
   152	    (hS : S.IsProjective) (r : Fin D.k) (ε : ℝ) (hwin : 1 - ε ≤ S.value) :
   153	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   154	    (directCoordinateProjStrat D S hS r).PassesLowIndividualDegreeTest (3 * ε) := by
   155	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   156	  exact ⟨directCoordinate_failure_le_three_mul_error D S hS r ε hwin⟩

   132	/-- The directly indexed axis-line versus point acceptance relation. -/
   133	def directAlinePointCondition (D : DirectLdParams)
   134	    (line point : DirectLdSpace D)
   135	    (f : Fin D.k → Fin (D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)
   136	    (a : Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D) : Prop :=
   137	  ∀ t : DirectScalarQ D,
   138	    point.point = line.point + t • coordinateDirection line.index →
   139	      ∀ j : Fin D.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j

   141	/-- The directly indexed diagonal-line versus point acceptance relation. -/
   142	def directDlinePointCondition (D : DirectLdParams)
   143	    (line point : DirectLdSpace D)
   144	    (f : Fin D.k → Fin (D.m * D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)
   145	    (a : Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D) : Prop :=
   146	  ∀ t : DirectScalarQ D,
   147	    point.point = line.point + t • line.direction →
   148	      ∀ j : Fin D.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j

   150	/-- The directly indexed low-degree win predicate.  It differs from
   151	`ldWinPredicate` only by reading the coordinate index directly from each line
   152	question. -/
   153	noncomputable def directLdWinPredicate (D : DirectLdParams) :
   154	    DirectLdQuestion D → DirectLdQuestion D →
   155	      DirectLdAnswer D → DirectLdAnswer D → Bool :=
   156	  open Classical in
   157	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   158	    if validDirectLdAnswer tA a && validDirectLdAnswer tB b then
   159	      match tA, tB, a, b with
   160	      | .point, .point, .pointVals u, .pointVals v => decide (u = v)
   161	      | .aline, .point, .alinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   162	          decide (directAlinePointCondition D xA xB f u)
   163	      | .point, .aline, .pointVals u, .alinePolys f =>
   164	          decide (directAlinePointCondition D xB xA f u)
   165	      | .dline, .point, .dlinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   166	          decide (directDlinePointCondition D xA xB f u)
   167	      | .point, .dline, .pointVals u, .dlinePolys f =>
   168	          decide (directDlinePointCondition D xB xA f u)
   169	      | .aline, .aline, .alinePolys f, .alinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   170	      | .dline, .dline, .dlinePolys f, .dlinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   171	      | _, _, _, _ => true
   172	    else false

   181	  AnswerB := DirectLdAnswer D
   182	  μ := directLdQuestionDistribution D
   183	  μ_prob := directLdQuestionDistribution_isProbability D
   184	  decide := directLdWinPredicate D

    19	/-- The off-diagonal defect in `def:consistency`, blueprint
    20	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:195-208`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:232-248`. -/
    21	noncomputable def consistencyDefect {X α ι : Type*}
    22	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    23	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    24	    (μ : Distribution X) (A B : X → α → Op ι)
    25	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
    26	  avgOver μ (fun x =>
    27	    ∑ a : α, ∑ b : α,
    28	      if a = b then 0 else
    29	        (inner ℂ ψ ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ).symm
    30	          ((A x a * B x b).mulVec ψ))).re)

    32	/-- A uniform consistency defect is invariant under a bijective relabeling of
    33	its question type. -/
    34	theorem consistencyDefect_uniform_question_equiv
    35	    {X Y Outcome iota : Type*}
    36	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Nonempty X]
    37	    [Fintype Y] [DecidableEq Y] [Nonempty Y]
    38	    [Fintype Outcome] [DecidableEq Outcome]
    39	    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    40	    (e : X ≃ Y) (A B : Y → Outcome → Op iota)
    41	    (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ iota) :
    42	    consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution X)
    43	        (fun x a => A (e x) a) (fun x a => B (e x) a) psi =
    44	      consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Y) A B psi := by
    45	  unfold consistencyDefect
    46	  simpa using avgOver_uniform_equiv e (fun x =>
    47	    ∑ a : Outcome, ∑ b : Outcome,
    48	      if a = b then 0 else
    49	        (inner ℂ psi ((EuclideanSpace.equiv iota ℂ).symm
    50	          (((A (e x) a) * (B (e x) b)).mulVec psi))).re)
    51	
    52	/-- A consistency defect is invariant under a bijective relabeling of both
    53	outcome families. -/
    54	theorem consistencyDefect_outcome_equiv
    55	    {X Alpha Beta iota : Type*}
    56	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X]
    57	    [Fintype Alpha] [DecidableEq Alpha]
    58	    [Fintype Beta] [DecidableEq Beta]
    59	    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    60	    (mu : Distribution X) (e : Beta ≃ Alpha)
    61	    (A B : X → Alpha → Op iota) (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ iota) :
    62	    consistencyDefect mu
    63	        (fun x b => A x (e b)) (fun x b => B x (e b)) psi =
    64	      consistencyDefect mu A B psi := by
    65	  unfold consistencyDefect
    66	  apply avgOver_congr
    67	  intro x
    68	  let term : Alpha → Alpha → ℝ := fun a b =>
    69	    if a = b then 0 else
    70	      (inner ℂ psi ((EuclideanSpace.equiv iota ℂ).symm
    71	        (((A x a) * (B x b)).mulVec psi))).re
    72	  calc
    73	    _ = ∑ a : Beta, ∑ b : Beta, term (e a) (e b) := by
    74	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    75	      intro a _
    76	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    77	      intro b _
    78	      unfold term
    79	      by_cases hab : a = b
    80	      · subst b
    81	        simp
    82	      · have heab : e a ≠ e b := fun h => hab (e.injective h)
    83	        simp [hab, heab]
    84	    _ =
    85	        ∑ a : Beta, ∑ b : Alpha, term (e a) b := by
    86	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    87	      intro a _
    88	      exact Equiv.sum_comp e (fun b => term (e a) b)
    89	    _ = ∑ a : Alpha, ∑ b : Alpha, term a b :=
    90	      Equiv.sum_comp e (fun a => ∑ b : Alpha, term a b)
    91	    _ = _ := rfl

    93	/-- Simultaneous bijective relabeling of uniform questions and outcomes leaves
    94	the consistency defect unchanged. -/
    95	theorem consistencyDefect_uniform_question_outcome_equiv
    96	    {X Y Alpha Beta iota : Type*}
    97	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Nonempty X]
    98	    [Fintype Y] [DecidableEq Y] [Nonempty Y]
    99	    [Fintype Alpha] [DecidableEq Alpha]
   100	    [Fintype Beta] [DecidableEq Beta]
   101	    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   102	    (questionEquiv : X ≃ Y) (outcomeEquiv : Beta ≃ Alpha)
   103	    (A B : Y → Alpha → Op iota) (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ iota) :
   104	    consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution X)
   105	        (fun x b => A (questionEquiv x) (outcomeEquiv b))
   106	        (fun x b => B (questionEquiv x) (outcomeEquiv b)) psi =
   107	      consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Y) A B psi := by
   108	  calc
   109	    consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution X)
   110	        (fun x b => A (questionEquiv x) (outcomeEquiv b))
   111	        (fun x b => B (questionEquiv x) (outcomeEquiv b)) psi =
   112	      consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution X)
   113	        (fun x a => A (questionEquiv x) a)
   114	        (fun x a => B (questionEquiv x) a) psi :=
   115	      consistencyDefect_outcome_equiv (uniformDistribution X)
   116	        outcomeEquiv _ _ psi
   117	    _ = consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Y) A B psi :=
   118	      consistencyDefect_uniform_question_equiv questionEquiv A B psi

   469	    fun s => (strategy.pointMeasurementB s.1).toSubMeas

   472	      let ℓ : AxisParallelLine params := { base := s.1, direction := s.2 }

   475	    fun s =>

    31	/-- The direct single-coordinate point/global defect is exactly the LDT
    32	defect after the polynomial, point, and scalar equivalences. -/
    33	theorem directPointPolynomial_consistencyDefect_eq
    34	    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
    35	    (hS : S.IsProjective) (r : Fin D.k) :
    36	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
    37	    ∀ (G : ProjMeas (MIPStarRE.LDT.Polynomial D.toLDTParameters) S.ιB),
    38	      consistencyDefect
    39	          (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))
    40	          (fun u a => heteroKron
    41	            ((directPointCoordinateMeasurementA D S r u).effect a) 1)
    42	          (fun u a => heteroKron 1
    43	            ((directPolynomialEvaluationMeasurement D G u).effect a)) S.ψ =
    44	        consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Point D.toLDTParameters))
    45	          (ldtPointAPlaced D S hS r)
    46	          (ldtPolynomialEvaluationRight D G) S.ψ := by
    47	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
    48	  intro G
    49	  calc
    50	    consistencyDefect
    51	        (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))
    52	        (fun u a => heteroKron
    53	          ((directPointCoordinateMeasurementA D S r u).effect a) 1)
    54	        (fun u a => heteroKron 1
    55	          ((directPolynomialEvaluationMeasurement D G u).effect a)) S.ψ =
    56	      consistencyDefect

    58	        (fun u a => ldtPointAPlaced D S hS r
    59	          (directPointEquiv D u) (directScalarEquiv D a))
    60	        (fun u a => ldtPolynomialEvaluationRight D G
    61	          (directPointEquiv D u) (directScalarEquiv D a)) S.ψ := by
    62	          apply consistencyDefect_congr
    63	          · intro u a

    74	        (ldtPolynomialEvaluationRight D G) S.ψ :=

+import MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.PolynomialAgreement
+import MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.MainTheorem.MainFormal
+import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.DirectLowDegree.Transport.Consistency.Defect
