    12	\title{Simultaneous Polynomial Measurements Are Not Obtained Coordinatewise}
    13	\author{}
    14	\date{2026-09-05}
    15	
    16	\begin{document}
    17	\maketitle
    18	
    19	\section{At a glance}
    20	
    21	\begin{itemize}
    22	  \item \textbf{Difficulty.} Easy for simultaneity parameter $k = 1$, hard
    23	  for general $k$.  The coordinatewise route planned for the formalization
    24	  applies the single-polynomial soundness theorem to each coordinate and
    25	  combines the resulting measurements by the sandwich of the source's
    26	  Lemma~\texttt{lem:ld-sandwich}; an explicit pair of measurements refutes
    27	  every bound this route could produce.  The source instead cites a
    28	  reduction of the $k$-tuple test to the single-polynomial test in $m + k$
    29	  variables, which is not formalized.
    30	  \item \textbf{Estimated weight.} The case $k = 1$ is closed by relabeling
    31	  the coordinate conclusions (about 150 lines).  The combining reduction
    32	  needs a combined strategy for the directly indexed game in dimension
    33	  $m + k$, a transfer of the success probability, and the extraction of
    34	  $k$ polynomials from one polynomial by linearity: roughly 8--15 new
    35	  definitions and 3000--5000 lines of formal proof.
    36	  \item \textbf{Mathlib/project split.} The counterexample is finite Fourier
    37	  analysis over $\F_{2^s}$ and a Gram-matrix estimate.  The missing reduction
    38	  is almost entirely project-local (game constructions and the consistency
    39	  calculus), with the Schwartz--Zippel lemma and multivariate polynomial
    40	  algebra taken from Mathlib.
    41	  \item \textbf{Key mathematical inputs.} Additive characters of $\F_q^2$
    42	  and isotropic vectors of a symmetric pairing in characteristic two; the
    43	  eigenvalue bound for nearly orthogonal unit vectors; the reduction proving
    44	  Theorem~4.43 from Theorem~4.40 in \cite{Natarajan2018NEEXP}.  Tracked in
    45	  \ghissue{134}.
    46	\end{itemize}
    47	
    48	\section{Key theorem forms}
    49	
    50	The source theorem (\texttt{lem:ld-soundness}) states that for every
    51	projective strategy passing the low individual degree game with parameters
    52	$(q,m,d,k)$ with probability at least $1 - \eps$ there are polynomial-tuple
    53	measurements $G^{\mathrm A}$ and $G^{\mathrm B}$, with outcomes
    54	$(g_1,\dots,g_k)$ of individual degree at most $d$, such that on average over
    55	a uniform point $u \in \F_q^m$
    56	\[
    57	  A^{\mathsf{Point},u}_{a} \ot I \simeq_{\delta_{\mathrm{ld}}}
    58	    I \ot G^{\mathrm B}_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot) = a]},
    59	  \qquad
    60	  G^{\mathrm A}_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot) = a]} \ot I \simeq_{\delta_{\mathrm{ld}}}
    61	    I \ot B^{\mathsf{Point},u}_{a},
    62	  \qquad
    63	  G^{\mathrm A}_{g} \ot I \simeq_{\delta_{\mathrm{ld}}} I \ot G^{\mathrm B}_{g},
    64	  \tag{source form}
    65	\]
    66	where $a = (a_1,\dots,a_k)$ and
    67	$\mathrm{eval}_u(g_1,\dots,g_k) = (g_1(u),\dots,g_k(u))$.
    68	
    69	The formalization planned to derive this from the case $k = 1$ as follows.
    70	Reading the $i$-th coordinate of every answer yields $k$ strategies for the
    71	game with $k = 1$, each passing with probability at least $1 - 3\eps$; the
    72	single-polynomial theorem gives projective measurements $G^{w,i}$ with
    73	\[
    74	  A^{\mathsf{Point},u}_{[a_i]} \ot I \simeq_{\delta}
    75	    I \ot G^{\mathrm B,i}_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot) = a_i]},
    76	  \qquad
    77	  G^{\mathrm A,i}_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot) = a_i]} \ot I \simeq_{\delta}
    78	    I \ot B^{\mathsf{Point},u}_{[a_i]},
    79	  \qquad
    80	  G^{\mathrm A,i}_{g} \ot I \simeq_{\delta} I \ot G^{\mathrm B,i}_{g},
    81	  \tag{coordinate form}
    82	\]
    83	where $A^{\mathsf{Point},u}_{[a_i]}$ is the $i$-th marginal of the joint
    84	point measurement; and the planned combination was the sandwich
    85	\[
    86	  C^{w}_{g_1,\dots,g_k}
    87	    = G^{w,k}_{g_k} \cdots G^{w,2}_{g_2}\, G^{w,1}_{g_1}\,
    88	      G^{w,2}_{g_2} \cdots G^{w,k}_{g_k},
    89	  \qquad
    90	  A^{\mathsf{Point},u}_{a} \ot I \simeq_{C k (\delta + md/q)^{1/2}}
    91	    I \ot C^{\mathrm B}_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot) = a]},
    92	  \tag{planned form}
    93	\]
    94	with a universal constant $C$, and likewise on the other side and for the
    95	global relation.  We show that no statement of the planned form holds: the
    96	coordinate form, even with $\delta = 0$ and even with both point
    97	measurements and all $2k$ polynomial measurements available, does not
    98	determine any polynomial-tuple measurement consistent with the joint point
    99	measurement.
   100	
   101	What the formalization proves is the source form for $k = 1$, with the
   102	error of the low individual degree theorem at the auxiliary parameter used
   103	by the transport, and this is the only value of $k$ instantiated by the
   104	Pauli basis test analysis.%
   105	\footnote{The declaration is
   106	\leanid{exists\_directSimultaneousPolynomialMeasurements\_of\_k\_eq\_one}
   107	in \doclink{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/DirectLowDegree/Transport/Simultaneous.lean};
   108	the instantiation with $k = 1$ at dimension $2m+2$ is in the proof of
   109	\texttt{lem:qld-4-7}, \path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex}.}
   110	
   111	\section{The source assertion}
   112	
   113	The proof of \texttt{lem:ld-soundness} in
   114	\cite[lines~413--458]{Ji2020MIPStar} treats $k = 1$ by an identification
   115	with the tensor-code test of \cite{Ji2021Quantum} (the identification is
   116	examined in \path{docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex}) and
   117	then extends to general $k$ by reference to the derivation of Theorem~4.43
   118	from Theorem~4.40 in \cite[lines~1409--1503]{Natarajan2018NEEXP}.  That
   119	derivation is not coordinatewise.  It builds two combined provers who play
   120	the single-polynomial test in $m + k$ variables: on a point $(\alpha, u)$
   121	the combined prover asks the original prover for the $k$ values
   122	$(b_1,\dots,b_k)$ at $u$ and returns $\sum_i \alpha_i b_i$, and on a line
   123	it returns the corresponding combination of the $k$ answer polynomials.  The
   124	single-polynomial theorem then yields one measurement with outcomes
   125	$g(\alpha,u)$, and the $k$ polynomials are recovered from $g$ because
   126	$g$ is exactly linear in $\alpha$ with high probability, by the
   127	Schwartz--Zippel lemma.  The simultaneity of the $k$ outputs is thus
   128	inherited from the joint answers of the original provers through a single
   129	application of the $k = 1$ theorem.
   130	
   131	\section{The counterexample}
   132	
   133	Let $q = 2^s$, let $d = 1$, and let $\Gamma$ be the set of univariate
   134	polynomials $g = g_0 + g_1 x$ over $\F_q$, so $|\Gamma| = N = q^2$.  Two
   135	distinct elements of $\Gamma$ agree at a uniformly random point of $\F_q$
   136	with probability at most $1/q$.  Bob's Hilbert space is $\C^{\Gamma}$ with
   137	standard basis $\{\ket{g}\}$; Alice's is a second copy, and the state is
   138	the maximally entangled state
   139	$\ket{\psi} = N^{-1/2} \sum_{g \in \Gamma} \ket{g}\ket{g}$, for which
   140	$(X \ot I)\ket{\psi} = (I \ot X^{\mathsf T})\ket{\psi}$ and
   141	$\bra{\psi} X \ot Y \ket{\psi} = N^{-1}\tr(X Y^{\mathsf T})$.
   142	
   143	Equip $\Gamma \cong \F_q^2$ with the symmetric pairing
   144	$\langle h, g\rangle = h_0 g_1 + h_1 g_0$ and the additive character
   145	$\chi(t) = (-1)^{\mathrm{tr}(t)}$, where $\mathrm{tr}$ is the absolute
   146	trace of $\F_q$; the pairing is nondegenerate, so
   147	$\phi_h = N^{-1/2} \sum_{g} \chi(\langle h, g\rangle)\ket{g}$, $h \in \Gamma$,
   148	is an orthonormal basis.  Evaluation at $u \in \F_q$ is represented by the
   149	vector $v_u = u + x$, since $\langle h, v_u\rangle = h_0 + h_1 u = h(u)$, and
   150	$\langle v_u, v_u\rangle = 2u = 0$ in characteristic two.  Bob's two
   151	coordinate measurements are
   152	\[
   153	  G^{1}_h = \ket{\phi_h}\bra{\phi_h},
   154	  \qquad
   155	  G^{2}_g = \ket{g}\bra{g},
   156	  \qquad
   157	  Q^{1,u}_{[a]} = \sum_{h(u) = a} G^1_h,
   158	  \qquad
   159	  Q^{2,u}_{[b]} = \sum_{g(u) = b} G^2_g .
   160	\]
   161	Writing $H_u = \{h : h(u) = 0\} = \F_q v_u$ and summing the character over
   162	the coset $\{h : h(u) = a\}$ gives the matrix elements
   163	\[
   164	  \bra{g'} Q^{1,u}_{[a]} \ket{g}
   165	    = \frac1N \sum_{h(u) = a} \chi(\langle h, g - g'\rangle)
   166	    = \frac{1}{q}\, \chi(\langle h_a, g - g'\rangle)\,
   167	      \mathbf 1[\,g(u) = g'(u)\,],
   168	\]
   169	where $h_a$ is any polynomial with $h_a(u) = a$: the sum over
   170	$H_u = \F_q v_u$ vanishes unless $\langle v_u, g - g'\rangle = 0$, that is,
   171	unless $g(u) = g'(u)$, because $v_u$ is isotropic.  Hence $Q^{1,u}_{[a]}$
   172	is block diagonal for the partition of $\Gamma$ by the value at $u$, it
   173	commutes with every $Q^{2,u}_{[b]}$, its diagonal entries all equal $1/q$,
   174	and each product $\Pi^u_{a,b} = Q^{1,u}_{[a]} Q^{2,u}_{[b]}$ is the rank-one
   175	projector onto the unit vector
   176	$\xi^u_{a,b} = q^{-1/2} \sum_{g(u) = b} \chi(\langle h_a, g\rangle)\ket{g}$.
   177	
   178	Let both players answer the point question $u$ with the joint projective
   179	measurement $\{\Pi^u_{a,b}\}_{a,b}$, which is real symmetric, and let Alice's
   180	coordinate polynomial measurements be the transposes $(G^{i})^{\mathsf T}$.
   181	On $\ket{\psi}$ every relation of the coordinate form holds with error
   182	$0$: the marginals of the joint point measurement are $Q^{1,u}_{[a]}$ and
   183	$Q^{2,u}_{[b]}$, which are exactly the evaluated coordinate measurements, and
   184	$(G^i)^{\mathsf T} \ot I$ agrees with $I \ot G^i$ on $\ket{\psi}$.  The
   185	collision probability is $1/q$.  The sandwich on Bob's side, evaluated at
   186	$u$, is
   187	\[
   188	  C^{\mathrm B}_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot) = (a,b)]}
   189	    = \sum_{g(u) = b} \ket{g}\bra{g}\, Q^{1,u}_{[a]}\, \ket{g}\bra{g}
   190	    = \frac1q\, Q^{2,u}_{[b]},
   191	\]
   192	and its consistency with the joint point measurement is
   193	\[
   194	  \sum_{a,b} \bra{\psi} \Pi^u_{a,b} \ot C^{\mathrm B}_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot) = (a,b)]}
   195	    \ket{\psi}
   196	    = \frac{1}{qN} \sum_{a,b} \tr\bigl(Q^{1,u}_{[a]} Q^{2,u}_{[b]}\bigr)
   197	    = \frac1q ,
   198	\]
   199	so the consistency defect is $1 - 1/q$ for every $u$, whereas the planned
   200	form promises at most $2C\,(1/q)^{1/2}$.  No universal constant $C$ survives
   201	$q \to \infty$; with the constant $C = 8$ established for the structured
   202	sandwich, the planned bound already fails at $q = 2^{9}$.  The same
   203	computation with the roles of the players exchanged refutes the planned
   204	bound for Alice's sandwich against Bob's point measurement, and
   205	$\sum_{g} \bra{\psi} (C^{\mathrm B}_g)^{\mathsf T} \ot C^{\mathrm B}_g \ket{\psi}
   206	= N^{-1} \sum_{g_1,g_2} |\langle g_2 | \phi_{g_1}\rangle|^4 = 1/N$ refutes it
   207	for the global relation.
   208	
   209	The obstruction is not specific to the sandwich.  Let
   210	$\{B_{g_1,g_2}\}$ be any POVM on Bob's space with polynomial-pair outcomes,
   211	and write $B_{g_1,g_2} = N p_{g_1,g_2}\,\rho_{g_1,g_2}$ with
   212	$p$ a probability distribution and $\rho$ density matrices.  Its
   213	consistency with the joint point measurement is
   214	\[
   215	  \E_{u} \sum_{g_1,g_2} p_{g_1,g_2}\,
   216	    \bra{\xi^u_{g_1(u),g_2(u)}}\, \rho_{g_1,g_2}\, \ket{\xi^u_{g_1(u),g_2(u)}}
   217	  \le \max_{g_1,g_2}\,
   218	    \lambda_{\max}\Bigl(\E_{u}\, \ket{\xi^u_{g_1(u),g_2(u)}}\!\bra{\xi^u_{g_1(u),g_2(u)}}\Bigr).
   219	\]
   220	For $u \ne u'$ the supports $\{g : g(u) = g_2(u)\}$ and
   221	$\{g : g(u') = g_2(u')\}$ meet exactly in $\{g_2\}$, so the $q$ unit vectors
   222	$\xi^u_{g_1(u),g_2(u)}$ have pairwise inner products of modulus $1/q$, and
   223	the largest eigenvalue of their Gram matrix is at most $1 + (q-1)/q < 2$.
   224	Hence the consistency of every polynomial-pair POVM with the joint point
   225	measurement is below $2/q$, on either side.  Consequently no argument that
   226	uses only the coordinate form --- with any error, any number of applications
   227	of the pasting or sandwich facts, and either player as reference --- can
   228	produce the source form for $k \ge 2$.
   229	
   230	Two remarks.  First, the pair $(\ket{\psi}, \Pi, G^1, G^2)$ is not a
   231	strategy for the low-degree game passing with high probability: by the same
   232	Gram-matrix bound no line measurement with polynomial-pair outcomes is
   233	consistent with the point measurements, so the source theorem is not
   234	contradicted; what fails is the coordinatewise route.  Second, the pasting
   235	fact (Fact~4.35 of \cite{Natarajan2018NEEXP}, imported as
   236	\texttt{lem:pasting}) does not repair the route: it requires the two
   237	coordinates to be evaluated at points $y_1, y_2$ whose conditional
   238	distribution supports a collision bound $\eta < 1$, whereas the low-degree
   239	game evaluates all coordinates at the same point, for which the conditional
   240	collision probability of any two polynomials agreeing there is $1$.
   241	
   242	\section{Comparison with the blueprint and formalization}
   243	
   244	The blueprint proof of \texttt{lem:ld-soundness} records the source route,
   245	including the extension from $k = 1$ to general $k$ by the derivation of
   246	Theorem~4.43 in \cite{Natarajan2018NEEXP}, and lists the game
   247	correspondence and the parameter bound as open obligations.  The present
   248	note adds a third: the extension is the combining reduction and must be
   249	formalized as such.  The directly indexed game and its transport prove the
   250	coordinate form from the low individual degree theorem for every $k$, and
   251	the source form for $k = 1$; the combination of the coordinate measurements
   252	by the sandwich is defined and is a POVM, but it carries no consistency
   253	estimate, and by the computation above it cannot.
   254	
   255	\section{Conclusion}
   256	
   257	The source statement is not contradicted.  Its proof for general $k$ is a
   258	reduction to a single application of the $k = 1$ theorem in $m + k$
   259	variables, and the formalization must follow that reduction; a
   260	coordinatewise application of the $k = 1$ theorem followed by any
   261	combination of the coordinate measurements provably cannot yield the
   262	theorem.  The application in the analysis of the Pauli basis test uses
   263	$k = 1$ only, for which the source form is proved from the low individual
   264	degree theorem.

    29	/-- Parameters for the directly indexed low-degree game.  Unlike `LdParams`,
    30	this directly indexed line-space construction has no divisibility field: its coordinate index is
    31	sampled from `Fin m` rather than encoded by fibers of `chiIndex`.
    32	
    33	This is the direct-index repair described in
    34	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`; it is not a second
    35	definition of the source verifier game. -/
    36	structure DirectLdParams where
    37	  q : ℕ
    38	  m : ℕ
    39	  d : ℕ
    40	  k : ℕ
    41	  hm : 1 ≤ m
    42	  hd : 1 ≤ d
    43	  hk : 1 ≤ k
    44	  hq : IsAdmissibleSize q
    45	
    46	/-- The canonical scalar model for directly indexed parameters. -/
    47	noncomputable def DirectLdParams.model (D : DirectLdParams) : FixedFieldModel D.q :=
    48	  fixedFieldModel D.q D.hq
    49	
    50	/-- The scalar field of a directly indexed low-degree game. -/
    51	abbrev DirectScalarQ (D : DirectLdParams) := D.model.K
    52	
    53	/-- The first coordinate, available because directly indexed dimensions are
    54	positive. -/
    55	def DirectLdParams.firstIndex (D : DirectLdParams) : Fin D.m :=
    56	  ⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one D.hm⟩
    57	
    58	instance (D : DirectLdParams) : Nonempty (Fin D.m) := ⟨D.firstIndex⟩
    59	
    60	/-- The direct game used at the extended dimension of the combining map.  Its
    61	field, degree, and simultaneity parameters are inherited from `P`, while its
    62	dimension is `2 * P.m + 2`; no divisibility assertion is introduced.
    63	
    64	The construction has dimension `2 * P.m + 2` without requiring
    65	`2 * P.m + 2 ∣ P.q`; it supplies the directly indexed line and coordinate
    66	spaces used in the dimension-extension argument of
    67	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1257-1293`.
    68	-/
    69	def AdmissibleParams.extendedDirectLd (P : AdmissibleParams) : DirectLdParams where
    70	  q := P.q
    71	  m := 2 * P.m + 2
    72	  d := P.d
    73	  k := 1
    74	  hm := by omega
    75	  hd := P.hd
    76	  hk := by decide
    77	  hq := P.hq
    78	
    79	/-- A common random sample for the directly indexed question distribution.
    80	The point, coordinate index, and unrestricted direction are mutually uniform. -/
    81	structure DirectLdSpace (D : DirectLdParams) where
    82	  point : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D
    83	  index : Fin D.m
    84	  direction : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D
    85	  deriving DecidableEq, Fintype
    86	
    87	instance (D : DirectLdParams) : Nonempty (DirectLdSpace D) :=
    88	  ⟨⟨0, D.firstIndex, 0⟩⟩
    89	
    90	/-- Decompose a direct sample into its point and the remaining independent
    91	coordinates. -/
    92	private def directLdSpacePointEquiv (D : DirectLdParams) :
    93	    DirectLdSpace D ≃
    94	      (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) ×
    95	        (Fin D.m × (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) where
    96	  toFun sample := (sample.point, sample.index, sample.direction)
    97	  invFun sample := ⟨sample.1, sample.2.1, sample.2.2⟩
    98	  left_inv sample := by cases sample; rfl
    99	  right_inv sample := by cases sample; rfl
   100	
   101	/-- Decompose a direct sample into its stored index and the remaining
   102	independent coordinates. -/
   103	def directLdSpaceIndexEquiv (D : DirectLdParams) :
   104	    DirectLdSpace D ≃
   105	      Fin D.m ×
   106	        ((Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) ×
   107	          (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) where
   108	  toFun sample := (sample.index, sample.point, sample.direction)
   109	  invFun sample := ⟨sample.2.1, sample.1, sample.2.2⟩
   110	  left_inv sample := by cases sample; rfl
   111	  right_inv sample := by cases sample; rfl
   112	
   113	/-- Compatibility name for the index-first direct-sample decomposition. -/
   114	abbrev directLdSpaceIndexSplitEquiv (D : DirectLdParams) :
   115	    DirectLdSpace D ≃
   116	      Fin D.m × ((Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) × (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) :=
   117	  directLdSpaceIndexEquiv D
   118	
   119	/-- Zero the coordinates preceding the directly sampled prefix index. -/
   120	def directPrefixProjection {D : DirectLdParams} (i : Fin D.m)
   121	    (v : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D :=
   122	  fun j => if j.val < i.val then 0 else v j
   123	
   124	/-- Canonical line descriptions whose coordinate index is stored directly.
   125	Coordinates are numbered from zero, so `index = i` represents coordinate
   126	`i + 1` in the paper. -/
   127	inductive DirectLineDesc (D : DirectLdParams) where
   128	  | axis (base : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) (index : Fin D.m)
   129	      (baseFixed : lineRepMap (coordinateDirection index) base = base)
   130	  | diagonal (base : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) (index : Fin D.m)
   131	      (direction : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)
   132	      (baseFixed : lineRepMap direction base = base)
   133	      (prefixZero : ∀ j : Fin D.m, j.val < index.val → direction j = 0)
   134	  deriving DecidableEq
   135	
   136	/-- The kind of a directly indexed line. -/
   137	def DirectLineDesc.kind {D : DirectLdParams} : DirectLineDesc D → LineKind
   138	  | .axis _ _ _ => .axis
   139	  | .diagonal _ _ _ _ _ => .diagonal
   140	
   141	/-- The coordinate index stored in a directly indexed line. -/
   142	def DirectLineDesc.index {D : DirectLdParams} : DirectLineDesc D → Fin D.m
   143	  | .axis _ index _ => index
   144	  | .diagonal _ index _ _ _ => index
   145	
   146	/-- The canonical base point of a directly indexed line. -/
   147	def DirectLineDesc.base {D : DirectLdParams} :
   148	    DirectLineDesc D → Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D
   149	  | .axis base _ _ => base
   150	  | .diagonal base _ _ _ _ => base
   151	
   152	/-- The geometric direction of a directly indexed line. -/
   153	def DirectLineDesc.direction {D : DirectLdParams} (line : DirectLineDesc D) :
   154	    Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D :=
   155	  match line with
   156	  | .axis _ index _ => coordinateDirection index
   157	  | .diagonal _ _ direction _ _ => direction
   158	
   159	/-- The base of a directly indexed description is fixed by its geometric
   160	direction. -/
   161	theorem DirectLineDesc.base_fixed {D : DirectLdParams} (line : DirectLineDesc D) :
   162	    lineRepMap line.direction line.base = line.base := by
   163	  cases line with
   164	  | axis base index baseFixed => exact baseFixed
   165	  | diagonal base index direction baseFixed prefixZero => exact baseFixed
   166	
   167	/-- Every directly indexed diagonal description retains its prefix-zero
   168	invariant. -/
   169	theorem DirectLineDesc.diagonal_prefix_zero {D : DirectLdParams}
   170	    (line : DirectLineDesc D) (hline : line.kind = .diagonal) :
   171	    ∀ j : Fin D.m, j.val < line.index.val → line.direction j = 0 := by
   172	  cases line with
   173	  | axis base index baseFixed => simp [DirectLineDesc.kind] at hline
   174	  | diagonal base index direction baseFixed prefixZero => exact prefixZero
   175	
   176	/-- The point set represented by a directly indexed line. -/
   177	noncomputable def DirectLineDesc.pointSet {D : DirectLdParams}
   178	    (line : DirectLineDesc D) : Set (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) :=
   179	  linePoints line.base line.direction

    19	This file builds the project's finite-dimensional measurement layer on top of

    21	for the quantum formalization in `references/ldt-paper/`.
    22	-/

    24	open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder

    26	namespace MIPStarRE.Quantum
    27	
    28	/-! ## Submeasurements and measurements -/
    29	
    30	/--
    31	A submeasurement on a finite answer type `α` is a family of PSD matrices
    32	`M : α → Op d` with `∑ a, M a ≤ 1`.
    33	-/
    34	structure Submeasurement (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] where
    35	  /-- The effect operators. -/
    36	  effect : α → Op d
    37	  /-- Each effect is positive semidefinite. -/
    38	  pos : ∀ a, 0 ≤ effect a
    39	  /-- The effects sum to at most the identity. -/
    40	  sum_le_one : ∑ a, effect a ≤ 1
    41	
    42	/--
    43	A measurement is a submeasurement whose effects sum exactly to the identity.
    44	-/
    45	structure Measurement (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    46	    extends Submeasurement α d where
    47	  /-- The effects sum to the identity. -/
    48	  sum_eq_one : ∑ a, effect a = 1
    49	
    50	/-! ## Totals and postprocessing -/
    51	
    52	namespace Submeasurement
    53	
    54	variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    55	variable {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
    56	
    57	/-! ### Totals and postprocessing -/
    58	
    59	/-- The total operator `∑ a, M_a`. -/
    60	noncomputable def total (M : Submeasurement α d) : Op d :=
    61	  ∑ a, M.effect a
    62	
    63	/--
    64	Data processing: relabel the answer set by `f : α → β`, summing the effects over
    65	fibers.
    66	-/
    67	noncomputable def postprocess [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    68	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) : Submeasurement β d where
    69	  effect b := ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
    70	  pos b := Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => M.pos a
    71	  sum_le_one := by
    72	    calc
    73	      ∑ b, ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
    74	          = ∑ a, M.effect a := Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect
    75	      _ ≤ 1 := M.sum_le_one
    76	
    77	/-- Restatement of `sum_le_one` in terms of the named total operator. -/
    78	theorem total_le_one (M : Submeasurement α d) :
    79	    M.total ≤ 1 := by
    80	  simpa [total] using M.sum_le_one
    81	
    82	/-- Postprocessing preserves the sum of all effects. -/
    83	theorem postprocess_sum_eq [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    84	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) :
    85	    ∑ a, M.effect a = ∑ b, (M.postprocess f).effect b :=
    86	  (Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect).symm
    87	
    88	/-- Postprocessing preserves the named total operator. -/
    89	theorem postprocess_total [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    90	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) :
    91	    (M.postprocess f).total = M.total := by
    92	  simpa [total] using (M.postprocess_sum_eq f).symm
    93	
    94	end Submeasurement

    98	variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]

   100	
   101	/--
   102	Build a complete measurement from effects whose sum is exactly the identity.
   103	
   104	This constructor keeps the equality proof as the primary hypothesis and derives
   105	the inherited submeasurement inequality automatically.  It is useful at paper
   106	sites that are explicitly POVMs rather than relaxed sub-POVMs.
   107	-/
   108	def ofSumEqOne (effect : α → Op d) (pos : ∀ a, 0 ≤ effect a)
   109	    (sum_eq_one : ∑ a, effect a = 1) : Measurement α d where
   110	  effect := effect
   111	  pos := pos
   112	  sum_le_one := le_of_eq sum_eq_one
   113	  sum_eq_one := sum_eq_one
   114	
   115	/-- The named total of a complete measurement is the identity. -/
   116	theorem total_eq_one (M : Measurement α d) :
   117	    M.total = 1 :=
   118	  M.sum_eq_one
   119	
   120	/--
   121	Postprocess a complete measurement by relabeling outcomes.
   122	
   123	This formalizes `references/ldt-paper/preliminaries.tex:169--180`: regrouping
   124	the effects along the fibers of `f` preserves the total operator, so a POVM
   125	remains a POVM after postprocessing.
   126	-/
   127	noncomputable def postprocess [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   128	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) : Measurement β d where
   129	  toSubmeasurement := M.toSubmeasurement.postprocess f
   130	  sum_eq_one := by
   131	    calc
   132	      ∑ b, ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
   133	          = ∑ a, M.effect a := Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect
   134	      _ = 1 := M.sum_eq_one
   135	
   136	@[simp] theorem postprocess_effect [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   137	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) (b : β) :
   138	    (M.postprocess f).effect b =
   139	      ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a :=
   140	  rfl
   141	
   142	@[simp] theorem postprocess_to_submeasurement [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   143	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) :
   144	    (M.postprocess f).toSubmeasurement = M.toSubmeasurement.postprocess f :=
   145	  rfl
   146	
   147	/-- A complete measurement is determined by its effects. -/
   148	theorem ext {M N : Measurement α d} (h : ∀ a, M.effect a = N.effect a) :
   149	    M = N := by
   150	  cases M with
   151	  | mk M hM =>
   152	      cases N with
   153	      | mk N hN =>
   154	          cases M with
   155	          | mk effectM posM leM =>
   156	              cases N with
   157	              | mk effectN posN leN =>
   158	                  simp only at h
   159	                  have heffect : effectM = effectN := funext h
   160	                  subst effectN
   161	                  rfl
   162	
   163	/-- Relabeling along `f` and then along `g` is relabeling along `g ∘ f`: the
   164	fiber of `g ∘ f` over `c` is the disjoint union of the fibers of `f` over the
   165	fiber of `g` over `c`, and regrouping a finite sum of effects along it does not
   166	change the sum. -/
   167	theorem postprocess_comp {γ : Type*} [Fintype γ]
   168	    [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β] [DecidableEq γ]
   169	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) (g : β → γ) :
   170	    (M.postprocess f).postprocess g = M.postprocess (fun a => g (f a)) := by
   171	  classical
   172	  apply ext
   173	  intro c
   174	  calc
   175	    ((M.postprocess f).postprocess g).effect c =
   176	        ∑ b : β, if g b = c then
   177	          ∑ a : α, if f a = b then M.effect a else 0
   178	        else 0 := by
   179	          change (∑ b ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun b : β => g b = c),
   180	            ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a : α => f a = b), M.effect a) = _
   181	          rw [Finset.sum_filter]
   182	          apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   183	          intro b _
   184	          by_cases hgb : g b = c
   185	          · simp only [hgb, if_true]
   186	            rw [Finset.sum_filter]
   187	          · simp [hgb]
   188	    _ = ∑ b : β, ∑ a : α,
   189	        if g b = c ∧ f a = b then M.effect a else 0 := by
   190	          apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   191	          intro b _
   192	          by_cases hgc : g b = c <;> simp [hgc]
   193	    _ = ∑ a : α, ∑ b : β,
   194	        if g b = c ∧ f a = b then M.effect a else 0 := by
   195	          rw [Finset.sum_comm]
   196	    _ = ∑ a : α,
   197	        if g (f a) = c then M.effect a else 0 := by
   198	          apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   199	          intro a _
   200	          by_cases hgc : g (f a) = c
   201	          · rw [Finset.sum_eq_single (f a)]
   202	            · simp [hgc]
   203	            · intro b _ hba
   204	              by_cases hfa : f a = b
   205	              · exact (hba hfa.symm).elim
   206	              · simp [hfa]
   207	            · simp
   208	          · have hzero :
   209	                (∑ b : β,
   210	                  if g b = c ∧ f a = b then M.effect a else 0) = 0 := by
   211	              apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
   212	              intro b _
   213	              by_cases hfa : f a = b
   214	              · subst b
   215	                simp [hgc]
   216	              · simp [hfa]
   217	            simp [hgc, hzero]
   218	    _ = (M.postprocess (fun a => g (f a))).effect c := by
   219	          change _ = ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter
   220	            (fun a : α => g (f a) = c), M.effect a
   221	          rw [Finset.sum_filter]
   222	
   223	end Measurement

     6	/-!
     7	# The scalar error of the low-degree soundness transport
     8	
     9	This module supplies the scalar half of the soundness transport for the
    10	directly indexed low-degree game.  Its content is purely arithmetic: the
    11	auxiliary sampling parameter with which the mature low individual degree
    12	theorem is applied to a coordinate strategy, the resulting bounds on the three
    13	terms of the mature error `mainFormalError`, and the absorption of the
    14	simultaneous-measurement estimate into the error function `deltaLd` of
    15	`lem:ld-soundness`.
    16	
    17	## Main definitions
    18	
    19	* `directLdAuxParameter D = 2560000 m³ d` is the sampling parameter handed to
    20	  `MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.mainFormal`.  It is the multiple of the exponential scale
    21	  `2560000 m²` of `mainFormalError` with quotient `m d`, so that the
    22	  exponential term of the mature error is exactly `exp (-m d)`.
    23	
    24	## Main results
    25	
    26	* `directLdAuxParameter_pos` and `four_hundred_mul_le_directLdAuxParameter` are
    27	  the two hypotheses `0 < k` and `400 m d ≤ k` of `mainFormal`, proved from the
    28	  positivity of the dimension and of the degree alone.
    29	* `directLd_test_term_le`, `directLd_field_term_le` and
    30	  `directLd_exponential_term_le` bound the three terms of
    31	  `mainFormalError D.toLDTParameters (directLdAuxParameter D) (3 ε)`: the test
    32	  term by `3 ε^(1/40000)`, the field term by `d q^(-1/40000)`, and the
    33	  exponential term by `2^(-b m d)` for every `0 ≤ b ≤ 1`.
    34	* `exists_directLdTransportConstants` exhibits, for a sandwich constant
    35	  `C₀ ≥ 1`, the explicit universal constants `a = 2500000000 C₀` and
    36	  `b = 1/80000` for which `C₀ k √(mainFormalError + m d / q + ε)` is at most
    37	  `deltaLd a b ε q m d k` in the regime `0 < ε ≤ 1`.
    38	* `one_le_deltaLd_of_one_le_error` and
    39	  `one_le_deltaLd_of_fieldSize_le_degree` bound `deltaLd` below by one in the
    40	  two degenerate regimes `1 ≤ ε` and `q ≤ d`, and
    41	  `consistencyDefect_heteroKron_le_one` bounds every bipartite consistency
    42	  defect on a unit state above by one.  Together they close both degenerate
    43	  regimes, where the conclusion of `lem:ld-soundness` carries no information.
    44	
    45	The exponent `b = 1/80000` is half the exponent `1/40000` carried by
    46	`mainFormalError`; the halving is exactly what the square root of the
    47	simultaneous-measurement estimate costs.

   394	We define a special class of measurements that are relevant to the soundness
   395	properties of the low-degree test.
   396	
   397	\begin{definition}[Low-degree polynomial measurements]
   398	  \label{def:ld-meas}
   399	  Define $\polymeas{m}{d}{q}$ to be the set of POVM measurements whose outcomes
   400	  correspond to (individual) degree-$d$ polynomials of $m$ variables over
   401	  $\F_q$.
   402	  More generally, for an integer $\ldc$ and tuples $m=(m_1, m_2, \ldots,
   403	  m_\ldc)$, $d=(d_1, d_2, \ldots, d_\ldc)$ and $q=(q_1, q_2, \ldots, q_\ldc)$,
   404	  we let $\simulpolymeas{m}{d}{q}{\ldc}$ be the set of measurements $G =
   405	  \{G_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots\,,\, g_\ldc}\}$ such that for $i\in\{1, 2, \ldots,
   406	  \ldc\}$, $g_i$ is a polynomial $g_i:\F_{q_i}^{m_i} \rightarrow
   407	  \F_{q_i}$ with individual degree $d_i$ (see \Cref{sec:ld-encoding} for a definition of individual degree). 
   408	\end{definition}
   409	
   410	Quantum soundness of a version of the classical low-degree test for polynomials of low \emph{total} degree was claimed
   411	in~\cite{natarajan2018low}, building on an analysis of a three-prover version of the test in~\cite{vidick2016three}. Unfortunately there is a gap in the soundness analysis of this test. For our construction we use the low individual degree test, whose quantum soundness is shown in~\cite{ML20} and generalized in~\cite{ji2021quantum}. We state the result in the form that is most directly useful for us, and show how the stated result follows from~\cite{ji2021quantum}.
   412	
   413	\begin{theorem}[Quantum soundness of the simultaneous classical low-degree test]
   414	  \label{lem:ld-soundness}
   415	  There exists a function $\delta_{\ld}(\eps, q, m, d, \ldc) = a (dm \ldc)^a (\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$ for universal constants $a\geq 1$ and $0<b\leq 1$ 
   416	such that the following
   417	  holds.
   418	  For all $\eps > 0$ and parameter tuple $\ldparams = (q, m, d, \ldc)$, for all
   419	  projective strategies $(\psi,A,B)$ that succeed with probability at least
   420	  $1-\eps$ in the game $\game^\ld_\ldparams$, there exists measurements
   421	  \[G^w \in \simulpolymeas{m}{d}{q}{\ldc}\] on $\mH_w$, for
   422	  $w\in\{\alice,\bob\}$, such that
   423	  \begin{equation*}
   424	    \begin{split}
   425	      A^{\Point,\, u}_{a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots\,,\, a_\ldc}
   426	      & \abc[\delta_{\ld}]
   427	      G^\bob_{[(g_1(u),g_2(u),\ldots,g_\ldc(u)) = (a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots \,,\, a_\ldc)]}\;,\\
   428	      G^\alice_{[(g_1(u),g_2(u),\ldots,g_\ldc(u)) = (a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots \,,\, a_\ldc)]}
   429	      & \abc[\delta_{\ld}]
   430				 B^{\Point,\, u}_{a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots\,,\, a_\ldc}\;,\\
   431	      G^\alice_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots \,,\, g_\ldc}
   432	      & \abc[\delta_{\ld}]
   433	      G^\bob_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots \,,\, g_\ldc}\;,
   434	    \end{split}
   435	  \end{equation*}
   436	  where $\delta_{\ld} = \delta_{\ld}(\eps, q, m, d, \ldc)$, 
   437	  and all three statements are with respect to the state $\ket{\psi}$.
   438	In addition, the first two approximations hold under the uniform distribution over $u\in \F_q^m$,
   439		whereas there is no question distribution associated with the third approximation.
   440	\end{theorem}
   441	
   442	\begin{proof}
   443	Let $\ldparams = (q, m, d, \ldc)$
   444	where $m, d, \ldc \in \N$ are integers, $q \in \N$ is an admissible field size,
   445	and $m$ divides $q$. Let $\Sigma=\F_q$. Let $\code \subseteq \Sigma^q$ be the Reed-Solomon code with degree $d$. Explicitly, $\code$ is the set of all $(p(x_1),\ldots,p(x_n))$ where $p:\F_q\to\F_q$ is a univariate polynomial of degree at most $d$ and $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ are an enumeration of $\F_q$. Then in the (standard) notation from~\cite{ji2021quantum} $\code$ is a linear $[q,d+1,n-d+1]_\Sigma$ code.
   446	
   447	Observe that the two-prover tensor code test, for the code $\code^{\otimes m}$, as described in~\cite[Figure 1 and Figure 2]{ji2021quantum}, is identical to the game $\game^\ld$ with parameters $\ldparams$ and $\ldc=1$, whose decider is presented in Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider}. This is because 
   448	\begin{enumerate}
   449	\item The \emph{axis-parallel line-versus-point test} from Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} is identical to the \emph{axis-parallel lines test} from~\cite[Figure 1]{ji2021quantum}, with the only difference that in Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} the roles of A and B are chosen uniformly at random. This is consistent with the two-prover variant of the tensor code test from~\cite[Section 4.1]{ji2021quantum}.
   450	\item The \emph{diagonal line-versus-point test} from Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} is identical to the \emph{subcube commutation test} from~\cite[Figure 1]{ji2021quantum}, with again the added symmetrization between players. 
   451	\item The \emph{consistency test} from Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} is identical to the \emph{synchronicity test} from~\cite[Figure 2]{ji2021quantum}.
   452	\end{enumerate}
   453	
   454	As a result,~\cite[Theorem 4.7]{ji2021quantum}, in which we choose the parameter $k$ as $k=m^3d$,  immediately yields \Cref{lem:ld-soundness}.
   455	
   456	To conclude it remains to extend the result to the case of general $\ldc$. This is done 
   457	via a standard reduction, following exactly the same steps as the derivation of Theorem 4.43 from Theorem 4.40 in~\cite{NW19}.
   458	\end{proof}

   155	\begin{notation}\label{not:conditioned-on-last-direction}
   156	Our proof will be via induction,
   157	i.e.\ proving soundness of the $(m+1,q,d)$-low individual degree test
   158	using the soundness of the $(m,q,d)$-low individual degree test.
   159	To do this, we will frequently use the axis-parallel line test in the specific case of $i = m+1$.
   160	Thus, it will be convenient to introduce the following notation.
   161	Let $(\psi, A, B, L)$ be a symmetric strategy for the $(m+1, q, d)$-low individual degree test,
   162	Then for each $u \in \F_q^m$ we will write $B^u_f$ as shorthand for $B^{\ell}_f$,
   163	where $\ell = \{(u, x) \mid x \in \F_q\}$.
   164	For a function $f:\ell \rightarrow \F_q$,
   165	we will also sometimes write $f(x)$ as shorthand for $f(u,x)$.
   166	\end{notation}
   167	
   168	\begin{definition}
   169	Consider the $(m,q,d)$-low individual degree test.
   170	For $j \in \{1, \ldots, m\}$,
   171	we refer to the \emph{$j$-restricted diagonal lines test}
   172	as the diagonal lines test conditioned on $\bi = j$.
   173	For example, in the $m$-restricted diagonal lines test,
   174	the line $\bell$ is simply a uniformly random line in $\F_q^m$.
   175	\end{definition}
   176	
   177	Now we state our main theorem using notation which will be introduced in \Cref{sec:prelims} below.
   178	This the formal version of \Cref{thm:main-informal}.
   179	
   180	\begin{theorem}[Main theorem; quantum soundness of the low individual degree test]\label{thm:main-formal}
   181	  Consider a projective strategy $(\psi, A^{\mathrm{A}},B^{\mathrm{A}},L^{\mathrm{A}},A^{\mathrm{B}},B^{\mathrm{B}},L^{\mathrm{B}})$ 
   182	   which passes the  $(m,q,d)$-low individual degree test with probability at least $1-\eps$.
   183	  Let $k \geq md$ be an integer.
   184	  Let
   185	  \begin{equation*}
   186	  \nu = 100000 k^2m^4 \cdot \Big(\eps^{1/40000} + (d/q)^{1/40000} + e^{-k/(2560000m^2)}\Big).
   187	  \end{equation*}
   188	Then there exists projective measurements $G^{\mathrm{A}}, G^{\mathrm{B}} \in \polymeas{m}{q}{d}$ with the following properties:
   189	\begin{enumerate}
   190	  \item (Consistency with~$A$):  On average over $\bu \sim \F_q^{m}$,
   191		  \begin{align*}
   192		  A^{\mathrm{A},u}_a \otimes I
   193		  	&\simeq_{\nu} I \otimes G^{\mathrm{B}}_{[g(u)=a]},\\
   194		I \otimes A^{\mathrm{B},u}_a
   195		  	&\simeq_{\nu}  G^{\mathrm{A}}_{[g(u)=a]} \ot I.
   196		  \end{align*}
   197	\item (Self-consistency):
   198		\begin{equation*}
   199		G^{\mathrm{A}}_g \ot I \simeq_{\nu} I \ot G^{\mathrm{B}}_g.
   200		\end{equation*}
   201	\end{enumerate}
   202	\end{theorem}
   203	
   204	We note that there is a tradeoff in \Cref{thm:main-formal} specified by the parameter~$k$.
   205	As~$k$ increases, $\nu$'s prefactor $k^2$ increases.
   206	On the other hand, as $k$ increases, the term $e^{- k/(2560000m^2)}$ which also occurs in $\nu$ \emph{decreases}.
   207	Thus, when applying this theorem, one must select~$k$ to balance these competing demands.
   208	Typically, choosing $k = \poly(m)$ should be more than sufficient for applications.
   209	We believe that this parameter~$k$ is an artifact of our proof,
   210	and we hope that it will be removed in the future.

+## The simultaneity obstruction
+
+For simultaneity parameter `k ≥ 2` the coordinate conclusions alone do not
+determine simultaneous polynomial measurements, so no palindromic combination
+of the coordinate measurements can be consistent with a joint point
+measurement in general.  Let `q = 2^s`, let the degree be `1`, and let Bob
+measure the univariate polynomials `g = g₀ + g₁ x` once in the standard basis
+`|g⟩` and once in the Fourier basis attached to the symmetric pairing
+`⟨h, g⟩ = h₀ g₁ + h₁ g₀`.  In characteristic two every evaluation functional
+`h ↦ h(u)` is represented by an isotropic vector of this pairing, so at every
+point `u` the value-level coarse-grainings `Q^{1,u}_{[a]}` (Fourier basis) and
+`Q^{2,u}_{[b]}` (standard basis) commute, and on the maximally entangled state
+Alice may answer point questions with the joint projective measurement
+`P^u_{a,b} = (Q^{1,u}_{[a]} Q^{2,u}_{[b]})ᵀ`.  All coordinate consistencies of
+`lem:ld-soundness` then hold with defect `0` and distinct polynomials collide
+at a uniform point with probability `1 / q`, but the sandwiched POVM has
+`∑_{g₂(u) = b} |g₂⟩⟨g₂| Q^{1,u}_{[a]} |g₂⟩⟨g₂| = q⁻¹ Q^{2,u}_{[b]}`, whose
+consistency defect against `P^u` is `1 - 1/q`; more strongly, every
+polynomial-pair POVM on Bob's side has defect at least `1 - 2/q` against

+reduction of Theorem 4.43 in the NEEXP paper, which applies the `k = 1`

+not formalized here.  The two-measurement pasting estimate (Fact 4.35 there)
+does not apply either, since it evaluates the two coordinates at
+independently sampled points while the low-degree game evaluates all
+coordinates at one point.  The counterexample and the resulting formal

   102	    (g g' : Polynomial params) (hneq : g ≠ g') :

   104	      (fun u => if g u = g' u then (1 : Error) else 0) ≤
   105	      (params.m * params.d : Error) / params.q := by

   108	    ⟨g.poly, by
   109	      rw [MvPolynomial.mem_restrictDegree_iff_sup]
   110	      simpa [MvPolynomial.degreeOf_def] using g.lowIndividualDegree⟩
   111	  let g'Low : polyFunc params.m (Scalar params) params.d :=
   112	    ⟨g'.poly, by

   114	      simpa [MvPolynomial.degreeOf_def] using g'.lowIndividualDegree⟩

   132	    calc

   153	            params.m (Scalar params) g.poly g'.poly : Error) := by
   154	              simp [polynomialAgreementProbability, div_eq_mul_inv]

   161	              (1 : Error)

   165	          params.m (Scalar params) g.poly g'.poly : Error) :=
   166	          havg_scalar

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/DirectLowDegree/Transport/BranchComparison.lean-7-
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/DirectLowDegree/Transport/BranchComparison.lean-8-Every branch of the mature low individual degree failure probability of a
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/DirectLowDegree/Transport/BranchComparison.lean-9-coordinate strategy `directCoordinateProjStrat` is compared with the ordered
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/DirectLowDegree/Transport/BranchComparison.lean-10-type-pair branch of the direct game asking the same questions.  An accepted
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/DirectLowDegree/Transport/BranchComparison.lean-11-direct answer pair reads out to equal mature answers: the line answer, rebased
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/DirectLowDegree/Transport/BranchComparison.lean-12-to the mature line and evaluated at the mature base point, is the point
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/DirectLowDegree/Transport/BranchComparison.lean-13-answer, and the zero-direction convention reads the constant value at the base
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/DirectLowDegree/Transport/BranchComparison.lean-14-point.  Hence the mature inconsistency mass at a question pair is at most the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/DirectLowDegree/Transport/BranchComparison.lean-15-rejected direct Born mass there.  The point-agreement and axis-line branches
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/DirectLowDegree/Transport/BranchComparison.lean:16:then compare exactly after the coordinate reindexing of `directPointEquiv`;
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/DirectLowDegree/Transport/BranchComparison.lean-17-the diagonal branches are treated in `Transport.DiagonalRecursion`.

    94	- `references/ldt-paper/inductive_step.tex` lines 119–133 (the `mainFormal`
    95	  Step 5 self-consistency cascade, issue #425),
    96	- `references/ldt-paper/commutativity-G.tex` (the `comMain` step, issue #297).

    98	Both call sites previously held a private duplicate of this proof; this is the
    99	shared, reusable form. -/
   100	lemma polynomialAgreement_avg_le_mdq
   101	    (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q]
   102	    (g g' : Polynomial params) (hneq : g ≠ g') :
   103	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (Point params))
   104	      (fun u => if g u = g' u then (1 : Error) else 0) ≤
   105	      (params.m * params.d : Error) / params.q := by
   106	  classical
   107	  let gLow : polyFunc params.m (Scalar params) params.d :=
   108	    ⟨g.poly, by
   109	      rw [MvPolynomial.mem_restrictDegree_iff_sup]
   110	      simpa [MvPolynomial.degreeOf_def] using g.lowIndividualDegree⟩
   111	  let g'Low : polyFunc params.m (Scalar params) params.d :=
   112	    ⟨g'.poly, by
   113	      rw [MvPolynomial.mem_restrictDegree_iff_sup]
   114	      simpa [MvPolynomial.degreeOf_def] using g'.lowIndividualDegree⟩
   115	  have hneqLow : gLow ≠ g'Low := by
   116	    intro hEq
   117	    have hpoly : g.poly = g'.poly := congrArg Subtype.val hEq
   118	    apply hneq
   119	    cases g
   120	    cases g'
   121	    cases hpoly
   122	    rfl
   123	  have hsz := schwartzZippel_individualDegree gLow g'Low hneqLow
   124	  have havg_scalar :
   125	      avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin params.m → Scalar params))
   126	        (fun u =>
   127	          if MvPolynomial.eval u g.poly = MvPolynomial.eval u g'.poly then
   128	            (1 : Error)
   129	          else 0) =
   130	      (polynomialAgreementProbability
   131	        params.m (Scalar params) g.poly g'.poly : Error) := by
   132	    calc
   133	      avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin params.m → Scalar params))
   134	          (fun u =>
   135	            if MvPolynomial.eval u g.poly = MvPolynomial.eval u g'.poly then
   136	              (1 : Error)
   137	            else 0)
   138	        = ∑ u : Fin params.m → Scalar params,
   139	            if MvPolynomial.eval u g.poly = MvPolynomial.eval u g'.poly then
   140	              (Fintype.card (Scalar params) ^ params.m : Error)⁻¹
   141	            else 0 := by
   142	              simp [avgOver, uniformDistribution]
   143	      _ = Finset.sum
   144	            ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin params.m → Scalar params)).filter
   145	              (fun u => MvPolynomial.eval u g.poly = MvPolynomial.eval u g'.poly))
   146	            (fun _ => (Fintype.card (Scalar params) ^ params.m : Error)⁻¹) := by
   147	              rw [← Finset.sum_filter]
   148	      _ = (((Finset.univ.filter fun u : Fin params.m → Scalar params =>
   149	              MvPolynomial.eval u g.poly = MvPolynomial.eval u g'.poly).card : ℕ) : Error) *
   150	            (Fintype.card (Scalar params) ^ params.m : Error)⁻¹ := by
   151	              simp
   152	      _ = (polynomialAgreementProbability
   153	            params.m (Scalar params) g.poly g'.poly : Error) := by
   154	              simp [polynomialAgreementProbability, div_eq_mul_inv]
   155	  calc
   156	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (Point params))
   157	        (fun u => if g u = g' u then (1 : Error) else 0)
   158	      = avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin params.m → Scalar params))
   159	          (fun u =>
   160	            if MvPolynomial.eval u g.poly = MvPolynomial.eval u g'.poly then
   161	              (1 : Error)
   162	            else 0) :=
   163	            polynomialAgreement_avg_eq_scalarDomain params g g'
   164	    _ = (polynomialAgreementProbability
   165	          params.m (Scalar params) g.poly g'.poly : Error) :=
   166	          havg_scalar
   167	    _ ≤ ((((params.m * params.d : ℕ) : ℚ≥0) / Fintype.card (Scalar params)) : Error) := by
   168	          exact_mod_cast hsz
   169	    _ = (params.m * params.d : Error) / params.q := by
   170	          simp [div_eq_mul_inv]

   172	/-- Reindex evaluation equality for degree-`d` line polynomials from coded
   173	`Fq params` parameters to the scalar field used by Mathlib's univariate
   174	polynomial API. -/
   175	lemma axisLinePolynomialAgreement_avg_eq_scalarDomain
   176	    (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q]
   177	    (f h : AxisLinePolynomial params) :
   178	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fq params))
   179	      (fun t => if f t = h t then (1 : Error) else 0) =
   180	      avgOver (uniformDistribution (Scalar params))
   181	        (fun x =>
   182	          if _root_.Polynomial.eval x f.poly = _root_.Polynomial.eval x h.poly then
   183	            (1 : Error)
   184	          else 0) := by
   185	  let e : Fq params ≃ Scalar params := (FieldModel.equiv (q := params.q)).symm
   186	  calc
   187	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fq params))
   188	        (fun t => if f t = h t then (1 : Error) else 0)
   189	      = avgOver (uniformDistribution (Scalar params))
   190	          (fun x => if f (e.symm x) = h (e.symm x) then (1 : Error) else 0) := by
   191	            simpa [e] using
   192	              (avgOver_uniform_equiv e
   193	                (fun t : Fq params => if f t = h t then (1 : Error) else 0))
   194	    _ = avgOver (uniformDistribution (Scalar params))
   195	        (fun x =>
   196	          if _root_.Polynomial.eval x f.poly = _root_.Polynomial.eval x h.poly then
   197	            (1 : Error)
   198	          else 0) := by
   199	            apply avgOver_congr
   200	            intro x
   201	            by_cases hx : _root_.Polynomial.eval x f.poly = _root_.Polynomial.eval x h.poly
   202	            · have hdecode : decodeScalar (e.symm x) = x := by
   203	                simp [e, decodeScalar]
   204	              have hcoded : f (e.symm x) = h (e.symm x) := by
   205	                change encodeScalar (_root_.Polynomial.eval (decodeScalar (e.symm x)) f.poly) =
   206	                  encodeScalar (_root_.Polynomial.eval (decodeScalar (e.symm x)) h.poly)
   207	                simpa [hdecode] using congrArg encodeScalar hx
   208	              simp [hx, hcoded]
   209	            · have hdecode : decodeScalar (e.symm x) = x := by
   210	                simp [e, decodeScalar]
   211	              have hcoded : ¬ f (e.symm x) = h (e.symm x) := by
   212	                intro hEq
   213	                apply hx
   214	                have henc :
   215	                    encodeScalar (_root_.Polynomial.eval x f.poly) =
   216	                      encodeScalar (_root_.Polynomial.eval x h.poly) := by
   217	                  simpa [AxisLinePolynomial.toFun, evalLinePolynomialModel, hdecode] using hEq
   218	                exact (FieldModel.equiv (q := params.q)).injective henc
   219	              simp [hx, hcoded]

   221	/-- Schwartz--Zippel for two distinct degree-`d` axis-line answers, stated with
   222	the ambient `m*d/q` loss used in the LDT estimates.  The underlying univariate
   223	root count gives `d/q`, and `params.hm` deliberately pads it to the paper's
   224	ambient `m*d/q` loss. -/
   225	lemma axisLinePolynomialAgreement_avg_le_mdq
   226	    (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q]
   227	    (f h : AxisLinePolynomial params) (hneq : f.poly ≠ h.poly) :
   228	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fq params))
   229	      (fun t => if f t = h t then (1 : Error) else 0) ≤
   230	      (params.m * params.d : Error) / params.q := by
   231	  classical
   232	  let S : Finset (Scalar params) :=
   233	    Finset.univ.filter (fun x : Scalar params =>
   234	      _root_.Polynomial.eval x f.poly = _root_.Polynomial.eval x h.poly)
   235	  have hS_card_le : S.card ≤ params.d := by
   236	    have hsub_ne : f.poly - h.poly ≠ 0 := sub_ne_zero.mpr hneq
   237	    have hsubset : S.val ⊆ (f.poly - h.poly).roots := by
   238	      intro x hx
   239	      have hx_eval : _root_.Polynomial.eval x f.poly = _root_.Polynomial.eval x h.poly := by
   240	        simpa [S] using hx
   241	      have hxroot : _root_.Polynomial.IsRoot (f.poly - h.poly) x := by
   242	        rw [_root_.Polynomial.IsRoot.def, _root_.Polynomial.eval_sub, sub_eq_zero]
   243	        exact hx_eval
   244	      exact (_root_.Polynomial.mem_roots hsub_ne).2 hxroot
   245	    have hcard := _root_.Polynomial.card_le_degree_of_subset_roots (p := f.poly - h.poly)
   246	      (Z := S) hsubset
   247	    have hdeg : (f.poly - h.poly).natDegree ≤ max f.poly.natDegree h.poly.natDegree := by
   248	      simpa [sub_eq_add_neg, _root_.Polynomial.natDegree_neg] using
   249	        (_root_.Polynomial.natDegree_add_le f.poly (-h.poly))
   250	    exact le_trans hcard (le_trans hdeg (max_le f.degreeBounded h.degreeBounded))
   251	  have havg_scalar :
   252	      avgOver (uniformDistribution (Scalar params))
   253	        (fun x =>
   254	          if _root_.Polynomial.eval x f.poly = _root_.Polynomial.eval x h.poly then
   255	            (1 : Error)
   256	          else 0) =
   257	        (S.card : Error) / Fintype.card (Scalar params) := by
   258	    calc
   259	      avgOver (uniformDistribution (Scalar params))
   260	        (fun x =>
   261	          if _root_.Polynomial.eval x f.poly = _root_.Polynomial.eval x h.poly then
   262	            (1 : Error)
   263	          else 0)
   264	        = ∑ x : Scalar params,
   265	            if _root_.Polynomial.eval x f.poly = _root_.Polynomial.eval x h.poly then
   266	              (1 / (Fintype.card (Scalar params) : Error))
   267	            else 0 := by
   268	              simp [avgOver, uniformDistribution]
   269	      _ = ∑ x ∈ S, (1 / (Fintype.card (Scalar params) : Error)) := by
   270	              rw [← Finset.sum_filter]
   271	      _ = (S.card : Error) * (1 / (Fintype.card (Scalar params) : Error)) := by
   272	              simp
   273	      _ = (S.card : Error) / Fintype.card (Scalar params) := by ring
   274	  have hline :
   275	      (S.card : Error) / Fintype.card (Scalar params) ≤
   276	        (params.d : Error) / params.q := by
   277	    rw [scalar_card]
   278	    exact div_le_div_of_nonneg_right (by exact_mod_cast hS_card_le) (by positivity)
   279	  have hmd : (params.d : Error) / params.q ≤ (params.m * params.d : Error) / params.q := by
   280	    apply div_le_div_of_nonneg_right ?_ (by positivity)
   281	    have hm : (1 : Error) ≤ (params.m : Error) := by exact_mod_cast params.hm
   282	    have hd : 0 ≤ (params.d : Error) := by positivity
   283	    calc
   284	      (params.d : Error) = (1 : Error) * (params.d : Error) := by ring
   285	      _ ≤ (params.m : Error) * (params.d : Error) :=
   286	          mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hm hd
   287	      _ = (params.m * params.d : Error) := by norm_num
   288	  calc
   289	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fq params))
   290	      (fun t => if f t = h t then (1 : Error) else 0)
   291	      = avgOver (uniformDistribution (Scalar params))
   292	        (fun x =>
   293	          if _root_.Polynomial.eval x f.poly = _root_.Polynomial.eval x h.poly then
   294	            (1 : Error)
   295	          else 0) := axisLinePolynomialAgreement_avg_eq_scalarDomain params f h
   296	    _ = (S.card : Error) / Fintype.card (Scalar params) := havg_scalar
   297	    _ ≤ (params.d : Error) / params.q := hline
   298	    _ ≤ (params.m * params.d : Error) / params.q := hmd

   300	open Classical in
   301	/-- Tensor-form Schwartz-Zippel collision bound.
   302	
   303	For each off-diagonal pair of polynomial outcomes, the point-collision
   304	coefficient is bounded by `params.m * params.d / params.q` via
   305	`polynomialAgreement_avg_le_mdq`. The remaining tensor residual is bounded by
   306	`1` using `sandwichTensor_residual_sum_le_one`, so the whole nonnegative
   307	collision sum has the same `m d / q` bound. -/
   308	lemma polynomialCollision_sandwichTensor_le_mdq
   309	    {ιA ιB β : Type*}
   310	    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB] [Fintype β]
   311	    (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q]
   312	    (ψ : QuantumState (ιA × ιB)) (hnorm : ψ.IsNormalized)
   313	    (Outer : SubMeas β ιA)
   314	    (Inner : SubMeas (Polynomial params) ιA) (Right : SubMeas (Polynomial params) ιB) :
   315	    (∑ gg : Polynomial params × Polynomial params, ∑ o : β,
   316	        (if gg.1 = gg.2 then 0 else
   317	          avgOver (uniformDistribution (Point params))
   318	            (fun u => if gg.1 u = gg.2 u then (1 : Error) else 0)) *
   319	          ev ψ
   320	            (leftTensor (ι₂ := ιB)
   321	                (Outer.outcome o * Inner.outcome gg.1 * Outer.outcome o) *
   322	              rightTensor (ι₁ := ιA) (Right.outcome gg.2))) ≤
   323	      (params.m * params.d : Error) / params.q := by
   324	  let δ : Error := (params.m * params.d : Error) / params.q
   325	  have hδ_nonneg : 0 ≤ δ := by
   326	    exact div_nonneg (by positivity) (by positivity)
   327	  have hcoef_le (gg : Polynomial params × Polynomial params) :
   328	      (if gg.1 = gg.2 then 0 else
   329	          avgOver (uniformDistribution (Point params))
   330	            (fun u => if gg.1 u = gg.2 u then (1 : Error) else 0)) ≤ δ := by
   331	    by_cases hEq : gg.1 = gg.2
   332	    · simp [hEq, hδ_nonneg, δ]
   333	    · simpa [hEq, δ] using
   334	        polynomialAgreement_avg_le_mdq params gg.1 gg.2 hEq
   335	  calc
   336	    (∑ gg : Polynomial params × Polynomial params, ∑ o : β,
   337	        (if gg.1 = gg.2 then 0 else
   338	          avgOver (uniformDistribution (Point params))
   339	            (fun u => if gg.1 u = gg.2 u then (1 : Error) else 0)) *
   340	          ev ψ

     5	/-!
     6	# Strategy transport for the directly indexed low-degree game
     7	
     8	This module reads one coordinate of a projective directly indexed strategy as
     9	a two-space mature low individual degree strategy.  The question and answer
    10	transport of `Transport.Questions` supplies the canonical direct question of

   114	/-- The coordinate axis-line family is independent of the chosen affine
   115	parametrization of a mature line. -/
   116	theorem directCoordinateAxisMeasurement_reparam
   117	    (D : DirectLdParams) (r : Fin D.k)
   118	    {iota : Type*} [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   119	    (M : DirectLdQuestion D →
   120	      MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement (DirectLdAnswer D) iota)
   121	    (hM : ∀ q, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (M q)) :
   122	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   123	    AxisParallelMeasurementReparamInvariant D.toLDTParameters
   124	      (directCoordinateAxisMeasurement D r M hM) := by
   125	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   126	  classical
   127	  intro line t f
   128	  simp only [directCoordinateAxisMeasurement, ProjMeas.postprocess,
   129	    SubMeas.postprocess_outcome, matrixMeasurementToLDTProjMeas_outcome]
   130	  rw [directAxisQuestionOf_rebase]

   133	        directAxisAnswerReadout D r (line.rebaseAt t) answer =
   134	          AxisLinePolynomial.reparamAt f t) =
   135	        Finset.univ.filter (fun answer =>
   136	          directAxisAnswerReadout D r line answer = f) := by

   138	    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
   139	    rw [directAxisAnswerReadout_rebase]
   140	    exact (AxisLinePolynomial.reparamAtEquiv t).injective.eq_iff

   146	    (D : DirectLdParams) (r : Fin D.k)

   172	private theorem strategy_carrier_nonempty {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) :
   173	    Nonempty (S.ιA × S.ιB) := by
   174	  by_contra h
   175	  rw [not_nonempty_iff] at h
   176	  letI := h

/-!
# Generalized Pauli operators and EPR states

The definitions here use finite matrix entries and rank-one projectors, so they
are usable by the later game statements without introducing an abstract
operator algebra.  The observable/projector expansions are obtained from
finite-field Fourier orthogonality in characteristic two.

## References

The source-facing nodes are `def:lin-reg`, `def:EPR`, `def:generalized-pauli`,
and `lem:pauli-observable-expansion` in
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:494-652`.  The paper origin is
`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:908-1161`.

import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.DirectLowDegree.Transport.Correspondence

/-!
# Question and answer transport for the directly indexed low-degree game

This module reads mature low individual degree questions as canonical direct
questions and rebases direct answers to the mature line parametrization.

Points and lines are decoded with the coordinate order reversed
(`directPointEquiv`), so that the suffix-zero direction restriction of the
mature diagonal test becomes the prefix-zero restriction of the direct game.
A mature diagonal line reveals no coordinate index, whereas a direct diagonal
question carries one.  The transported question uses the *leading index* of
the decoded direction, the least coordinate at which the direction is
nonzero.  Under the direct sampler, this is the index attached to the sampled
direction exactly when the direction is nonzero at the sampled index
(`directDiagonalIndexOf_prefixProjection`), an event of conditional
probability `1 - 1/q`; on the mature side, the leading index of a decoded
`j`-restricted direction is `Fin.rev j` exactly when its pivot coordinate is
nonzero (`directDiagonalIndexOf_extendRestrictedDirection`).  Diagonal answers
on zero-direction lines are read as the constant polynomial carrying their
value at the base point, following `rem:ld-win-zero-direction`.

  1409	\subsection{Quantum soundness of the classical simultaneous low-degree test}\label{sec:q-simultaneous}
  1410	
  1411	We would now like to use \Cref{thm:anand-thomas-classical-low-degree}
  1412	to show quantum soundness for the simultaneous classical low-degree test.
  1413	This will be done using the same reduction presented in~\Cref{sec:simultaneous-classical}.
  1414	The main result is the following.
  1415	
  1416	\begin{theorem}[Quantum soundness of the simultaneous classical
  1417	  low-degree test]
  1418	  \label{thm:simultaneous-ldt}
  1419	There exists a constant $c > 0$ and a function $\delta(\eps) = \mathrm{poly}(\epsilon, d (m + \ell)/q^c)$ such that the following holds.
  1420	Suppose Alice and Bob are entangled provers who pass $\game_{\mathrm{Surface}}^\ell(m,d,q,2)$ with probability at least $1-\eps$
  1421	using the strategy $(\psi, M)$, where~$M$ consists of projective measurements.
  1422	Then there exists a measurement $G \in \simulpolymeas{m}{d}{q}{\ell}$ such that
  1423	\begin{equation*}
  1424	M^w_{b_1, \ldots, b_\ell} \otimes I_{\reg{Bob}} \consistency_{\delta(\eps)} I_{\reg{Alice}} \otimes G_{[g_1(w), \ldots, g_\ell(w) = b_1, \ldots, b_\ell]},
  1425	\qquad
  1426	G_{g_1, \ldots, g_\ell} \otimes I_{\reg{Bob}}
  1427	\consistency_{\delta(\eps)}
  1428	I_{\reg{Alice}} \otimes G_{g_1, \ldots, g_\ell},
  1429	\end{equation*}
  1430	where the first is on the uniform distribution over $\F_q^m$.
  1431	\end{theorem}
  1432	
  1433	\begin{proof}
  1434	Suppose Alice and Bob pass $\game_{\mathrm{Surface}}^\ell(m, d, q,2)$ with probability at least $1-\eps$.
  1435	We will use them to simulate two provers, ``Combined Alice" and ``Combined Bob", who pass
  1436	the single-function low-degree test $\game_{\mathrm{Surface}}(\ell + m, d+1, q,2)$ with probability at least $1-\eps$.
  1437	They are specified as follows:
  1438	\begin{itemize}
  1439	\item[$\circ$] \textbf{Combined Alice:} Given $\bs \subseteq \F_q^{\ell + m}$, draw $\bs' \sim_2 \bs_{\mathrm{proj}}$.  Give it to Alice, who responds with $\boldf_1, \ldots, \boldf_{\ell}: \bs' \rightarrow \F_q$.  Output the function $\mathrm{combine}_{\boldf}|_{\bs}$.
  1440	\item[$\circ$] \textbf{Combined Bob:} Given $(\bx, \by) \in \F_q^{\ell + m}$, compute $\by \in \F_q^m$. Give it to Bob, who responds with $\bb_1, \ldots, \bb_\ell \in \F_q$.
  1441				Return $\mathrm{combine}_{\bb}(\bx) \in \F_q$.
  1442	\end{itemize}
  1443	By \Cref{prop:really-the-same-dist}, $\bs'$ and $\by$ are distributed as the questions in $\game_{\mathrm{Surface}}^\ell(m, d, q,2)$.
  1444	Using our assumption on Alice and Bob, this means that $\boldf_1(\by) = \bb_1$, \ldots, $\boldf_\ell(\by) = \bb_\ell$ with probability at least $1-\eps$.
  1445	As a result, $(\mathrm{combine}_{\boldf}|_{\bs})(\bx, \by) = \mathrm{combine}_{\bb}(\by)$ with probability at least~$1-\eps$.
  1446	By \Cref{prop:sub-subspace}, $\mathrm{combine}_{\boldf}|_{\bs}$ is a degree-$(d+1)$ function on~$\bs$,
  1447	and so it is a valid response to subspace queries.
  1448	This means Combined Alice and Bob pass~$\game_{\mathrm{Surface}}(\ell + m, d+1, q, 2)$ with probability at least~$1-\eps$.
  1449	
  1450	Thus, we can apply \Cref{thm:anand-thomas-classical-low-degree}.
  1451	It gives a measurement $G \in \polymeas{\ell+m}{d+1}{q}$ such that
  1452	\begin{equation}\label{eq:g-meas-equals-combine-meas}
  1453	M^y_{[\mathrm{combine}_b(x)=\nu]} \otimes I_{\reg{Bob}}
  1454	\consistency_{\delta(\eps)} I_{\reg{Alice}} \otimes G_{[g(x, y) = \nu]},
  1455	\qquad
  1456	G_g \otimes I_{\reg{Bob}} \consistency_{\delta(\eps)} I_{\reg{Alice}} \otimes G_g,
  1457	\end{equation}
  1458	where $\delta(\eps) = \poly(\eps, (d+1)(\ell+m)/q^c)$.
  1459	This means that if we give Alice~$\by$ and she returns~$\bb$, and Bob simply returns~$\bg$,
  1460	then $\mathrm{combine}_{\bb}(\bx) = g(\bx, \by)$ with probability at least~$1-\delta(\eps)$.
  1461	
  1462	We would like to show that~$\bg$ is exactly linear in~$x$ with high probability, over the randomness in the measurement~$G$.
  1463	Let us condition on a $\bg$ which is not exactly linear.
  1464	By \Cref{prop:exactly-linear-prop}, the probability that $\bg|_{\by}$ is not exactly linear is at least $1-(d+1)/q$.
  1465	On the other hand, because $\mathrm{combine}_{\bb}(\bx)$ is always exactly linear by construction,
  1466	the probability that $\bg|_{\by}(\bx) = \mathrm{combine}_{\bb}(\bx)$ is at most $(d+1)/q$ by Schwartz-Zippel (\Cref{lem:schwartz-zippel}).
  1467	As a result, the probability that $\bg(\bx, \by) = \mathrm{combine}_{\bb}(\bx)$ is at most $(d+1)/q + (d+1)/q$.
  1468	Thus, if we write $\mu_{\mathrm{linear}}$ for the probability that $\bg$ is exactly linear, we have equality at most $\mu_{\mathrm{linear}} + 2(d+1)/q$ fraction of the time.
  1469	Rearranging, $\bg$ is exactly linear with probability
  1470	\begin{equation*}
  1471	\mu_{\mathrm{linear}} \geq 1 - 2\delta(\eps) - 2(d+1)/q.
  1472	\end{equation*}
  1473	Define a new measurement $\{H_{g_1, \ldots, g_\ell}\} \in \simulpolymeas{m}{d}{q}{\ell}$ operationally as follows: first, measure~$G$ and receive~$\bg$.
  1474	If it is exactly linear, it can be written as $\sum_i x_i \cdot \bg_i(y)$, and so output $\bg_1, \ldots, \bg_\ell$.
  1475	If~$\bg$ is \emph{not} exactly linear, output any arbitrary degree-$d$ polynomials instead.
  1476	When~$\bg$ is exactly linear, we have $\mathrm{combine}_{\bg_1, \ldots, \bg_\ell}(x, y) = \bg(x, y)$.
  1477	Since this happens with probability at least $1-\delta(\eps)$,
  1478	we can replace~$G$ with~$H$ in \Cref{eq:g-meas-equals-combine-meas}, yielding
  1479	\begin{equation}\label{eq:no-name-is-a-bad-name}
  1480	M^y_{[\mathrm{combine}_b(x)=\nu]} \otimes I_{\reg{Bob}}
  1481	\consistency_{\delta(\eps)} I_{\reg{Alice}} \otimes H_{[\mathrm{combine}_g(x, y) = \nu]},
  1482	\end{equation}
  1483	On the other hand, because~$H$ is just~$G$ with data processing applied to its output,
  1484	we can apply \Cref{fact:specialize-the-simeq} to \Cref{eq:g-meas-equals-combine-meas}. This produces the equation
  1485	\begin{equation*}
  1486	H_{g_1, \ldots, g_\ell} \otimes I_{\reg{Bob}} \consistency_{\delta(\eps)} I_{\reg{Alice}} \otimes H_{g_1, \ldots, g_\ell}.
  1487	\end{equation*}
  1488	
  1489	Consider $\bg_1, \ldots, \bg_\ell$ drawn by Bob using~$H$.
  1490	For any fixed~$b$ and~$y$, if it is not the case that $g_1(y) = b_1$, \ldots, $g_\ell(y) = b_\ell$,
  1491	then the probability that $\mathrm{combine}_{\bg}(\bx, y) = \mathrm{combine}_{b}(\bx)$
  1492	over a random~$\bx$ is at most $1/q$ by Schwartz-Zippel, since both are exactly linear functions.
  1493	Thus, if Alice draws~$\bb_1, \ldots, \bb_\ell$ given~$\by$,
  1494	and we write~$\eta$ for the probability that $\bg_1(\by) = \bb_1$, \ldots, $\bg_\ell(\by) = \bb_\ell$,
  1495	then the probability that $\mathrm{combine}_{\bg}(\bx, \by) = \mathrm{combine}_{\bb}(\bx)$ is at most
  1496	$\eta +  (1-\eta) \cdot 1/q$.
  1497	Combined with \Cref{eq:no-name-is-a-bad-name}, this implies that
  1498	\begin{equation*}
  1499	\Pr[\bg_1(\by) = \bb_1, \ldots, \bg_\ell(\by) = \bb_\ell] \geq 1- \delta(\eps) - 1/q.
  1500	\end{equation*}
  1501	Or, equivalently,
  1502	\begin{equation*}
  1503	M^y_{b_1, \ldots, b_\ell} \otimes I_{\reg{Bob}}
  1504	\consistency_{\delta(\eps)} I_{\reg{Alice}} \otimes G_{[g_1(y), \ldots, g_\ell(y) = b_1, \ldots, b_\ell]}.\qedhere
  1505	\end{equation*}
  1506	\end{proof}

  1508	\subsection{Self-testing}
  1509	
  1510	The games presented in \Cref{sec:classical-q-low-deg,sec:q-simultaneous} might be referred to as ``measurement testers":
  1511	if a strategy passes them with high probability, then we can extract some property on its measurements.
  1512	In this section, we will introduce a significantly stronger notion of testing called \emph{self-testing}.
  1513	A self-tester is a game in which if a prover passes with high probability,
  1514	then not only do we do exactly which measurements the prover must be performing,
  1515	we also know which exactly state it must be performing them on (up to local isometry).
  1516	(We note that some works use ``self-testing" to refer both to ``measurement testing" and what we refer to as ``self-testing"~\cite{NV18a}.
  1517	In this work, we will reserve the term exclusively for the latter.) We begin with a definition.
  1518	
  1519	\begin{definition}
  1520	We say that $\mathcal{S} = (\psi, M)$ is a \emph{partial strategy} for $\game$
  1521	if $M$ contains the POVM $M^x$ for only a subset of the questions in~$\game$.
  1522	We call this set of questions $\mathcal{S}$'s \emph{question set}.
  1523	A strategy $\mathcal{S}' = (\psi, M')$ \emph{extends} $\mathcal{S}$ if $(M')^x = M^x$ for every~$x$ in $\mathcal{S}$'s question set.
  1524	\end{definition}
